SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: HorizonVoyage Demo Travel Medical Plan (Sample Only)

§1.1 Definition of Insured Traveler
The Insured Traveler means the demo participant enrolled under this synthetic plan who is age 18 or older at the date of departure. Enrollment is created automatically for demonstration purposes and carries no real coverage. All names, amounts, and events in this document are fabricated for software testing.

§1.2 Definition of Covered Trip
A Covered Trip means a fictional journey outside the traveler's home country lasting between 7 and 180 consecutive days. Trips shorter than 7 days are treated as excursions and are not eligible under §2.1. The trip must begin and end on dates recorded in the demo enrollment record.

§1.3 Definition of Emergency Medical Condition
An Emergency Medical Condition means a fabricated sudden illness or injury that a reasonable demo physician would judge requires immediate care. Routine checkups, elective procedures, and pre-scheduled treatments are explicitly not emergencies under this plan.

§2.1 Eligibility Requirements
Applicants must be between 18 and 79 years old and hold a valid passport from a listed demo country. Enrollment must be completed at least 72 hours before departure, except that travelers already abroad may enroll with a 48-hour waiting period before any benefit applies. Travelers over 79 may enroll only with a fictional medical review approval.

§2.2 Eligibility Exceptions
Dependent children under 18 may be added to a parent's enrollment at no additional demo premium, limited to four dependents per enrollment. Dependents over 18 must enroll separately under §2.1. Students on fictional study programs may extend coverage once, for up to 90 additional days.

§3.1 Emergency Medical Benefits
The plan pays 100 percent of covered emergency medical expenses up to a demo limit of 250,000 currency units per trip. This includes hospital rooms up to 300 units per day, intensive care up to 800 units per day, and emergency surgery as described in §3.2. Outpatient visits are covered up to 150 units per visit, with a maximum of 20 visits per trip.

§3.2 Surgical and Hospital Benefits
Emergency surgery performed within 24 hours of a qualifying incident in §1.3 is covered up to 40,000 units per occurrence. Non-emergency surgery requires prior approval as described in §4.2 and is otherwise excluded. Hospital stays beyond 30 days per trip require the traveler to notify the demo administrator, after which coverage continues at 50 percent of eligible charges.

§3.3 Evacuation and Repatriation
Emergency evacuation to the nearest adequate demo facility is covered up to 100,000 units, and repatriation of remains up to 25,000 units. Evacuation must be arranged by the fictional assistance coordinator to be payable. Transportation home after medical discharge is covered up to 2,500 units once per trip.

§3.4 Trip Interruption Benefit
If the traveler is hospitalized for at least 5 consecutive days, the plan pays 200 units per day for a maximum of 10 days of interrupted travel. A return ticket change fee up to 400 units is also covered once per trip. This benefit does not apply to interruptions caused by events listed in §5.2.

§4.1 Deductibles and Coinsurance
A deductible of 250 units per trip applies to all medical benefits under §3.1 and §3.2. After the deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of eligible charges outside the home region and 100 percent within it. The traveler's maximum annual out-of-pocket share is capped at 5,000 units.

§4.2 Prior Approval Rules
Hospital admissions, surgery, MRI or CT imaging, and any treatment expected to exceed 2,000 units require prior approval from the demo administrator within 48 hours of the event. Emergency admissions qualify if notice is given within 72 hours of admission. Failure to obtain approval reduces payable benefits by 25 percent, except where the traveler was physically unable to give notice, in which case full benefits apply.

§4.3 Benefit Period and Claim Deadlines
Coverage for a condition begins on the date of the qualifying event and continues for 60 days, even if the trip ends sooner. Written notice of any claim must reach the administrator within 30 days of the event. Completed claim documentation must be submitted within 90 days, or benefits are forfeited unless the delay was beyond the traveler's control.

§5.1 General Exclusions
The plan excludes self-inflicted injury, participation in professional sports, war zones named on the demo exclusion list, and treatment of conditions diagnosed before enrollment. Cosmetic procedures and dental work other than emergency pain relief up to 300 units are excluded. Experimental treatments and any care provided in the traveler's home country are excluded without exception.

§5.2 Exclusion Exceptions
Pre-existing conditions are covered up to 10,000 units if the traveler purchased a demo waiver rider and the condition was stable for 180 days before departure. Extreme sports are covered up to 15,000 units if the traveler purchased the adventure rider described in §2.2 enrollment options. All other exclusions in §5.1 apply regardless of rider purchase.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are filed through the fictional claims portal using a fabricated reference generated at enrollment. The administrator must issue an initial decision within 15 business days of complete documentation. Payments are issued in the demo currency within 10 business days of approval.

§6.2 Appeals Process
A traveler may appeal a denied claim within 60 days of the decision by submitting new documentation to the fictional appeals unit. A second-level review by a different demo reviewer must be completed within 30 business days. If the appeal is upheld, benefits are paid retroactively to the original event date as described in §6.1.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: Meridian Flex PPO 500 Demonstration Plan

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this demonstration plan, a "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January 1. "Covered Expense" means a medically necessary charge that is reasonable and customary, as determined by the plan administrator. "Network Provider" means any provider contracted with the demonstration network, which exists only for software testing purposes.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are eligible for coverage. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous employment. Eligible dependents include a legal spouse, domestic partner, and children under age 26, or under age 30 if enrolled full-time in an accredited school.

§1.3 Enrollment and Notice
New employees must complete an enrollment form within 31 days of first becoming eligible. Late enrollees may join only during the annual open enrollment period in November. Changes in dependent status must be reported within 60 days of the qualifying event.

§2.1 Hospital Benefits
The plan pays 80 percent of covered room and board charges after the deductible, up to a semi-private room rate of $1,200 per day. Inpatient stays are covered for up to 120 days per Plan Year. Intensive care is covered at 80 percent up to $2,500 per day.

§2.2 Physician Services
Office visits to network physicians are covered at 100 percent after a $25 copayment. Non-network office visits are covered at 60 percent after the deductible. Surgical procedures are covered at 80 percent of reasonable and customary charges.

§2.3 Mental Health and Substance Abuse
Outpatient mental health visits are covered up to 40 sessions per Plan Year at 80 percent after a $20 copayment. Inpatient substance abuse treatment is limited to 30 days per Plan Year. These benefits follow the same appeal rules described in §6.2.

§2.4 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $35 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $60 copayment. A 90-day maintenance supply is available through the designated mail-order channel for twice the retail copayment. Coverage is limited to a 34-day supply per retail fill.

§3.1 Preventive Care
Routine physical examinations, immunizations, and age-appropriate cancer screenings are covered at 100 percent with no deductible. Well-child visits are covered through age 18 up to six visits per year. Preventive benefits are not subject to the out-of-pocket maximum described in §4.2.

§3.2 Emergency Care
Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent after a $150 copayment, which is waived if the member is admitted within 24 hours. Members must notify the plan administrator within 48 hours of any emergency admission, or within 72 hours if incapacitated. Urgent care clinic visits carry a $50 copayment.

§4.1 Deductible
The annual deductible is $500 per individual and $1,000 per family, applied to most covered expenses. Preventive care as described in §3.1 is exempt from the deductible. Deductible amounts carry over for the first three months of a new Plan Year for members who were covered during the prior year.

§4.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
Annual out-of-pocket costs are limited to $4,000 per individual and $8,000 per family. Once the maximum is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of covered expenses for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copayments for prescription drugs under §2.4 do not count toward this maximum.

§4.3 Lifetime Maximum
The lifetime maximum benefit for all covered expenses is $2,000,000 per covered person. Once the lifetime maximum is exhausted, no further benefits are payable under this plan. This limit does not apply to benefits payable under §2.3.

§5.1 Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, dental care for persons over age 19, vision hardware beyond one pair of lenses per Plan Year, or experimental treatments. Injury or illness arising from participation in a professional athletic contest is also excluded. These exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following a covered mastectomy or accidental injury.

§5.2 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions other than emergencies require prior approval at least seven days before admission. Outpatient MRI, CT, and PET scans require prior approval at least five business days in advance. Failure to obtain approval reduces payment for the service by 50 percent.

§5.3 Continuation of Coverage
Coverage may be continued for up to 18 months following termination of employment, at a monthly premium of 102 percent of the full cost. Continuation is available for up to 36 months in cases of death or divorce of the covered employee. Notice of the right to continue must be sent within 44 days of the qualifying event.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible if that deadline is impracticable. The plan administrator will adjudicate complete claims within 30 days. Members will receive an explanation of benefits showing amounts paid and applied to the deductible under §4.1.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. The administrator must issue a written decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first denial, and the decision on that appeal is final for this demonstration plan.

§6.3 Plan Administration
The plan is administered by a demonstration-only administrative committee that exists solely for this software model. Premium contributions are 20 percent of premium for single coverage and 25 percent for family coverage. This document is entirely synthetic and confers no real benefits or obligations.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Orchid High-DeductibleHealth Plan Demo Edition

§1.1 Definitions
In this document, "Plan" refers to the Meridian Orchid High-DeductibleHealth Plan Demo Edition. "Covered Person" means an enrollee or enrolled dependent as described in §2.1. "Calendar Year" means the twelve-month period from January 1 through December 31. "Allowed Amount" means the maximum fee the Plan recognizes for a service, which is set administratively at 140 percent of the standard regional fee index.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees of participating demo employers who work at least 25 hours per week are eligible to enroll. Coverage begins after a 60-day waiting period from the date of hire or the first day of the month following enrollment, whichever is later. Eligibility for enrollment each year is determined on December 1 of the prior year.

§1.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which the covered person ceases to be eligible. Covered persons may continue coverage for up to 90 days after termination by paying the full monthly cost plus a 15 percent surcharge. Termination does not affect claims processing rights under §6.1.

§2.1 Enrollment and Dependents
Enrollment must be completed within 30 days of the eligibility date described in §1.2. Eligible dependents include a spouse, domestic partner, and children up to age 26 or up to any age if disabled before age 26. New dependents must be reported to the administrator within 31 days of the qualifying event.

§2.2 Effective Dates and Open Enrollment
The annual open enrollment period runs from November 1 through December 15 each year. Changes made during open enrollment take effect on January 1. Mid-year changes are allowed only for qualifying events reported under §2.1.

§3.1 Deductible
The Plan pays nothing for most services until the Covered Person has paid an annual deductible of $3,400 for individual coverage or $6,800 for family coverage. Payments toward the deductible count only for services applied to the deductible as described in §3.2. Once the deductible is met, the cost-sharing rules in §3.3 apply.

§3.2 Medical Benefits
After the deductible is satisfied, the Plan pays 80 percent of the Allowed Amount for inpatient hospital care, outpatient surgery, and physician visits. Preventive care, including one annual physical and immunizations, is covered at 100 percent without satisfying the deductible. Physical therapy is limited to 40 visits per Calendar Year, with visits beyond that requiring approval under §4.1.

§3.3 Cost Sharing
Coinsurance of 20 percent applies after the deductible under §3.1 until the Covered Person reaches an out-of-pocket maximum of $7,200 for individual coverage or $14,400 for family coverage. After the out-of-pocket maximum is reached, the Plan pays 100 percent of the Allowed Amount for the remainder of the Calendar Year. Emergency room visits carry a separate $350 copayment that is waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Prescription drugs are covered at 100 percent after the deductible for generic drugs and at 75 percent for brand-name drugs. A 90-day supply of maintenance medications is available at two times the 30-day cost share. Certain specialty drugs require prior approval under §4.1.

§3.5 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, limited to 50 visits per Calendar Year. Inpatient mental health care is covered for up to 60 days per Calendar Year. Substance use treatment is subject to the same limits and prior approval requirements in §4.1.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Certain services, including inpatient admissions, advanced imaging, and the specialty drugs in §3.4, require prior approval from the administrator. Requests must be submitted at least 10 business days before scheduled services or within 48 hours after emergency admissions. Approvals are valid for 60 days from the date of issuance.

§4.2 Open Notification Deadlines
Covered Persons must notify the administrator of any admission to a non-network facility within 3 business days. Notice of a change in dependent status under §2.1 must be given within 31 days. Failure to provide timely notice reduces the Allowed Amount by 25 percent, unless the failure was due to circumstances beyond the person's control.

§4.3 Coordination of Benefits
If a Covered Person has coverage under another plan, this Plan will pay only the difference between its Allowed Amount and the amount paid by the primary plan. The other coverage will be presumed primary unless the Covered Person shows otherwise within 60 days. Overpayments must be refunded to the Plan within 90 days.

§5.1 Exclusions
The Plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, dental care for persons over age 19 except as required by accident, vision correction, weight-loss surgery unless medically necessary, and services received outside the country except for emergencies. Experimental or investigational treatments are excluded unless the treatment has been approved by a national oversight body. Exclusions do not apply to services required by the mandates described in §5.2.

§5.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following an accident or cancer treatment is not considered cosmetic and is covered. Dental care required to treat injuries to sound natural teeth from an accident is covered at 80 percent after the deductible. Emergency care received outside the country is reimbursed at in-network rates as described in §3.2.

§5.3 Annual Limits
The Plan limits combined inpatient days to 120 per Calendar Year except for maternity care. Out-of-network benefits are capped at $150,000 per Calendar Year. No annual limit applies to amounts paid after the out-of-pocket maximum is reached under §3.3.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service. Complete claims are paid or denied within 30 days, or within 60 days if more information is required. Notices of denial must state the reason, the clause relied on, and the appeal rights under §6.2.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care appeals. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of a first-level denial and must be reviewed by a reviewer not involved in the original decision.

§6.3 External Review
If a second-level appeal under §6.2 upholds a denial, the Covered Person may request external review within 60 days. The external reviewer's decision is binding on the Plan. The Plan pays the cost of the external review.

§7.1 Administration
The Plan is administered by the demo employer's benefits office on behalf of the illustrative Plan sponsor. Contribution rates are $185 per month for individual coverage and $440 per month for family coverage, payable through payroll deduction. The administrator may update the fee index in §1.1 annually.

§7.2 Records and Privacy
The administrator maintains claims records for seven years after the Calendar Year of service. Records are used only to administer the Plan and to process appeals under §6.2. Covered Persons may request copies of their records once per Calendar Year at no cost.

§7.3 Amendments and Notices
The demo employer may amend this document by giving Covered Persons 30 days written notice, except that reductions in benefits require 60 days notice. Any amendment that changes the deductible in §3.1 takes effect only at the start of a Calendar Year. Notices are delivered electronically unless paper copy is requested.

SYNTHETIC
Short-Term Care Plan "Aurora Bridge Coverage 90" (Demo Document, Not a Real Policy)

§1.1 Definitions
In this document, "Covered Person" means an individual enrolled under this Plan whose coverage has become effective. "Eligible Expense" means a charge for a Covered Service that does not exceed the Reasonable Charge shown in §4.2. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the first day of the month after enrollment.

§1.2 Plan Purpose
This Plan provides temporary medical benefits for a maximum of ninety consecutive days per coverage period. It is designed as bridge coverage only and is not a substitute for comprehensive insurance. All provisions in this document are fictional and exist solely for software demonstration purposes.

§1.3 Definitions Continued
"Covered Service" means a service listed in §3.1 through §3.5 and performed by a Licensed Provider. "Deductible" means the amount a Covered Person pays before benefits begin, as set out in §5.1. "Network Facility" means any clinic or hospital identified in the demonstration provider directory.

§2.1 Eligibility
An applicant must be between eighteen and sixty-four years of age and reside in a state where the Plan is offered for demonstration. Applicants must complete the synthetic enrollment form and answer the five health questions in the demo questionnaire. Coverage may not be issued to any person currently hospitalized.

§2.2 Effective Date and Waiting Period
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the later of the day after the enrollment form is approved or the date selected by the applicant. There is a five-day waiting period for illness benefits, during which no Illness Covered Services are payable. Accidental Injury benefits, as described in §3.2, are payable from the first day of coverage with no waiting period.

§2.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends automatically at 11:59 p.m. on the ninetieth day, when the premium is not paid within the ten-day grace period, or when the Covered Person attains the day limit described in §4.4. No benefits are payable for services rendered after termination except as provided in §6.3. A single extension of up to thirty days may be purchased once per Plan Year at the premium rate in §5.4.

§3.1 Physician Office Visits
The Plan pays eighty percent of Eligible Expenses for medically necessary office visits to a Licensed Provider after the Deductible is satisfied. Visits are limited to four per Covered Person per Plan Year. Preventive screening visits are covered at one hundred percent up to one hundred fifty dollars per Plan Year and do not count against the four-visit limit.

§3.2 Emergency and Accidental Injury Benefits
Emergency room treatment is covered at seventy percent of Eligible Expenses, subject to a two hundred fifty dollar emergency room copayment waived if the Covered Person is admitted as an inpatient. Accidental Injury benefits are payable from day one as stated in §2.2. Follow-up care for the same injury is covered for sixty days from the date of the emergency visit.

§3.3 Inpatient Hospital Benefits
The Plan pays seventy-five percent of Eligible Expenses for inpatient hospital stays up to a maximum of twenty days per Plan Year. The daily Reasonable Charge for inpatient stays is capped at four thousand dollars per day. A separate inpatient Deductible of five hundred dollars applies, as described in §5.1.

§3.4 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs are covered at one hundred percent after a fifteen dollar copayment per prescription. Brand-name drugs are covered at fifty percent with a forty dollar copayment. The annual prescription benefit is capped at one thousand dollars per Covered Person.

§3.5 Diagnostic and Imaging Services
Laboratory tests are covered at eighty percent of Eligible Expenses with no visit limit. Advanced imaging such as magnetic resonance or computed tomography scans is covered only with prior approval as described in §6.1. Imaging is limited to two procedures per Plan Year per Covered Person.

§4.1 Overall Benefit Maximum
The total benefit payable under this Plan is fifty thousand dollars per Covered Person per Plan Year. Once the maximum is reached, no further benefits are payable for the remainder of the Plan Year. Unused benefit amounts do not carry forward between Plan Years.

§4.2 Reasonable Charge Limits
Eligible Expenses may not exceed the Reasonable Charge, defined as one hundred twenty percent of the median charge for the same service in the same demonstration region. Charges above this limit are the sole responsibility of the Covered Person. Providers may bill the Covered Person for the difference only if permitted under §7.2.

§4.3 Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
No benefits are payable for conditions for which the Covered Person received advice, diagnosis, or treatment during the twelve months before the effective date. This limitation does not apply to Accidental Injury benefits described in §3.2. The limitation ends after thirty days of continuous coverage for conditions disclosed on the enrollment questionnaire.

§4.4 Day and Visit Limits
Inpatient days under §3.3 are limited to twenty per Plan Year. Office visits under §3.1 are limited to four per Plan Year. Physical therapy visits are limited to six per Plan Year, and none may be used before the Deductible in §5.1 is met.

§5.1 Cost Sharing Overview
The Deductible is five hundred dollars per Covered Person per Plan Year and applies to all Covered Services except preventive visits under §3.1 and emergency copayments under §3.2. After the Deductible, the Plan pays the percentages stated in §3.1 through §3.5. The Covered Person pays all remaining coinsurance and copayments.

§5.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The Covered Person's total annual out-of-pocket amount, including the Deductible, copayments, and coinsurance, is capped at six thousand dollars per Plan Year. Once this cap is reached, the Plan pays one hundred percent of Eligible Expenses for the remainder of the Plan Year. Amounts above the Reasonable Charge in §4.2 do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§5.3 Premiums
The monthly premium is two hundred ten dollars per Covered Person age forty and under and three hundred dollars for ages forty-one through sixty-four. Premiums are due on the first day of each coverage month. The first premium must be received before the effective date described in §2.2.

§5.4 Extension Premium
The thirty-day extension described in §2.3 costs one hundred fifty dollars for the younger age band and two hundred twenty dollars for the older band. The extension premium must be paid in full at least five days before the ninetieth day of coverage. No extension is available to a Covered Person whose coverage terminated for nonpayment.

§6.1 Prior Approval Requirements
Advanced imaging under §3.5, inpatient admissions under §3.3, and any single treatment expected to exceed two thousand dollars require prior approval. The request must be submitted at least five business days before the scheduled service, except in an emergency where notice within forty-eight hours of admission is sufficient. Approval is valid for thirty days from the date issued.

§6.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service, and claims received later are denied unless it was not reasonably possible to submit them. Written notice of a hospital admission must be given within two business days. Notice of a Covered Person's change of address must be given within thirty days.

§6.3 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within thirty days of receipt of all required documentation. If a claim is denied, the Covered Person receives a written explanation citing the clause relied upon, such as §4.3 or §4.4. Payment is made to the provider for assigned claims and to the Covered Person otherwise.

§6.4 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denial within one hundred eighty days by submitting a written request to the demonstration appeals office. A first-level appeal is decided within forty-five days by a reviewer who did not make the original denial. A second-level appeal must be requested within sixty days of the first-level decision and is decided within sixty days; the result of the second-level appeal is final under this Plan.

§7.1 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for cosmetic procedures, elective self-inflicted injuries, professional athletic injuries, war or military action, or services received outside the demonstration region except emergency care as described in §3.2. Dental care is excluded unless it treats an Accidental Injury covered under §3.2. Vision and hearing aids are excluded in all cases.

§7.2 Exceptions and Provider Billing
The regional exclusion in §7.1 does not apply to emergency services received within fifty miles of the demonstration region boundary. Providers who accept the Plan may not bill a Covered Person above the Reasonable Charge under §4.2. Non-network providers may bill the difference, which does not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum in §5.2.

§7.3 Administration and Misstatement
Enrollment data used to administer this Plan is synthetic and must not contain real personal information. If a demonstration record contains a misstatement of age or region, benefits are adjusted to what the premium paid would have purchased. This Plan is governed by the fictional rules of the demonstration environment, and all disputes are resolved through the appeal process in §6.4.

SYNTHETIC
Sample Plan: Meridian Flex PPO 750 Demo Plan

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an Employee or Dependent who is enrolled under this Plan and whose coverage has not terminated. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January 1 and ending December 31. "Allowed Amount" means the negotiated fee the Plan permits for a Covered Service, which may be less than the provider's billed charge.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible for coverage effective the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous employment. Dependents include a legal spouse and children under age 26. Eligibility must be verified by the Plan Administrator before enrollment is processed.

§1.3 Enrollment and Waiting Period
Initial enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the date eligibility begins. Late enrollees outside the annual open enrollment window must wait until the next January 1 for coverage to begin. Open enrollment runs each year from November 1 through November 30.

§2.1 Physician Services
The Plan pays 80 percent of the Allowed Amount for in-network physician visits after the deductible, and 60 percent out-of-network. Preventive care, including one annual physical and age-appropriate immunizations, is covered at 100 percent in-network with no deductible. Specialist visits require no referral under this PPO plan.

§2.2 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital care is covered at 80 percent in-network after the deductible, subject to a 120-day limit per confinement per Plan Year. Emergency room services are covered at the in-network level regardless of facility status when treated within 72 hours of onset. Semi-private room and board is covered up to the Allowed Amount.

§2.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 copay, preferred brand a $40 copay, and non-preferred brand a $75 copay per 30-day supply. A 90-day maintenance supply is available at twice the 30-day copay through the mail order program. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §3.1.

§3.1 Prior Approval
Certain services, including inpatient admissions, imaging over $1,500, and specialty drugs, require prior approval from the Utilization Review vendor. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment by 50 percent, except in cases of emergency admission, where notice must be given within 48 hours. Prior approval decisions are issued within 5 business days of a complete request.

§3.2 Cost Sharing Limits
The annual deductible is $1,500 per Covered Person and $3,000 per family. The out-of-pocket maximum is $5,000 per person and $10,000 per family, after which the Plan pays 100 percent of Allowed Amounts for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copays do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§3.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays as secondary in accordance with standard ordering rules. Benefits paid will not exceed the amount this Plan would have paid as primary payer. The Plan Administrator may request other coverage information annually.

§4.1 Exclusions
Services not medically necessary, cosmetic surgery, and weight loss programs are excluded. Experimental or investigational treatments are excluded unless the procedure is part of an approved clinical trial for a life-threatening condition. Dental and vision care are excluded except as described in §4.2.

§4.2 Limited Vision and Dental Benefits
The Plan provides one eye examination per Plan Year with a $25 copay and one pair of corrective lenses every 24 months. Dental benefits are limited to accident-related treatment of natural teeth, payable at 80 percent of the Allowed Amount up to $1,000 per accident. Routine dental cleanings remain excluded under this Plan.

§4.3 Mental Health and Substance Use
In-network outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent with a 30-visit limit per Plan Year. Inpatient substance use treatment is limited to 60 days per Plan Year and requires prior approval as described in §3.1. Out-of-network mental health services are covered at 60 percent without visit limits.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible for out-of-network claims. In-network providers submit claims directly, and Covered Persons are not responsible for filing. Claims submitted more than 12 months after the date of service will be denied as untimely.

§5.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice by submitting a written request to the Plan Administrator. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care claims. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of a first-level denial.

§5.3 Notices and Termination
Covered Persons must report address changes and family status changes within 31 days of the event. Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment terminates, except as continued under COBRA-type continuation rules administered by the Plan Administrator. Termination of coverage does not affect the right to appeal claims for services rendered during the coverage period, as described in §5.2.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Compass PPO 2500 Demonstration Plan

§1.1 Plan Identity
This document describes the Meridian Compass PPO 2500, a preferred provider organization health plan created solely for software demonstration purposes. The plan is fictional and carries no real-world coverage obligations. All names, amounts, and rules are invented for testing interface behavior.

§1.2 Definitions
Covered Person means an enrolled employee or eligible dependent who has satisfied the waiting period. Network Provider means a practitioner or facility contracted with the fictional Compass network. Allowed Amount means the maximum the plan recognizes for a covered service, which is 1,400 units for an office visit under this demonstration.

§1.3 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous service. Dependents eligible for enrollment include a lawful spouse and children under age 26. Enrollment changes outside the annual open period require notice within 31 days of a qualifying event.

§2.1 Effective Date and Waiting Period
Coverage begins on the first day of the month after the waiting period described in §1.3 is satisfied. Late enrollees who declined initial coverage wait until the next annual enrollment period. A dependent reaching the age limit in §1.3 loses coverage on the last day of the month containing the birthday.

§2.2 Annual Deductible
Each Covered Person pays a deductible of 2,500 units per calendar year for network services and 4,000 units for out-of-network services. Family coverage accumulates at 5,000 units network and 8,000 units out-of-network. Deductible amounts reset each January 1.

§2.3 Coinsurance and Out-of-Pocket Maximum
After the deductible in §2.2 is met, the plan pays 80 percent of the Allowed Amount for network services and 60 percent for out-of-network services. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is 6,500 units per person network and 12,000 units out-of-network. Once the maximum is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of the Allowed Amount for the remainder of the year.

§3.1 Physician Services
The plan covers office visits to network physicians at a flat copayment of 35 units, waived for preventive visits. Specialist visits require a copayment of 60 units. Out-of-network physician services are subject to the deductible and coinsurance in §2.2 and §2.3.

§3.2 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital care is covered for up to 120 days per confinement, with a per-admission copayment of 500 units for network facilities. Emergency room visits are covered at a 250 unit copayment, waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient within 24 hours. Out-of-network emergency services are paid at the network level.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
The plan covers generic drugs at a 15 unit copayment, preferred brand drugs at a 45 unit copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs at a 90 unit copayment. A 90-day supply through the maintenance program costs two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §4.1 and carry a 20 percent coinsurance up to a monthly maximum of 300 units.

§3.4 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at the same cost sharing as §3.1, with a limit of 40 visits per year. Inpatient substance use treatment is covered for up to 30 days per calendar year. Intensive outpatient programs are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, limited to 60 sessions per year.

§3.5 Therapy and Rehabilitation
Physical therapy is covered for 30 visits per calendar year, occupational therapy for 20 visits, and speech therapy for 20 visits, all subject to a 40 unit network copayment per visit. Visits may be combined across therapy types up to a combined limit of 50. Speech therapy for congenital conditions is an exception to the visit limit in this section.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Certain services require prior approval from the plan administrator, including inpatient admissions, imaging over 800 units in Allowed Amount, and specialty drugs under §3.3. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before scheduled non-emergency services. Emergency admissions require notification within 48 hours or the benefit is reduced by 25 percent.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, vision correction surgery, or services received outside the country except emergencies. Weight loss programs are excluded, though medically necessary bariatric surgery is an exception when prior approval under §4.1 is obtained. Dental care for adults is excluded except for treatment of accidental injury to sound natural teeth.

§4.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this plan pays the difference between its Allowed Amount and the primary plan payment, not to exceed the amount it would pay as primary. The plan may recover overpayments made because of coordination errors. Claims affected by coordination must be reported within 90 days of the primary payment.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. Network Providers submit claims on behalf of Covered Persons, while out-of-network services may require the member to submit documentation. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt.

§5.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days, and a second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first decision. Urgent care appeals are decided within 72 hours.

§5.3 Administration
The plan is administered by a fictional benefits department for demonstration purposes only. This plan and all cross-references among §3.3, §4.1, and §5.2 exist to exercise document navigation in software. No real benefits, payments, or obligations arise from this document.

§1.1 Definitions
This plan is a fictional product created solely for software demonstration purposes. The term "Covered Person" means an individual who has enrolled in this sample plan within the demo environment. The term "Benefit Period" means the simulated coverage window of ninety consecutive days beginning on the demo enrollment date.

§1.2 Fictional Nature
All dollar amounts, limits, and procedures in this document are invented and have no real-world effect. No actual insurance, payment, or coverage is created by this document. Any resemblance to a real plan is unintended.

§1.3 Interpretation
In this demo, headings are for navigation only. Words like "visit" and "day" refer to simulated records in the demo database. Conflicts between clauses are resolved in favor of the clause with the lower section number.

§2.1 Eligibility
A demo user is eligible if the simulated applicant is between ages 18 and 64 in the demo profile. The applicant must reside in the fictional state of Demo Land within the sample dataset. Dependents under age 26 may be added to the simulated record.

If the demo user selects the fictional Express Start option, the waiting period is reduced to one day for an added fee of 40 sample dollars. Pre-existing simulated conditions recorded before the enrollment date are subject to §4.3.

If the emergency visit results in inpatient admission, the copayment is credited toward the hospital copayment in §3.1. §4.1 Prior Approval
Simulated inpatient admissions, surgeries, advanced imaging, and brand-name drugs require prior approval recorded at least 3 demo days before the service. Approval may be granted retroactively within 2 demo days after an emergency admission. Services without required approval are paid at 50 percent of the demo benefit amount.

§4.2 Referral Rules

§7.4 Administration
This sample plan is administered by the fictional Demo Administration Unit within the software environment. Demo records are retained for the life of the demo session plus 30 days. This plan may be modified or deleted by the demo administrator at any time without notice.

When a Member has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays secondary according to the birthday rule for dependent children. Payments made by this Plan as secondary will not exceed the amount it would have paid as primary. Overpayments must be refunded within 60 days of written notice. This Plan will not reduce payment below the amount described in §2.1 by more than the primary plan's payment.

§3.4 Subrogation
The Plan has the right to recover benefits paid from any third party responsible for an injury, up to the total amount paid. Members must notify the Plan within 30 days of any claim or lawsuit against a third party. Recovery costs are shared with the Member at a 20 percent ratio after the Plan is made whole. Members must cooperate with the Plan's reasonable requests for documentation.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions (except emergency admissions, which require notice within 48 hours), imaging exceeding $1,000 in allowed charges, specialty drugs under §2.3, and durable medical equipment over $2,500. Requests must be submitted at least 10 business days before the service. Approval is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance. Emergency services are never denied solely for lack of prior approval.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be filed within 12 months of the date of service. Written notice of an appeal must be filed within 180 days of the denial notice. Members must notify the Plan of address changes within 60 days. Failure to timely file a claim voids coverage for that service, except where the Member was mentally incapacitated, in which case the deadline extends 90 days after incapacity ends.

§4.3 Cost Sharing Limits
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 per person and $12,000 per family for in-network services, and $12,000 per person out of network. Once the in-network maximum is reached, the Plan pays 100 percent of the Allowed Amount for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copayments under §2.1 count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Premiums, penalties under §3.1, and amounts above the Allowed Amount do not count toward the maximum.

§4.4 Emergency Care
Emergency services are covered at the in-network level regardless of provider, after a $150 emergency room copayment that is waived if the Member is admitted within 24 hours. Post-stabilization services are covered at network levels once the attending physician determines the Member may be transported. Out-of-network follow-up care is subject to §2.1 cost sharing. Members are encouraged, but not required, to notify their primary care provider within 24 hours.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be submitted on the demonstration claim form within the deadline in §4.2. The Plan will adjudicate clean claims within 30 days and deny or request information within 45 days. Payment is made to the Member unless the provider is assigned benefits. An explanation of benefits accompanies each adjudication.

§5.2 Appeals
A Member may appeal a denial in two levels. The first-level appeal must be filed within the period in §4.2 and is decided by a reviewer not involved in the original denial within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care. A second-level appeal must be filed within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided within 45 days. External review by a fictional independent board is available after exhaustion of both levels.

§5.3 Plan Administration
The Plan Administrator maintains enrollment records, issues identification cards within 15 days of enrollment, and publishes an annual summary of benefits before each Plan Year. Amendments take effect on the first day of the month following adoption, except reductions in benefits require 90 days advance notice. The Administrator may correct clerical errors within 12 months of discovery. Interpretations of ambiguous provisions are resolved in favor of coverage for demonstration purposes only.

§5.4 General Provisions
This Plan is governed by the fictional laws of the Demonstration Jurisdiction. No provision may be waived orally. If any clause is held invalid, the remainder continues in effect. This document supersedes all prior demonstration summaries dated before the current Plan Year.

SYNTHETIC
Azure Valley Select HMO — Demo Plan Alpha

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan" means the Azure Valley Select HMO Demo Plan Alpha described in this document. "Network Provider" means a provider contracted with the Plan as of the date of service. "Medical Necessity" means a service that is clinically appropriate and not primarily for convenience. "Copayment" means the fixed dollar amount the Member pays at the time of service.

§1.2 Eligibility and Enrollment
Members must reside in the fictional service area and enroll during an open enrollment period or within 30 days of a qualifying event. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following approval, subject to a 60-day waiting period for non-preventive services. Dependent coverage ends at age 26 unless the dependent is disabled.

§1.3 Effective Date and Termination
Coverage terminates at 11:59 p.m. on the last day of the month in which membership ends. Members may continue coverage for up to 18 months under the Plan's continuation provision by paying the full premium plus 2 percent. Termination does not affect claims for services rendered before the termination date.

§2.1 Primary Care Physician
Each Member must select a Primary Care Physician from the Network Directory. The Primary Care Physician coordinates all care and issues referrals for specialty services. Members may change their Primary Care Physician once per quarter by notifying Member Services in writing.

§2.2 Referrals and Prior Approval
Specialist visits require a referral under §2.1 except for emergency care, annual eye exams, and routine gynecological care. Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, MRI and CT imaging, and any procedure costing more than 1,500 dollars. The Plan will respond to prior approval requests within 5 business days.

§2.3 Emergency Care
Emergency services are covered at network rates regardless of provider, with a 150 dollar emergency room copayment waived if the Member is admitted within 24 hours. Members must notify the Plan within 48 hours of an emergency admission, or the admission is subject to review under §4.2. Follow-up care must be transferred to a Network Provider.

§3.1 Covered Benefits
The Plan covers physician visits, hospitalization, maternity care, mental health services, prescription drugs, and preventive care as described in §3.2. Office visits carry a 25 dollar copayment and specialist visits a 40 dollar copayment. Inpatient stays are covered at 100 percent after a 500 dollar per-admission deductible.

§3.2 Preventive Services
Annual physicals, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings are covered at 100 percent with no copayment. One routine eye exam per year and two cleanings per year are included. Preventive services do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum in §5.2.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a 10 dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs a 30 dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a 60 dollar copayment. A 90-day supply is available through the mail-order program at 2.5 times the retail copayment. Certain specialty drugs require prior approval under §2.2.

§4.1 Limits and Exclusions
Cosmetic surgery, fertility treatment, and experimental procedures are excluded. Dental care for members over age 19 is excluded except as required by accidental injury. Hearing aids are limited to one device per ear every 36 months.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Services excluded under §4.1 are covered when medically necessary to treat a diagnosed condition, subject to prior approval under §2.2. Reconstructive surgery following a covered mastectomy is covered in full. Dental care related to cancer treatment is covered at network rates.

§4.3 Out-of-Network Services
Services from non-Network Providers are not covered except for emergency care under §2.3 and services unavailable in the network. If the Plan approves an out-of-network referral, the Member pays the applicable copayment plus 20 percent of allowed charges. Members are not balance-billed for approved referrals.

§5.1 Cost Sharing Limits
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is 6,000 dollars per Member and 12,000 dollars per family. Once the maximum is reached, covered services are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the calendar year. Copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance all count toward the maximum.

§5.2 Annual Limits
Coverage for physical therapy is limited to 30 visits per year, chiropractic care to 20 visits per year, and inpatient mental health care to 45 days per year. Speech therapy is limited to 40 visits per year for members under age 18. Limits reset each January 1.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Network Providers file claims directly with the Plan, and Members using out-of-network services under §4.3 must submit claims within 180 days of service. Clean claims are paid within 30 days of receipt. Explanations of benefits are mailed within 10 days of payment or denial.

§6.2 Appeals
Members may appeal a denial within 180 days by submitting a written request to the appeals department. A first-level decision is issued within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent matters. A second-level review by an independent reviewer is available after exhaustion of the first level.

§6.3 Grievances
Grievances concerning quality of care or service may be filed at any time and are acknowledged within 5 business days. The Plan issues a written grievance decision within 30 days. Filing a grievance does not affect the appeal rights described in §6.2.

§7.1 Notices and Administration
All notices to the Plan must be in writing and sent to the address shown on the Member identification card. The Plan may amend this document upon 60 days written notice to Members. This policy is synthetic and exists solely for software demonstration purposes.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: AuroraFlex Silver 2200 Demo Plan

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "covered service" to mean a health care service listed in §3.1 and not excluded under §4.1. The term "plan year" begins on the first day of the demo month and ends twelve months later. The word "member" refers to the synthetic enrollee created for this software demonstration.

§1.2 Eligibility
A member must reside in the demo service area and be at least eighteen simulated years old. Dependents may be added within thirty-one days of a qualifying synthetic life event. Enrollment takes effect on the first day of the following demo month.

§1.3 Waiting Period
New members must wait fourteen days before non-emergency covered services are payable. Emergency services are payable from the effective date. Preventive care described in §3.2 has no waiting period.

§2.1 Premium and Cost Sharing
The monthly premium for this demo plan is 2200 demo dollars. The annual deductible is 3000 demo dollars per member. After the deductible, the member pays twenty percent coinsurance for most covered services.

§2.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The out-of-pocket maximum is 6500 demo dollars per plan year. Once reached, the plan pays one hundred percent of allowed amounts for covered services. Premiums and non-covered services do not count toward this maximum.

§2.3 Copayments
Primary care visits carry a 25 demo dollar copayment. Specialist visits carry a 60 demo dollar copayment. Copayments apply before the deductible is satisfied, as described in §2.1.

§3.1 Covered Benefits
Covered services include inpatient hospital care, outpatient surgery, physician visits, emergency care, prescription drugs, and mental health services. Inpatient care is covered up to ninety days per plan year. Prescription drugs are covered per the demo formulary in §3.3.

§3.2 Preventive Care
Annual wellness visits, standard immunizations, and recommended screenings are covered at one hundred percent with no cost sharing. One wellness visit per plan year is allowed. Additional preventive visits follow the cost sharing in §2.3.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a 15 demo dollar copayment, preferred brands 45 demo dollars, and non-preferred brands 90 demo dollars. A thirty-day supply is standard; a ninety-day supply is available through the demo mail channel. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§3.4 Emergency Services
Emergency room visits are covered at network cost sharing regardless of location. A 150 demo dollar copayment applies, waived if the member is admitted within twenty-four hours. Follow-up care is subject to §3.1.

§4.1 Limits and Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures, experimental treatments, and services outside the demo formulary are excluded. Dental and vision care for adults are excluded except accidental injury to sound natural teeth. Exclusions do not apply to services required by emergency stabilization under §3.4.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident is payable despite the cosmetic exclusion in §4.1. Off-formulary drugs may be covered upon a documented medical necessity appeal under §6.2. Maxillofacial devices for sleep apnea are covered at fifty percent.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, imaging over 500 demo dollars in allowed cost, and specialty drugs require prior approval. Requests must be submitted at least five days before scheduled services. Approval is valid for sixty days from the date of issuance.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Members must notify the plan of inpatient admissions within forty-eight hours, or the claim is reduced by twenty percent. Emergency admissions must be reported within seventy-two hours. Failure to notify does not reduce claims for services under §3.2.

§5.3 Network Rules
In-network services are paid at the cost sharing in §2.1. Out-of-network services are paid at sixty percent of the allowed amount after a separate 1000 demo dollar deductible. Out-of-network emergency care is always paid as in-network per §3.4.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be filed within ninety days of the date of service. Clean claims are paid within thirty days of receipt. Denied claims generate a written explanation within fourteen days.

§6.2 Appeals
A member may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial notice. First-level appeals are decided within thirty days; expedited appeals within seventy-two hours when life or health is at risk. A second-level appeal may be requested within sixty days of a first-level denial.

§6.3 Termination and Continuation
Coverage ends if premiums remain unpaid for thirty-one days after the due date. A member whose coverage ends may reinstate within sixty days by paying all overdue premiums. Reinstated members are not subject to the waiting period in §1.3.

§6.4 Plan Administration
The plan administrator maintains records for seven demo years. Changes to benefits or cost sharing require sixty days advance written notice to members. This document exists solely for software demonstration and confers no actual coverage.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: MetroFlex Commercial Property Shield 500

§1.1 Definitions
The term "Insured Premises" means the commercial office location listed on the schedule, together with adjacent walkways used for business access. The term "Covered Property" means furniture, fixtures, computers, and inventory owned by the insured or held in trust for others. The term "Peril" means any covered cause of loss described in §3.1.

§1.2 Eligibility
This policy applies only to businesses with fewer than 250 employees and annual gross receipts under 40 million dollars. The insured must occupy at least 60 percent of the Insured Premises for business purposes. Eligibility begins after a 14-day waiting period from the application date, unless waived by written endorsement.

§2.1 Effective Period
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the effective date shown on the schedule and continues for a 12-month term. Renewal requires written notice at least 30 days before expiration. The insurer may non-renew with 60 days advance notice for material misrepresentation discovered during the term.

§2.2 Prior Approval Requirements
Any alteration to the Insured Premises exceeding 25,000 dollars in value requires prior written approval from the insurer. Off-premises storage of Covered Property for more than 45 consecutive days also requires prior approval. Failure to obtain approval reduces recovery under §3.2 by 25 percent.

§2.3 Notice Deadlines
The insured must report any loss within 72 hours of discovery. A written proof of loss must be submitted within 60 days of the initial report. Late notice is excused only where the insured demonstrates the delay was beyond reasonable control.

§3.1 Covered Perils
The policy covers direct physical loss caused by fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, explosion, sprinkler leakage, and vehicle impact. Coverage for water damage applies only when the water escapes from plumbing systems within the Insured Premises. Theft coverage applies only when there are visible marks of forcible entry or exit.

§3.2 Benefits and Payment Limits
The insurer will pay the lesser of the actual cash value or the scheduled limit of 500,000 dollars per occurrence for Covered Property. Business interruption benefits are limited to 25,000 dollars per month for a maximum of 6 consecutive months. Electronic data restoration is payable up to 10,000 dollars per policy year.

§3.3 Cost Sharing
A deductible of 2,500 dollars applies to each occurrence under §3.1. A separate deductible of 10,000 dollars applies to water damage and sprinkler leakage claims. The insured retains 10 percent coinsurance on business interruption benefits, calculated after the deductible.

§4.1 Exclusions
Loss caused by flood, earthquake, wear and tear, inherent vice, or intentional acts of the insured is excluded. Nuclear hazard and war are excluded in all forms. Cyber events, including ransomware and data breach, are excluded except for the electronic data restoration benefit described in §3.2.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Flood is covered up to 50,000 dollars per occurrence if the insured has purchased the Water Endorsement and paid the additional premium. Earthquake loss is covered when damage results from ensuing fire. Excluded causes of loss do not bar coverage for a subsequent covered peril, provided the covered peril is not excluded under §4.1.

§4.3 Concurrency Limitation
Where a claim involves both covered and excluded perils, the insurer pays only the portion of loss directly attributable to covered perils. The insured bears the burden of segregating covered from excluded damage. If segregation is impossible, the insurer pays 50 percent of the disputed portion up to 100,000 dollars.

§5.1 Claims Administration
The insurer will acknowledge each claim within 5 business days of receipt. An adjuster will inspect the Insured Premises within 15 calendar days for claims exceeding 10,000 dollars. Payment is issued within 30 calendar days of reaching agreement on the amount of loss.

§5.2 Appeals
The insured may appeal a denied claim within 90 days of the denial notice. Appeals must be submitted in writing and include supporting documentation. The insurer will issue a final appeal decision within 45 days of receiving a complete appeal.

§5.3 Dispute Resolution
If an appeal under §5.2 is unsuccessful, the parties shall submit to mediation before initiating litigation. Mediation costs are shared equally between the parties. Suit must be brought within 2 years of the date of loss, and no suit lies unless the insured has complied with §2.3.

§6.1 Subrogation
The insurer acquires the insured's rights of recovery against third parties to the extent of payment made. The insured must not impair subrogation rights, including by settling with a responsible third party without consent. The insured may recover any deductible amount from a third-party recovery before the insurer's share.

§6.2 Policy Administration
The insured must maintain accurate records of Covered Property and make them available for inspection annually. Premium is due within 30 days of the invoice date, and coverage suspends if premium remains unpaid 10 days after written reminder. All notices under this policy must be delivered to the addresses shown on the schedule.

§6.3 Cancellation
The insured may cancel this policy at any time with 15 days written notice and receive a pro rata refund. The insurer may cancel for nonpayment with 10 days notice or for fraud with immediate effect upon written notice. Any refund under this section is calculated without penalty to either party.

SYNTHETIC
Demo Plan: NovaShield Short-Term Medical Sample Plan (Illustration Only)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Expense" means a charge for a Medically Necessary service rendered by an Eligible Provider, not exceeding the Usual and Customary rate. "Benefit Period" means the period beginning at 12:01 a.m. on the Coverage Effective Date and ending at 12:00 midnight on the earlier of the Coverage End Date or the date the Covered Person reaches the $250,000 Policy Maximum. "Deductible" means the amount the Covered Person must pay before benefits are payable.

§1.2 Definitions Continued
"Medically Necessary" means a service or supply that is appropriate and generally accepted by the simulated medical community for the diagnosed condition. "Eligible Provider" means any licensed practitioner, facility, or pharmacy operating within the demo environment. "Usual and Customary" means the 80th percentile of charges recorded in the synthetic fee schedule maintained for this demonstration.

§1.3 Interpretation
Words in the singular include the plural, and headings are for convenience only. Any undefined term carries its ordinary meaning within this fictional document. Ambiguities shall be resolved in favor of clarity for the software demonstration, not in favor of any party.

§2.1 Eligibility
A person is eligible if they are between 18 and 64 years of age, reside in a state where the demo plan is offered, and are not covered by another medical plan at the time of application. Eligibility also requires completion of a synthetic health questionnaire with no more than two disclosed pre-existing conditions. Applicants must be able to perform at least three of six simulated activities of daily living.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Coverage begins on the later of the day the application is approved or the 5th day after the postmark date of a completed application. For applicants disclosing a pre-existing condition, a 30-day waiting period applies to treatment of that condition only. No benefits are payable for services rendered before the Coverage Effective Date.

§2.3 Effective and Termination Dates
Coverage terminates at 12:00 midnight on the earliest of the end date selected, the date the $250,000 Policy Maximum is exhausted, the date premium is not paid within the 10-day grace period, or the date the Covered Person becomes eligible for other medical coverage. Termination does not affect claims for services rendered while coverage was in force, provided they are submitted within 90 days as described in §6.1.

§3.1 Inpatient Hospital Benefit
The plan pays 80% of Covered Expenses for room and board, up to $1,200 per day for a semi-private room, after the Deductible. The daily limit rises to $1,800 for intensive care. The inpatient stay limit is 60 days per Benefit Period, and stays related to a pre-existing condition count toward the same limit but are subject to the waiting period in §2.2.

§3.2 Outpatient and Physician Benefit
The plan pays 100% of Covered Expenses for physician office visits after a $40 copayment per visit, limited to 6 visits per Benefit Period. Outpatient surgical procedures are paid at 80% after the Deductible. Emergency room visits are paid at 100% after a $250 copayment, which is waived if the Covered Person is admitted as an inpatient within 24 hours under §3.1.

§3.3 Prescription Drug Benefit
Generic drugs are covered at 100% after a $15 copayment; brand-name formulary drugs at 75% after a $35 copayment; and non-formulary brand drugs at 50% after a $60 copayment. A 30-day supply limit applies per fill. No prescription benefit applies during the pre-existing condition waiting period described in §2.2.

§3.4 Additional Benefits
The plan pays up to $500 per Benefit Period for diagnostic imaging, $300 for lab work, and $150 for one routine eye examination. Ambulance services are covered up to $750 per trip for ground transport and $2,000 for air transport when Medically Necessary. These benefits are subject to the same Deductible as described in §1.1.

§4.1 Cost Sharing Summary
The Deductible is $2,500 per Covered Person per Benefit Period, with a family maximum of $5,000. After the Deductible, the Covered Person pays 20% coinsurance up to an out-of-pocket maximum of $7,500 per person. Copayments under §3.2 and §3.3 do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.2 Prior Approval Requirement
Inpatient admissions, outpatient surgeries, air ambulance, and any service expected to exceed $1,500 require prior approval. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before non-emergency services, or within 48 hours after emergency services. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces benefits by 50%, except where the Covered Person was unconscious or incapacitated.

§4.3 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of a planned admission must be given at least 5 business days in advance. Notice of an emergency admission must be given within 48 hours, or as soon as reasonably possible. Claims submitted without timely notice remain payable if the delay was beyond the Covered Person's reasonable control.

§5.1 Exclusions
No benefit is payable for services related to war, self-inflicted injury, cosmetic procedures, experimental treatment, dental care, vision correction surgery, or maternity care. Exclusions do not apply to complications arising from a covered accidental injury, which are paid as described in §3.1. Substance use treatment is excluded, except for one medically supervised detoxification stay of up to 5 days per Benefit Period.

§5.2 Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
Charges arising from a disclosed pre-existing condition are payable only after the 30-day waiting period in §2.2 has been satisfied. Undisclosed conditions discovered during a claim review are excluded entirely and may result in rescission under §5.3. This limitation does not apply to accidental injuries unrelated to the condition.

§5.3 Rescission
The plan may rescind coverage only if the Covered Person made an intentional misrepresentation on the synthetic health questionnaire. Rescission requires 30 days written notice and refunds all premium paid less claims already paid. Rescission does not apply to innocent omissions that did not affect the underwriting decision.

§5.4 Other Limitations
No duplicate benefits are payable under more than one clause for the same charge. Benefits in excess of the Usual and Customary amount are the Covered Person's responsibility. Charges for services rendered by a provider related to the Covered Person within the third degree are excluded.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible if that is not feasible. Claims received after 12 months from the date of service are denied without appeal rights. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 calendar days, and partial payments are issued for incomplete claims pending missing information.

§6.2 Claim Denials
A denied claim receives a written explanation identifying the clause under which it was denied, such as §5.1 or §5.2. The explanation states the specific reason, the amount denied, and the appeal deadline. Denials based on missing prior approval under §4.2 must cite the date the request was received.

§6.3 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denial within 180 days of the explanation of denial. Appeals must be in writing and may include supporting records from an Eligible Provider. A first-level appeal is decided within 30 days by a reviewer not involved in the original denial.

§6.4 Second-Level Appeals and Arbitration
If the first appeal is denied, a second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days and is decided within 45 days by a different reviewer. If the second appeal is denied, the Covered Person may elect binding arbitration under the simulated arbitration framework of this demo jurisdiction. Arbitration costs are shared equally, and the result is final for purposes of this fictional plan.

§7.1 Administration
Premiums are $150 per month for a single Covered Person, $280 for two, and $400 for a family, payable in advance. A 10-day grace period applies after each due date, during which coverage continues. This plan is a synthetic artifact for software demonstration only and confers no actual coverage or legal rights.

SYNTHETIC
Fictional Demo Health Plan: AuroraFlex Silver 750 Sample Plan

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "covered person" to mean an enrollee or enrolled dependent listed on the application record. The term "network provider" means any provider in the demonstration provider directory maintained for this software demo. The term "plan year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the first day of the demo calendar month selected at enrollment.

§1.2 Eligibility
Any fictional applicant in the demo dataset may enroll during the simulated open enrollment window. Dependents under age 26 in the synthetic data are eligible for coverage. Enrollment takes effect on the first day of the month following a completed demo enrollment transaction, subject to the waiting period in §1.3.

§1.3 Waiting Period
Coverage for non-emergency services begins after a 30-day waiting period from the effective date. Preventive care described in §3.1 is exempt from the waiting period. Emergency services are never subject to the waiting period.

§2.1 Benefits Overview
This plan covers hospitalization, physician services, prescription drugs, and emergency care for covered persons. Inpatient coverage is limited to 60 days per plan year. Outpatient visits are covered subject to the cost sharing in §4.1.

§2.2 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $40 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $75 copayment. A 90-day supply is available through the demo mail-order channel at twice the retail copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.2.

§3.1 Preventive Care
Preventive services, including annual physicals, immunizations, and screening tests listed in the demo schedule, are covered at 100 percent with no cost sharing. One preventive visit per covered person per plan year is covered. Services performed during a preventive visit that are diagnostic rather than preventive are subject to the cost sharing in §4.1.

§3.2 Mental Health Services
Outpatient mental health visits are covered up to 30 visits per plan year with a $25 copayment. Inpatient mental health care is counted within the 60-day hospitalization limit in §2.1. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms as mental health services.

§3.3 Maternity Care
Prenatal visits are covered as preventive care under §3.1. Delivery and related inpatient care are subject to the deductible and the hospital day limit in §2.1. A newborn is automatically covered for the first 31 days, after which a demo enrollment update is required.

§3.4 Emergency Care
Emergency room services carry a $150 copayment, waived if the visit results in a direct inpatient admission. Emergency care received outside the demo network is covered at the in-network level. Follow-up care after an emergency visit is not emergency care and is subject to §2.1 and §4.1.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
The annual deductible is $750 per covered person and $1,500 per demo household. After the deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of allowed amounts for in-network services and 60 percent for out-of-network services. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $4,500 per person, after which the plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the remainder of the plan year. Copayments described in §2.2 and §3.2 do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.2 Out-of-Network Limits
Out-of-network charges above the demo allowed amount are the responsibility of the covered person. Balance billing by out-of-network providers is not covered. Emergency services are excepted from this clause as provided in §3.4.

§5.1 Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures, experimental treatments, and services not listed in the demo benefit schedule are excluded. Weight loss surgery is excluded except when medically necessary documentation is approved under §5.2. Dental and vision care for adults are excluded, though pediatric vision is covered once per plan year.

§5.2 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions planned at least 7 days in advance, imaging exceeding $1,000 in demo allowed amount, and all specialty drugs. Requests must be submitted through the demo portal and are decided within 5 business days, or 72 hours for urgent requests. Denied prior approval may be appealed under §6.2.

§5.3 Notice Deadlines
Claims for out-of-network services must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Inpatient stays must be reported within 48 hours of admission when not pre-approved under §5.2. Failure to meet a deadline results in denial unless the covered person shows the delay was reasonable under demo rules.

§6.1 Claims Administration
In-network providers submit claims directly through the demo clearinghouse. Covered persons using out-of-network providers must submit an itemized claim form within the deadline in §5.3. Claims are paid within 30 days of receipt or a demo explanation of benefits is issued.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The demo review committee issues a written decision within 30 days of receiving a complete appeal. A second-level appeal is available within 60 days of a first-level denial, and the decision at that level is final for purposes of this synthetic plan.

§6.3 Termination and Reinstatement
Coverage terminates if demo premium data shows nonpayment beyond a 30-day grace period. A covered person whose coverage terminated may request reinstatement within 60 days by paying all outstanding demo premiums. Reinstated coverage is not subject to a new waiting period under §1.3.

§7.1 Coordination of Benefits
When a covered person has other synthetic coverage, this plan pays secondary according to the demo coordination rules. Claims must identify all other coverage at submission. Overpayments identified during coordination must be refunded within 60 days.

§7.2 Subrogation
If a covered person recovers damages related to an injury for which this plan paid benefits, the plan may recover up to the amount it paid. The covered person must notify the plan within 30 days of any settlement. Recovery is reduced proportionally when the covered person incurred attorney fees, except that no recovery is taken from funds designated for future medical care in the demo dataset.

§7.3 Plan Changes
The demo sponsor may amend this plan by publishing an updated synthetic document at least 60 days before the change takes effect. Mid-year benefit reductions do not apply to services already authorized under §5.2. Continued enrollment after the effective date constitutes acceptance of the amended terms.

§7.4 Governing Provisions
This document is entirely fictional and exists only to populate a software demonstration. No real coverage, obligation, or benefit is created by these clauses. Any resemblance to an actual insurance product is unintentional.
