SYNTHETIC
WhiskerShield Complete Pet Protection Plan

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Pet" means a dog or cat enrolled under this plan that is between eight weeks and fourteen years of age at the time of enrollment. "Eligible Expense" means a veterinary charge for a covered condition that is reasonable, customary, and documented by an invoice. "Pre-existing Condition" means any illness or injury first observed, diagnosed, or treated before the effective date of coverage or during a waiting period.

§1.2 Enrollment and Eligibility
Enrollment requires a completed application and payment of the first monthly premium of forty dollars for cats and sixty-two dollars for dogs. A pet must be examined by a licensed veterinarian within thirty days before enrollment or within fourteen days after the effective date. Pets older than fourteen years may be enrolled only under the Legacy Rider described in §2.4.

§1.3 Waiting Periods
Coverage for accidents begins five days after the effective date. Coverage for illnesses begins twenty-one days after the effective date. Coverage for orthopedic conditions begins forty-five days after the effective date unless the pet passes a waiting-period waiver examination, in which case it begins immediately after the exam.

§2.1 Accident Benefits
The plan pays eighty percent of Eligible Expenses for accidents, up to an annual limit of twelve thousand dollars. This includes emergency care, surgery, hospitalization up to ten days per incident, and prescription medications for up to sixty days per incident. The remaining twenty percent is the pet owner's cost share as described in §3.2.

§2.2 Illness Benefits
The plan pays seventy percent of Eligible Expenses for illnesses, up to an annual limit of eight thousand dollars. Chronic conditions are covered for up to three consecutive years per diagnosis, after which the condition is considered managed and excluded under §4.3.

§2.3 Wellness Add-On
For an additional fourteen dollars per month, the plan reimburses up to four hundred fifty dollars per year for routine care, including two examinations, two vaccinations, one dental cleaning, and one heartworm or flea prevention refill. Wellness benefits are not subject to deductible or cost share.

§2.4 Legacy Rider
Pets aged eleven to fourteen may enroll with a reduced annual limit of four thousand dollars and a cost share of thirty percent. The Legacy Rider excludes hereditary conditions entirely, except hip dysplasia, which is covered if the pet was examined and cleared before enrollment as described in §1.2.

§3.1 Deductible
An annual deductible of two hundred fifty dollars applies to accident and illness benefits under §2.1 and §2.2. The deductible resets each policy year on the effective date. Wellness benefits under §2.3 are not subject to the deductible.

§3.2 Cost Sharing
After the deductible is met, the plan reimburses the percentages stated in §2.1, §2.2, and §2.4. Reimbursement is based on the actual invoice amount, capped at the fee schedule published in the administrator's benefit guide. Cost share does not apply to wellness benefits under §2.3.

§3.3 Annual and Lifetime Limits
The total combined benefit for accidents and illnesses is capped at fifteen thousand dollars per policy year. A lifetime cap of forty thousand dollars applies across all years of continuous enrollment. Amounts paid under §2.3 do not count toward either cap.

§4.1 General Exclusions
The plan does not cover pre-existing conditions as defined in §1.1, cosmetic procedures, breeding costs, or elective euthanasia. Experimental treatments not approved by the attending veterinarian's written justification are excluded.

§4.2 Curable Pre-Existing Condition Exception
A pre-existing condition that showed no symptoms and required no treatment for eighteen consecutive months is considered cured and becomes covered, subject to the waiting periods in §1.3. Bilateral conditions such as cruciate ligament injuries are covered on the second side if the first side was treated after coverage began.

§4.3 Managed Chronic Conditions
After the three-year coverage window in §2.2 expires, medications and monitoring for that condition are excluded. Emergency flare-ups requiring hospitalization remain covered as accidents under §2.1 only if caused by an unrelated event.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Non-emergency procedures expected to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars require prior approval submitted at least five business days in advance. Emergency treatment requires notice to the administrator within seventy-two hours of admission. Failure to notify within seventy-two hours reduces reimbursement by twenty-five percentage points.

§5.2 Claim Submission
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of treatment and must include the itemized invoice and medical record notes. Claims received after ninety days are denied without appeal rights, except for claims delayed by documented hospitalization exceeding thirty days.

§5.3 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within sixty days of the denial notice. The administrator must issue a written decision within thirty days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal may be filed within thirty days of the first decision and is reviewed by a different examiner.

§5.4 Premium Changes
Premiums may increase once per policy year by no more than fifteen percent, with sixty days written notice. Pets with continuous enrollment for five or more years receive a loyalty discount of ten percent applied after any increase.

§6.1 Administration
The administrator processes claims within fifteen business days of complete submission. Reimbursements are issued by electronic transfer or mailed check at the pet owner's choice. Policy documents are stored for seven years and are available upon written request.

§6.2 Cancellation and Continuity
The pet owner may cancel within thirty days of the effective date for a full premium refund if no claims were filed. The administrator may cancel only for non-payment, with ten days notice and a cure period. Continuous enrollment is preserved during any cure period for purposes of the lifetime cap in §3.3 and the cure exception in §4.2.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Horizon Choice HDHP 4500 (Demo Plan, Fictional)

§1.1 Definitions
In this fictional plan, "Qualifying Expense" means any charge covered under §3 that would be permitted by a high-deductible health plan under applicable demo rules. "Plan Year" means the twelve months beginning each January 1 for this software demonstration. "Designated Bazaar" means the fictitious network of providers labeled Demo-Network-A within the software.

§1.2 Eligibility
Sample users may enroll in this synthetic plan if they are simulated employees who work at least 30 demo-hours per week. Enrollment takes effect on the first day of the simulated month following a 60-day waiting period. Eligibility ends when the demo user record is deactivated, at which point continuation under the fictional COBRA-like module may apply.

§1.3 Effect of Enrollment
Enrollment in this demo plan also enrolls the user in the fictional Demo Health Savings Account feature without further action. Contributions to that account are simulated at 50 percent of the deductible, capped at 1,500 demo-dollars per Plan Year. This arrangement does not create any real account or entitlement.

§2.1 Covered Services
The plan pays for simulated physician visits, inpatient stays, outpatient surgery, prescription drugs under the fictional tier formulary, and emergency care rendered inside or outside Designated Bazaar. All amounts are expressed in demo-dollars and have no real-world meaning. Services must be rendered by simulated providers recorded in the demo database.

§2.2 Preventive Care
Preventive services on the fictional Demo Preventive List are covered at 100 percent before the deductible. This benefit is limited to one annual physical, one well-child visit per simulated minor per year, and the immunizations listed in that demo list. If a preventive visit produces a diagnostic service, that service is subject to the deductible under §4.1.

§2.3 Prescription Drugs
Simulated drugs on Tier 1 cost 15 demo-dollars, Tier 2 cost 40 demo-dollars, and Tier 3 cost 75 demo-dollars after the deductible is met. Before the deductible is satisfied, drugs are paid at full simulated price except for insulin analogs and the asthma controller drugs on the fictional Demo Preventive Drug List, which cost 25 demo-dollars at all times. A 90-day simulated retail fill is available at 2.5 times the 30-day cost sharing.

§2.4 Mental Health and Substance Use
Simulated outpatient therapy visits are covered up to 40 visits per Plan Year. Simulated inpatient behavioral treatment is covered up to 60 days per Plan Year. These services are never subject to prior approval when rendered in an outpatient office setting.

§3.1 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual deductible is 4,500 demo-dollars per individual and 9,000 demo-dollars per family, embedded so that each individual meets the individual deductible before benefits begin. After the deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of simulated allowed charges until the out-of-pocket limit. The out-of-pocket limit is 6,500 demo-dollars per individual and 13,000 demo-dollars per family, after which the plan pays 100 percent of covered charges for the rest of the Plan Year. The deductible and out-of-pocket limits described here also apply to prescription drug cost sharing under §2.3.

§3.2 Copayments and Coinsurance
After the deductible, simulated office visits carry a 30 demo-dollar copayment and specialist visits a 50 demo-dollar copayment. Simulated urgent care carries a 75 demo-dollar copayment and the emergency room a 300 demo-dollar copayment that is waived if the user is admitted as a simulated inpatient. Copayments do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket limit in §3.1.

§3.3 Emergency Services
Emergency services are covered without prior approval at the in-network simulated cost sharing regardless of where they are rendered. Balance-billed simulated amounts above the allowed charge do not count toward the limits in §3.1 and are recorded separately in the demo ledger. A follow-up simulated office visit within 7 days of an emergency discharge is covered as a routine visit under §3.2.

§4.1 Limits
Simulated inpatient stays are limited to 120 days per Plan Year unless a continued-stay approval is granted under §5.1. Simulated physical, occupational, and speech therapy are limited to a combined 30 visits per Plan Year. Simulated chiropractic care is limited to 12 visits per Plan Year, of which the first 4 are covered before the deductible as preventive spinal manipulation.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes simulated cosmetic surgery, experimental procedures not on the fictional Demo Approved Technology List, vision hardware beyond one pair of simulated lenses per Plan Year, and elective dental care for users over age 19. Orthodontia is excluded except when required by a simulated cleft palate condition documented in the demo record. Exclusions do not apply to services needed to repair a complication of a previously covered simulated procedure, provided the complication was not reasonably foreseeable under demo logic.

§4.3 Non-Network Providers
Simulated out-of-network services are covered at 60 percent after a separate out-of-network deductible of 6,750 demo-dollars per individual. Users pay simulated charges above the recognized amount directly in the demo interface. Out-of-network cost sharing does not accumulate toward the in-network limits in §3.1.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Simulated inpatient admissions, imaging listed as advanced on the Demo Imaging List, and all Tier 3 drugs require prior approval. Approval decisions are rendered in the simulation within 5 demo-days for standard requests and 1 demo-day for expedited requests. Services approved under this clause are still subject to the deductible in §3.1.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Users must notify the fictional plan administrator of a simulated inpatient admission within 48 hours, or within 24 hours for simulated maternity admissions. Failure to notify reduces the simulated paid amount by 15 percent, not to exceed 500 demo-dollars. Simulated claims for out-of-network care must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service.

§6.1 Claims Processing
Simulated claims are adjudicated within 30 demo-days of receipt, and 95 percent of clean simulated claims are processed within 15 demo-days under the demo service standard. Users receive a simulated explanation of payment showing allowed amounts, amounts applied to the deductible under §3.1, and the simulated balance. Duplicate simulated claims for the same date and code are rejected automatically by the demo engine.

§6.2 Appeals
A user may appeal a denied simulated claim within 180 days by filing through the demo appeal module. First-level appeals are decided within 30 demo-days, and second-level appeals within 60 demo-days, by a simulated reviewer not involved in the original denial. A denial involving a simulated urgent care request is decided within 72 demo-hours at every level.

§6.3 External Review and Termination
If the second-level appeal under §6.2 upholds a denial, the user may request simulated external review within 60 days. This fictional plan may be terminated by the demo administrator with 30 days written simulated notice, except that termination is immediate for simulated fraud as defined in the demo integrity module. Upon termination, accumulated deductible amounts under §3.1 are preserved in the demo record for 90 days to allow seamless re-enrollment in the demonstration.

SYNTHETIC
Made-Up Plan Name: Meridian Flex PPO 2500 Demonstration Plan

§1.1 Plan Purpose
This document describes a demonstration preferred provider organization plan created solely for software testing. All terms, amounts, and procedures are fictional and should not be treated as a real insurance product. The plan simulates how coverage rules interact with claims processing systems.

§1.2 Definitions
Covered Person means an employee or dependent enrolled under §2.1. Network Provider means a provider contracted with the fictional Meridian network. Allowed Amount means the maximum the plan recognizes for a service, set at the fee schedule published annually. Deductible means the amount a Covered Person pays before benefits apply, which is $2,500 per person or $5,000 per family per calendar year.

§1.3 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible for coverage. Dependents include a legal spouse and children under age 26. Eligibility determinations are made by the fictional employer's human resources simulation module.

§2.1 Enrollment and Waiting Period
New employees must enroll within 31 days of their hire date. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following completion of a 60-day waiting period. Late enrollees may only join during the annual open enrollment window of November 1 through November 30.

§2.2 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment terminates. A Covered Person may continue coverage for up to 18 months under the simulated continuation rules at a monthly premium of $640. Notice of election must be submitted within 45 days of termination.

§3.1 Physician Services
The plan pays 80 percent of the Allowed Amount for in-network physician visits after the Deductible is satisfied. Out-of-network visits are paid at 60 percent. Preventive visits are covered at 100 percent with no Deductible, as described in §3.2.

§3.2 Preventive Care
Annual physicals, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings are covered at 100 percent in network. One well-child visit per child per year is included without cost sharing. Services billed as preventive but medically necessary beyond the screening protocol are processed under §3.1.

§3.3 Hospital Benefits
In-network hospital stays are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, with a $350 per-admission copayment. Out-of-network stays are covered at 60 percent with a $750 per-admission copayment. The plan limits covered stays to 120 days per calendar year, excluding stays related to childbirth as described in §3.4.

§3.4 Maternity Care
Prenatal visits are covered at 100 percent in network without Deductible. Delivery is subject to the hospital copayment under §3.3 but not the Deductible. A 48-hour inpatient stay following vaginal delivery and 96 hours following cesarean delivery is automatically approved.

§3.5 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $15 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $45 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $90 copayment. A 90-day supply through the simulated mail channel costs two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval under §4.1 and are limited to a 30-day supply.

§3.6 Mental Health Services
In-network outpatient therapy is covered at 80 percent with a 30-visit annual limit. In-network residential treatment is limited to 45 days per calendar year. Out-of-network services are covered at 60 percent with a 20-visit annual limit.

§3.7 Emergency Care
Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent after a $250 copayment, waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient. The network requirement in §3.1 does not apply to emergency services. Follow-up care within 72 hours of discharge is processed as a regular office visit.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions other than emergencies, imaging over $1,500, physical therapy beyond 12 visits, and all specialty drugs. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least 5 business days before the service. Approval is valid for 60 days from the date issued.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, vision correction surgery, experimental treatments, and services rendered by an immediate family member of the Covered Person. Weight reduction programs are excluded except when prescribed for a documented metabolic condition. Dental care is excluded except for injury to sound natural teeth occurring while covered under this plan.

§4.3 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $6,500 per person and $13,000 per family for in-network services. Once reached, the plan pays 100 percent of the Allowed Amount for the remainder of the calendar year. Copayments under §3.5 do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.4 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has other coverage, this plan pays according to the birthday rule for dependent children. Payments made by this plan will not exceed the Allowed Amount less amounts paid by the primary plan. Overpayments must be reimbursed within 90 days of notice.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service. Claims missing required itemized detail will be pended for 30 days pending additional information. Clean claims are simulated to be paid within 14 calendar days.

§5.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The first-level appeal is decided within 30 days, and a second-level appeal within 45 days. A Covered Person may submit written comments and records at any level.

§5.3 Notice Deadlines
Notice of intent to appeal a prospective denial of a scheduled service must be given at least 10 days before the service date. Notice of a dependent status change must be given within 31 days of the event. Failure to meet these deadlines forfeits the associated benefit except in cases of documented incapacity.

§5.4 Plan Administration
The plan administrator maintains enrollment records and issues summary notices twice per year. Changes to benefit levels under §3.1 through §3.7 require 60 days advance written notice to enrollees. The administrator's decisions on administrative matters, other than claim denials subject to §5.2, are final under this demonstration.

§5.5 Subrogation
If a Covered Person recovers damages from a third party for an injury also paid by the plan, the plan is entitled to reimbursement up to amounts paid. The Covered Person must notify the administrator within 30 days of filing any third-party claim. Recovery costs are shared proportionally when the Covered Person was not made whole.

§5.6 Fraud and Misuse
Intentional misstatement of facts on enrollment or claim forms voids benefits for the affected services. The administrator may recover amounts paid based on fraudulent submissions within 3 years of payment. Restitution arrangements are simulated and carry no real-world consequence.

§6.1 Amendment and Termination
The fictional employer may amend or terminate this demonstration plan at any time with 30 days notice. Terminated coverage does not affect claims for services rendered before the termination date. This document expires automatically when the demonstration environment is destroyed.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Flex Short-Term Disability Plan (Demo Form D-774)

§1.1 Covered Person
A covered person is any enrolled participant who satisfies the eligibility rules in §2.1. Coverage applies only while the participant is actively employed by the sponsoring employer. Dependents are not eligible for disability benefits under this plan.

§1.2 Disability
Disability means the inability, due to injury or sickness, to perform the material duties of your own occupation. Total disability must be certified by a licensed physician. Pregnancy is treated as a disability only for the recovery period described in §3.3.

§1.3 Benefit Week
A benefit week begins each Monday and ends the following Sunday. A week counts as a week of disability only if you are disabled for at least four of its five scheduled workdays. Partial weeks are counted in the manner described in §3.4.

§2.1 Eligibility
You are eligible on the first day of the month following 30 days of continuous employment of at least 30 hours per week. Enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the eligibility date. Late enrollment requires evidence of insurability, which the administrator may decline.

§2.2 Effective Date of Coverage
Coverage takes effect on the eligibility date if any required contribution is paid by the employer, and otherwise on the date your first contribution is authorized. No benefits are payable for a disability that begins before your coverage is effective.

§2.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which your employment ends. You may continue coverage under the continuation rules of §2.4, but not beyond 12 weeks.

§2.4 Continuation During Leave
Coverage may be continued during an approved unpaid leave of absence if you pay the full monthly contribution of 96.50. Failure to pay within 30 days of the due date ends continuation coverage. Any disability beginning during continuation is subject to §3.2.

§3.1 Weekly Benefit
The plan pays 65 percent of your pre-disability weekly earnings, up to a maximum of 1,150 per week. The minimum weekly benefit is 45. Benefits are calculated using the definition of benefit week in §1.3.

§3.2 Benefit Duration and Waiting Period
Benefits begin on the eighth calendar day of disability, except that accidents meeting the definition in §1.2 have a zero-day waiting period. The maximum benefit period is 11 weeks for sickness and 26 weeks for accident. If the waiting period is not satisfied, the days are bridged if you return to work for fewer than 14 days and relapse, as provided in §4.2.

§3.3 Pregnancy Benefits
Benefits for normal pregnancy are payable for 6 weeks for vaginal delivery and 8 weeks for cesarean delivery. A physician may certify an extended recovery period due to complications, which is payable for up to 4 additional weeks at the rate in §3.1.

§3.4 Part-Week and Partial Benefits
If you are disabled for fewer than five workdays in a benefit week, the weekly benefit is prorated by one-fifth for each day of disability. If you return to work in a reduced-capacity role with earnings of less than your pre-disability earnings, the plan pays 75 percent of the difference, up to 700 per week, for no more than 8 weeks.

§3.5 Coordination with Other Income
Benefits are reduced by other wage-replacement income, including state disability and workers' compensation awards, so that total income does not exceed 85 percent of pre-disability earnings. You must report other income within 10 days of receipt. Overpayments are recoverable under §6.3.

§4.1 Exclusions
No benefit is payable for disability caused by war, self-inflicted injury, commission of a felony, or cosmetic surgery that is not medically necessary. Disability caused by substance use is excluded unless you are participating in a recognized treatment program. Mental or nervous conditions are limited to the 6-week duration described in §4.2 rather than the standard duration in §3.2.

§4.2 Exceptions and Special Limits
Mental or nervous conditions, and disabilities related to chronic fatigue or unverified pain, are payable for a maximum of 6 weeks. An exception may be granted where inpatient hospitalization occurs, in which case the full 11-week duration in §3.2 applies. Relapse within 14 days of return to work is treated as one continuous period of disability for the purpose of waiting periods and duration limits.

§4.3 Preexisting Conditions
A disability arising from a condition for which you received treatment, consultation, or medication during the 3 months before your effective date is excluded for the first 12 months of coverage. Treatment limited to routine maintenance of a stable condition does not count as preexisting treatment. If you had comparable prior coverage continuing without a break of more than 30 days, the exclusion is reduced by the length of that prior coverage.

§5.1 Prior Approval
 elective treatment scheduled in advance, including surgery, requires notification to the administrator at least 5 business days before the disability begins. Failure to notify may delay benefits until notice is provided. Emergency conditions are exempt from prior approval.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
You must give written notice of disability within 20 days of the first day of disability, or as soon as reasonably possible. Proof of disability from your treating physician is due within 30 days of the claim date and every 30 days thereafter. Continued failure to submit proof suspends benefits until proof is received.

§5.3 Cost Sharing and Contributions
Participants contribute 24 percent of the monthly premium through payroll deduction, and the employer contributes the remainder. No contribution is required during an approved family leave under the continuation rules of §2.4. Contributions are not refundable once paid.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are administered by the plan's designated claims unit, which pays benefits weekly in arrears. A claim decision is issued within 20 days of receipt of complete proof of disability. If additional time is needed, you will be notified of the reason and the decision date, which may be extended once by 15 days.

§6.2 Appeals
If a claim is denied, you may appeal in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. Your appeal must be decided within 45 days, extendable once by 30 days if you agree. The appeal review is conducted by a reviewer who was not involved in the original denial, and the reviewer's decision is final under this plan.

§6.3 Overpayments and Plan Changes
Overpayments arising from coordination under §3.5 or Clerical error must be repaid within 90 days of written demand, or the administrator may deduct them from future benefits. The sponsor may amend benefit levels, contribution rates, or limits at any plan anniversary upon 60 days' notice. This document is for demonstration purposes only and confers no rights.

SYNTHETIC
Luminara Health Flex HMO Plan 7C

§1.1 Definitions
In this plan, "network provider" means a facility or professional that has signed a participation agreement with the plan administrator. "Covered service" means a medically necessary service listed in §3 that is not excluded under §4. "Plan year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the member's enrollment anniversary date.

§1.2 Eligibility
Coverage is available to employees who work at least 30 hours per week and to their enrolled dependents. New enrollees are subject to a 60-day waiting period before any benefits begin, except that preventive care under §3.2 begins on day one. Dependents may remain enrolled until the end of the plan year in which they turn 26.

§1.3 Enrollment Changes
Members may add dependents within 31 days of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, or loss of other coverage. Changes made outside that window take effect only at the next open enrollment period. Open enrollment runs each year during the first 30 days of November.

§1.4 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the member's employment ends or premiums become more than 30 days delinquent. Members terminated for nonpayment may reinstate coverage within 45 days by paying all back premiums plus a $75 reinstatement fee.

§2.1 Primary Care and Referrals
Each member must designate a primary care provider from the network directory. Specialist visits require a referral from the primary care provider, except for routine obstetric care and annual eye examinations. Referrals remain valid for 12 months or 6 visits, whichever comes first.

§2.2 Out-of-Network Rule
Services from providers outside the network are not covered except for emergency care as described in §3.5 and authorized referrals when no network specialist is available within 50 miles. In such authorized cases, the plan pays at the in-network level. Members who knowingly use out-of-network providers without authorization are responsible for the entire charge.

§2.3 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, advanced imaging such as MRI and PET scans, and any procedure with an expected charge above $2,500. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least 10 business days before the scheduled service. Emergency admissions must be reported to the plan within 48 hours of admission.

§2.4 Emergency Care Notification
Members receiving emergency care at a non-network facility must notify the plan within 48 hours of stabilization, or a family member may do so on their behalf. Failure to notify reduces the plan's payment by 20 percent, unless the member was medically unable to communicate. Follow-up care after an emergency must be transferred to a network provider within 14 days.

§3.1 Covered Benefits Overview
The plan covers physician visits, hospitalization, maternity care, mental health services, prescription drugs, and preventive services as itemized in §§3.2 through 3.6. All covered services are subject to the cost sharing in §5. Services excluded under §4 are never payable, even if recommended by a provider.

§3.2 Preventive Services
Annual physical examinations, immunizations, and age-appropriate cancer screenings are covered at 100 percent with no member cost sharing. One routine gynecological examination per plan year is included. Preventive services are not subject to the deductible described in §5.1.

§3.3 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered for up to 60 days per plan year at the network rate. Each admission requires a $350 copayment, payable once per admission regardless of length of stay. Stays beyond 60 days require documented medical necessity and are reviewed weekly by the plan's utilization staff.

§3.4 Mental Health Benefits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered up to 30 sessions per plan year with a $25 copayment per session. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered up to 45 days per plan year and requires prior approval under §2.3. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms as other mental health services.

§3.5 Emergency Services
Emergency room visits are covered at a $150 copayment, waived if the member is admitted as an inpatient. Emergency care is always covered regardless of network status, as described in §2.2. Members are encouraged to use urgent care centers instead, where the copayment is only $40.

§3.6 Prescription Drugs
Prescriptions are covered through the plan formulary with a $15 copayment for generic drugs, $45 for preferred brand drugs, and $90 for non-preferred brand drugs. A 90-day supply of maintenance medications is available at twice the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval and are limited to a 30-day supply per fill.

§4.1 Excluded Services
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, dental care for members over age 19, vision hardware beyond one pair of standard lenses per plan year, or fertility treatments beyond the initial diagnostic evaluation. Weight loss surgery is covered only when medically necessary criteria are met and prior approval is obtained under §2.3. Experimental treatments are excluded as described in §4.2.

§4.2 Experimental and Investigational Care
Services are considered experimental if they are not approved by recognized national review bodies or if available evidence does not demonstrate a health benefit. The plan's medical committee makes this determination in writing within 30 days of a request. Coverage may be granted as an exception when the treatment is part of an approved clinical trial.

§4.3 Limits on Therapy and Durable Equipment
Physical, occupational, and speech therapy are each limited to 40 combined visits per plan year, with additional visits allowed upon documented progress. Durable medical equipment is covered up to $5,000 per plan year with prior approval. Replacement of equipment is covered only after 36 months of use or documented change in condition.

§5.1 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual deductible is $1,500 per member and $3,000 per family, applying to all services except preventive care under §3.2. After the deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of allowed charges. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $6,500 per member, after which the plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the rest of the plan year.

§5.2 Copayments and Coordination
Copayments listed in §3 do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. When a member has other coverage, this plan coordinates benefits so that combined payments do not exceed the total allowed charge. Members must disclose other coverage at enrollment and upon request.

§6.1 Claims Filing
Network providers file claims directly with the plan; members using authorized out-of-network care must file within 90 days of service. Claims forms must include itemized bills and proof of payment. Clean claims are paid within 30 days of receipt; incomplete claims are returned within 15 days with a statement of what is missing.

§6.2 Claims Denials
The plan issues a written denial within 30 days of receiving a claim, stating the specific reason and the clause relied upon. Denials based on medical necessity are reviewed by a licensed clinician who was not involved in the original decision. Members may request a copy of the clinical criteria used.

§6.3 Appeals
Members may appeal a denial within 180 days by submitting a written request to the appeals office. A first-level appeal is decided within 30 days, or 72 hours when the treating provider certifies that a delay could jeopardize health. A second-level appeal by a separate review panel is available within 60 days of a first-level denial.

§6.4 External Review
If both internal appeals fail, members may request external review by an accredited independent review organization within 60 days. The external reviewer's decision is binding on the plan. The plan pays the $500 filing fee for external review when the original claim exceeded $1,000.

§7.1 Premiums and Administration
Premiums are due on the first day of each month, with a 30-day grace period before termination under §1.4. The plan administrator maintains member records for at least seven years and issues an annual summary of benefits each January. Members must report address changes within 60 days to avoid disruption of notices under §§6.2 and 6.3.

SYNTHETIC
Aurora Bridge Supplement Plan Z-9

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this policy, "Covered Services" means the benefits listed in §3.1 through §3.4. "Enrollment Date" means the first day of the month following receipt of a completed application and the initial premium payment. "Calendar Year" means January 1 through December 31 of each policy year.

§1.2 Eligibility
Applicants must be at least 65 years of age or entitled to federal retirement health benefits under a qualifying government program. Enrollment is permitted during the six-month open enrollment period beginning the Enrollment Date, or during the annual election window from October 15 through December 7. Late enrollees are subject to a 12% premium surcharge for each year of delayed enrollment, rounded up to the nearest whole year.

§1.3 Waiting Periods
A 90-day waiting period applies to benefits for pre-existing conditions, defined as any condition for which treatment was sought within 12 months before the Enrollment Date. No waiting period applies to accidental injury claims or to the preventive benefits described in §3.4.

§2.1 Hospital Benefits
The plan pays 100% of covered inpatient hospital charges after a daily coinsurance of $45 for days 61 through 90 of any benefit period. The lifetime reserve day pool is 60 days; once exhausted, the plan pays a flat $500 per day for up to 30 additional days per Calendar Year. Charges beyond these limits are the member's responsibility.

§2.2 Skilled Nursing Facility Benefits
The plan pays the full daily amount for days 21 through 100 in a certified skilled nursing facility per benefit period, provided the stay follows a qualifying hospital admission of at least 3 days. Days 1 through 20 are covered without member cost sharing. Stays beyond 100 days are excluded except as described in §4.2.

§2.3 Physician and Outpatient Benefits
The plan pays 20% of the approved amount for physician services after the member satisfies the annual Part B-style deductible of $240. Office visits are subject to a $15 copayment that does not count toward the deductible. Telehealth visits are reimbursed at the same rate as in-person visits.

§2.4 Emergency and Foreign Travel Benefits
Emergency services are covered at 100% after a $75 copayment, with no deductible. Foreign travel emergency coverage pays up to $50,000 per Calendar Year with a $250 deductible and a $45,000 lifetime maximum. Coverage begins 60 days after the foreign travel benefit rider is added and requires prior approval as described in §4.1.

§3.1 Blood Services
The plan covers the first three pints of blood per Calendar Year that are not otherwise replaced or donated. Blood furnished as part of a covered inpatient stay is subject to the cost sharing in §2.1. Autologous blood stored before the Enrollment Date is excluded.

§3.2 Preventive Services
Annual wellness visits, one bone density measurement every 24 months, and one glaucoma screening every 36 months are covered at 100% with no deductible or copayment. Screening colonoscopies are covered at 100%; therapeutic procedures performed during the same encounter are subject to the 20% coinsurance in §2.3.

§3.3 Durable Medical Equipment
The plan pays 80% of the approved rental or purchase price of durable medical equipment prescribed by a participating provider. Repair of covered equipment is included up to $300 per item per Calendar Year. Equipment costing more than $2,500 requires prior approval under §4.1.

§3.4 Excess Charges and Limits
Excess charges above the approved amount for physician services are covered up to 15% of the approved amount, not to exceed $1,500 per Calendar Year. Benefits under this section are not subject to the deductible described in §2.3. Annual out-of-pocket spending under this section is capped at $6,800.

§4.1 Prior Approval and Notice Requirements
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions that are not emergencies, for durable medical equipment exceeding $2,500, and for all foreign travel claims. Requests must be submitted in writing at least 10 business days before the service date, except in emergencies where notice must be given within 72 hours of stabilization. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment for the service by 50%.

§4.2 Extended Care Exception
Members who exhaust the 100 skilled nursing days described in §2.2 may apply once per lifetime for a 20-day extension. Approval requires a physician certification submitted within 15 days of the exhaustion date and is limited to members with no more than one prior extension.

§4.3 General Exclusions
The plan does not cover dental care except when required for the treatment of a covered accident, routine vision hardware more than one pair per Calendar Year, cosmetic surgery, or services rendered by providers who are not participating except in emergencies. Hearing aids are covered only up to $500 per ear every 36 months, an exception to the general exclusion for routine sensory devices.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service; claims received later are denied unless the delay was beyond the member's reasonable control. The plan will issue payment or a denial notice within 30 days of receiving a clean claim. Members may assign payment rights to a participating provider.

§5.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days; second-level appeals may be requested within 60 days of the first-level decision and are decided by an independent reviewer within 45 days. Members may submit up to 10 pages of supporting documentation with any appeal, and benefits under §3.1 through §3.4 may be reinstated retroactively if the appeal is successful.

SYNTHETIC
Lumina Shield Silver 700 Sample Plan (Fictional Demo Document)

§1.1 Definitions
This document uses "Plan Year" to mean the twelve-month period beginning each January 1 and ending December 31. "Covered Services" means medically necessary services listed in §3 that are rendered by an In-Network Provider unless stated otherwise. "Deductible" means the amount a Member must pay before the Plan begins paying benefits, set at 3,500 dollars per person and 7,000 dollars per family per Plan Year.

§1.2 Definitions continued
"Out-of-Pocket Maximum" means the most a Member pays in cost sharing during a Plan Year, which is 8,200 dollars per person and 16,400 dollars per family. "Emergency Service" means care required for a condition that a reasonable person would believe needs immediate attention. "Prior Approval" means advance written confirmation from the Plan that a service is covered, as described in §5.1.

§1.3 Fictional data notice
All names, amounts, providers, and rules in this document are synthetic and generated for software demonstration only. This document creates no rights and describes no real insurance product. Any resemblance to a real plan is unintentional.

§2.1 Eligibility
Coverage is available to fictional enrollees who reside in the Demo Service Area and are not eligible for other synthetic coverage. Enrollment is effective on the first day of the month following approval of a demo application. Newborns are covered automatically for the first 31 days, after which the enrollee must add the child within 60 days.

§2.2 Waiting periods
A 90-day waiting period applies to elective joint replacement and bariatric surgery benefits under §3.4. There is no waiting period for Emergency Services or preventive care. Pre-existing conditions are covered from the effective date without exclusion.

§2.3 Dependent rules
Dependents may remain on the policy until age 26. A dependent who becomes disabled before that age may remain covered indefinitely if the disability began while covered. Changes in dependents must be reported within 30 days of the event.

§3.1 Preventive benefits
Preventive services are covered at 100 percent with no deductible when rendered by an In-Network Provider. This includes one annual physical examination, recommended immunizations, and screening mammograms. Coverage follows the synthetic preventive schedule referenced in §3.2.

§3.2 Office visits and diagnostics
Primary care office visits are covered at a 25 dollar copayment after the Deductible is met. Specialist visits carry a 50 dollar copayment. Laboratory tests are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, and advanced imaging such as MRI requires Prior Approval as described in §5.1.

§3.3 Hospital and emergency benefits
Inpatient hospitalization is covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, limited to 120 days per Plan Year. Emergency Services are covered at the In-Network level regardless of provider network status and without Prior Approval. A 300 dollar emergency room copayment applies, waived if the visit results in direct admission.

§3.4 Prescription drugs
Prescription drugs are covered in three synthetic tiers with copayments of 15 dollars for generic, 45 dollars for preferred brand, and 90 dollars for non-preferred brand drugs. A 90-day supply is available at retail for maintenance drugs at 2.5 times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require Prior Approval under §5.2 and are limited to a 30-day supply per fill.

§4.1 Limits on therapy services
Physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy are each limited to 30 combined visits per Plan Year. Additional visits beyond 30 require Prior Approval and medical documentation. Visits for maintenance rather than restorative purposes are excluded under §6.2.

§4.2 Mental health and substance use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at a 30 dollar copayment with no visit limit. Inpatient mental health care is covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, limited to 60 days per Plan Year. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms as described in §3.3 for hospital care.

§4.3 Dental and vision limits
Adult dental is limited to 1,000 dollars per Plan Year, with a separate 50 dollar deductible. Pediatric dental is covered at 80 percent up to a 2,000 dollar annual maximum. One eye examination and one pair of corrective lenses are covered every 24 months with a 25 dollar copayment.

§5.1 Prior approval rules
Prior Approval is required for inpatient admissions other than emergencies, advanced imaging, specialty drugs, and the therapy extensions mentioned in §4.1. Requests must be submitted at least 10 days before a scheduled service. The Plan must respond within 5 business days; failure to respond within that period is deemed approval.

§5.2 Notice deadlines
Members must notify the Plan of an emergency inpatient admission within 48 hours of admission or by noon of the second business day, whichever is later. Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service. Failure to meet the notice deadline in this section reduces payment by 25 percent but does not deny coverage entirely.

§5.3 Coordination of benefits
When a Member has coverage under more than one synthetic plan, this Plan pays secondary unless its rules make it primary. Members must disclose other coverage at enrollment and within 30 days of any change. Overpayments discovered through coordination must be refunded within 60 days of notice.

§6.1 General exclusions
Services not medically necessary, experimental treatments, and cosmetic surgery are excluded. Dental care for adults beyond the limits in §4.3, hearing aids beyond one per ear every 36 months, and weight loss drugs are excluded. Exclusions do not apply where required by the synthetic regulatory framework referenced in §1.3.

§6.2 Exclusion exceptions
Cosmetic surgery is covered when needed to repair damage from an accident or a covered reconstructive purpose following mastectomy. Hearing aid exclusion does not apply to children under age 18, who receive one hearing aid per ear every 24 months. Experimental treatment may be covered if the treating provider certifies it is the standard of care for the Member's condition and Prior Approval is granted under §5.1.

§6.3 Out-of-network rules
Out-of-Network Provider services are covered at 60 percent after the Deductible, except Emergency Services as described in §3.3. Members are not responsible for amounts above the Plan's allowed charge for emergency out-of-network care. Out-of-network cost sharing does not count toward the In-Network Out-of-Pocket Maximum but counts toward a separate out-of-network maximum of 12,000 dollars.

§7.1 Claims administration
In-Network Providers submit claims directly and Members are not required to file. For out-of-network care, Members submit an itemized claim form within the deadline in §5.2. Clean claims are paid within 30 calendar days of receipt.

§7.2 Denials and appeals
A denied claim triggers a written explanation within 10 business days stating the reason and the appeal rights in this section. Members may file a first-level appeal within 180 days of denial, and the Plan must decide within 30 days. A second-level appeal to the synthetic independent review body must be filed within 60 days of the first-level decision.

§7.3 Urgent appeals
Urgent care appeals, where a delay could jeopardize health, are decided within 72 hours of receipt. A Member may request an expedited external review at the same time as the internal appeal. The outcomes of urgent appeals are honored retroactively to the date of service.

§8.1 Premiums and administration
Monthly premiums for this demo plan are 420 dollars per person and 1,150 dollars per family, payable by the first of each month. A 30-day grace period applies before termination for nonpayment. Reinstatement after termination requires payment of all arrears within 60 days of the termination date.

§8.2 Changes to the plan
The Plan may amend benefit terms upon 60 days written notice before the start of a Plan Year. Mid-year changes affecting active treatment require 30 days notice and do not reduce benefits already authorized under §5.1. Members affected by mid-year changes may disenroll within 30 days of the notice.

§8.3 Termination of coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which a Member requests termination or fails to pay premiums after the grace period. Claims for services rendered before termination are processed under the terms in §7.1 for 90 days afterward. This synthetic document expires automatically at the end of any demonstration session in which it appears.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: Meridian Flex Recovery Plan 500-D

§1.1 Definitions
As used in this synthetic plan, "Disability" means a certified inability to perform the core duties of the Insured Person's own occupation for more than four consecutive scheduled workdays. "Certified" means supported by written documentation from a licensed treating provider participating in the simulated provider network. "Elimination Period" means the consecutive days of certified Disability that must pass before weekly benefits begin, as described in §3.1.

§1.2 Eligibility
An Insured Person must be an active participant of the demo enrollment group, working at least 24 hours per week in a covered role. Coverage begins on the first day of the calendar month following 30 days of continuous service. Persons working fewer than 24 hours per week may enroll only during the annual synthetic open enrollment window, subject to the reduced benefit described in §3.3.

§1.3 Enrollment and Effective Dates
Enrollment elections must be submitted through the demo administration portal within 31 days of the eligibility date. Late enrollees are subject to a 90-day waiting period before coverage takes effect. Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which the Insured Person's participation in the demo group ends.

§2.1 Weekly Benefit
While Disabled and under the ongoing care of a treating provider, the Insured Person receives a weekly benefit equal to 60 percent of pre-Disability weekly earnings, up to a maximum of 1,400 dollars per week. The minimum weekly benefit is 75 dollars. Benefits are paid every 14 days in arrears through the demo payment system.

§2.2 Maximum Benefit Duration
Weekly benefits continue for up to 26 weeks per period of Disability for conditions classified as standard. Conditions classified as extended, including certified post-surgical recovery lasting longer than 12 weeks, may receive up to 39 weeks of benefits. No benefits are payable beyond 52 weeks for any single period of Disability, regardless of classification.

§2.3 Partial Disability Benefits
An Insured Person who returns to work in a reduced-capacity arrangement receives a partial benefit equal to the difference between 60 percent of pre-Disability earnings and current earnings, subject to the weekly maximum in §2.1. Partial benefits may continue for up to 12 weeks. The Insured Person must submit interim progress documentation every 14 days to remain eligible.

§3.1 Elimination Period
The standard Elimination Period is 14 calendar days of certified Disability. For accidents occurring while on covered employer travel, the Elimination Period is reduced to 7 days. Days of paid leave used during the Elimination Period do not count toward it, except that up to 5 days of accrued sick leave may be elected to count retroactively if requested within 20 days of the Disability start date.

§3.2 Prior Approval Requirements
Non-emergency surgical procedures expected to result in Disability of 10 or more days require prior approval submitted at least 10 business days before the procedure date. Emergency procedures are exempt from prior approval, but notification must be submitted within 3 business days of the event. Failure to obtain required prior approval reduces the weekly benefit in §2.1 by 25 percent for the first 4 weeks of benefits.

§3.3 Cost Sharing and Offsets
The Insured Person is responsible for a 50 dollar per-claim processing deduction from the first benefit payment. Weekly benefits are offset dollar-for-dollar by simulated short-term wage-replacement payments from other demo sources, except for payments from personal savings accounts. For reduced-hours enrollees under §1.2, the weekly benefit is capped at 700 dollars.

§4.1 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for Disabilities caused by elective cosmetic procedures, participation in professional athletics, or service in the demo armed forces reserve beyond 15 days of annual duty. Disabilities arising from undocumented off-network treatment are excluded, except in certified emergencies where network access was not reasonably available within 50 miles. Exclusions do not apply to Disabilities caused by certified mental health conditions, which are covered for up to 12 weeks per period.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
The Insured Person must notify the administrator of a Disability within 20 calendar days of the start of the Elimination Period under §3.1. Continued Disability must be recertified every 30 days. Late initial notice reduces benefits retroactively by 10 percent for each full week of delay, up to a maximum reduction of 50 percent.

§4.3 Limits on Recurring Disabilities
A recurrence of the same certified condition within 60 days of returning to work is treated as a continuation of the original period of Disability and does not require a new Elimination Period. A new period of Disability from a different certified condition begins a fresh Elimination Period and a fresh maximum duration under §2.2. No more than two periods of Disability may begin in any 12-month span.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Initial claims must be submitted through the demo claims portal within 60 days of the end of the Elimination Period. Submissions must include the treating provider's certification and the Insured Person's earnings statement from the 8 weeks preceding Disability. Incomplete claims are suspended for up to 45 days pending completion, after which they are denied without prejudice to resubmission.

§5.2 Claims Review
The administrator reviews complete claims within 10 business days and issues a written determination. Benefits under §2.1 begin within 5 business days of an approval determination. Approved claims are subject to audit for up to 12 months, and the administrator may request supplemental documentation no more than twice per claim period.

§5.3 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must state the grounds and may include new certification or documentation. A first-level appeal is decided within 30 calendar days by a reviewer not involved in the original determination, and a second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first appeal decision, decided within 45 calendar days.

§5.4 Administration and Termination of Claims
The administrator maintains all claim records in the demo system for 3 years following final payment or denial. An Insured Person may request a copy of their claim file at no cost once per claim period. Benefits cease immediately upon return to full-duty work, expiration of the maximum duration in §2.2, or termination of the demo demonstration environment.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: DemoShield High-Deductible Health Plan 4500

§1.1 Definitions
In this synthetic plan, "Covered Person" means an individual enrolled under this demonstration document. "Deductible" means the annual amount of Covered Expenses the Covered Person must pay before the plan begins payment, set at 4,500 for single coverage and 9,000 for family coverage. "Covered Expense" means a charge for a Medically Necessary service rendered by an In-Network Provider while this demo policy is in force.

§1.2 Eligibility and Enrollment
Employees of the fictional demo employer are eligible after completing a 60-day waiting period from their start date. Enrollment applications must be submitted within 31 days of becoming eligible. Dependents may include a spouse and children under age 26, except that a child under 26 who is totally disabled may remain covered, as described in §2.3.

§1.3 Effective Date and Termination
Coverage becomes effective on the first day of the month following completion of the waiting period in §1.2. Coverage terminates at midnight on the last day of the month in which employment ends, except that a Covered Person may continue coverage for 18 months under a demonstration continuation provision at a monthly cost of 620. Termination does not affect claims for services rendered before the termination date, subject to the claim deadline in §5.1.

§2.1 Deductible and Coinsurance
After the Deductible in §1.1 is satisfied, the plan pays 80 percent of Covered Expenses for In-Network Providers and 60 percent for Out-of-Network Providers. The Covered Person pays the remaining coinsurance. Preventive services listed in §2.2 are exempt from the Deductible.

§2.2 Preventive Care Benefits
Routine physical examinations are covered once every 12 months at 100 percent, with no Deductible. Immunizations, cancer screenings, and annual well-child visits are also covered at 100 percent, up to a combined maximum of 1,500 per year. These benefits are not subject to the coinsurance described in §2.1.

§2.3 Dependent Disability Extension
A dependent child who becomes totally disabled before reaching age 26 may remain covered beyond that age. Proof of disability must be submitted within 90 days of the child's 26th birthday. The plan may require updated proof annually, and failure to provide it will end coverage as described in §1.3.

§2.4 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 100 percent of the In-Network negotiated rate after the Deductible, up to a limit of 120 days per confinement. An additional 500 per day copayment applies from day 121 onward. Private room charges are covered only when medically necessary, as determined under §1.1.

§2.5 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs are covered at 15 per fill after the Deductible. Preferred brand drugs are covered at 45 per fill, and non-preferred brand drugs at 75 per fill. A 90-day maintenance supply is available at a cost equal to 2.5 times the single fill amount. Specialty drugs require Prior Approval under §3.1.

§3.1 Prior Approval Requirement
Certain services, including inpatient admissions, imaging over 750 in cost, and all specialty drugs, require Prior Approval before services are rendered. The fictional administrator must receive the request at least 5 business days before a scheduled service, or within 2 business days of an emergency admission. Failure to obtain Prior Approval reduces payment by 25 percent, except in emergencies, where no reduction applies.

§3.2 Notice of Claim Deadlines
Written notice of a claim must be given within 20 days of an incident, or as soon as reasonably possible in the case of emergency. Claim forms must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Late claims may be denied unless the delay was beyond the Covered Person's reasonable control, consistent with the emergency exception in §3.1.

§3.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under another demonstration plan, this plan pays only the excess of its benefit over what the other plan pays. The Covered Person must disclose all other coverage at enrollment and within 30 days of any change. Payments made in error must be refunded within 60 days of notice.

§3.4 Third Party Liability
If a Covered Person's injury is caused by another party, the plan pays benefits subject to a subrogation lien. The Covered Person must reimburse the plan from any recovery, up to benefits paid, except that reimbursement is waived when the recovery is less than 10,000. This provision does not reduce the Preventive Care Benefits in §2.2.

§4.1 Annual Out-of-Pocket Limit
The annual out-of-pocket limit is 6,500 for single coverage and 13,000 for family coverage. Once this limit is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of Covered Expenses for the rest of the year. Deductible amounts under §1.1 and copayments under §2.5 count toward this limit; charges from Out-of-Network Providers above the allowed amount do not.

§4.2 Lifetime Maximum
The lifetime maximum benefit under this synthetic plan is 3,000,000 per Covered Person. Once reached, no further benefits are payable, except that the Preventive Care Benefits in §2.2 remain available. Notice will be sent within 30 days of the Covered Person reaching 90 percent of the maximum.

§4.3 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for cosmetic surgery, experimental treatment, vision correction surgery, or services rendered by a member of the Covered Person's household. Injury or sickness arising from war or participation in a felony is also excluded. These exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following a covered accident, as described in §2.4.

§4.4 Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
A pre-existing condition is one for which the Covered Person received diagnosis or treatment within 12 months before the effective date in §1.3. Such conditions are excluded for 12 months, except that a newborn or newly adopted child is exempt from this limitation. Creditable prior coverage reduces the exclusion period day for day, provided it was verified at enrollment under §1.2.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims should be submitted on the demo claim form to the fictional administrator within 90 days of service, consistent with §3.2. The administrator will pay or deny each claim within 30 days of receipt, or 60 days if additional information is needed. Payment is made to the provider or the Covered Person, depending on assignment of benefits.

§5.2 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must be in writing and will be reviewed by a different reviewer within 60 days. If the denial is upheld, a second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days, and the result of that appeal is final under this synthetic document.

§5.3 Provider Networks
In-Network Providers are those under contract with the fictional network at the time of service. Out-of-Network services are covered at the reduced coinsurance in §2.1, and the Covered Person may be billed for amounts above the allowed charge. Emergency services are always paid at the In-Network level, regardless of provider status.

§5.4 Urgent Care and Emergency Benefits
Emergency room services are covered at 250 per visit after the Deductible, waived if the Covered Person is admitted as an inpatient under §2.4. Urgent care visits are covered at 75 per visit. Follow-up care within 72 hours of an emergency is paid at the same level as the emergency visit.

§6.1 Reinstatement
If coverage lapses for nonpayment of premium, it may be reinstated within 31 days by paying all past-due amounts. Coverage is continuous for claims purposes if reinstated within that period, except that the pre-existing limitation in §4.4 applies anew to the gap period. Reinstatement does not shorten the out-of-pocket accumulation under §4.1.

§6.2 Misstatement of Age or Facts
If an age or dependent status misstatement is found, benefits will be adjusted to what the correct premium would have purchased. Misstatements discovered more than 2 years after enrollment are not grounds for rescission, except for intentional fraud. Any premium adjustment will be handled through the administrator described in §5.1.

§6.3 Amendment and Interpretation
The fictional sponsor may amend this demo plan by written notice to Covered Persons at least 30 days before the change takes effect. This document is governed by the fictional laws of the demo jurisdiction. Any ambiguity will be resolved in favor of coverage, except where a specific dollar limit in §§1.1 through 4.2 plainly applies.

SYNTHETIC
Demo Group Health Plan "Blue Meadow Select", a fictional plan created solely for software demonstration purposes.

§1.1 Purpose
This document describes the Blue Meadow Select health plan for employees of a fictional small business. It exists only as sample text for testing claims and enrollment software. No real coverage is offered or implied.

§1.2 Definitions
"Plan Year" means the twelve-month period from January 1 through December 31. "Covered Person" means an eligible employee or enrolled dependent as described in §2.1. "Negotiated Rate" means the fictional pre-agreed provider fee used for all demo calculations.

§1.3 Employer
The sponsoring employer is a fictional company with between 5 and 50 demo employees. The employer contributes 60 percent of employee-only premium and 40 percent of dependent premium. Contribution rates are fixed for the Plan Year.

§2.1 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of employment. A spouse, domestic partner, and children under age 26 may be enrolled. Enrollment must be requested within 31 days of the eligibility date.

§2.2 Waiting Period for Certain Benefits
Dental and vision benefits under §3.3 begin after a 90-day waiting period from the enrollment date. No waiting period applies to medical benefits. The waiting period is waived for new hires who enroll during an annual open enrollment window.

§2.3 Special Enrollment
A Covered Person may enroll mid-year within 31 days of marriage, birth, adoption, or loss of other coverage. Coverage for a newborn is automatic for the first 31 days if the parent is enrolled. Written notice of the qualifying event is required.

§3.1 Medical Benefits
The plan pays 80 percent of the Negotiated Rate for in-network physician visits after the deductible. Preventive care, including one annual physical, is covered at 100 percent with no deductible. Out-of-network services are covered at 60 percent of a fictional reasonable charge.

§3.2 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, limited to 60 days per Plan Year. Each admission requires a $250 fictional copayment. Semiprivate room charges are covered at the Negotiated Rate; private rooms are covered only when medically necessary.

§3.3 Dental and Vision Benefits
Dental coverage includes two cleanings per Plan Year, paid at 100 percent up to $75 per visit. Basic restorative work is covered at 70 percent, subject to a $1,000 annual maximum per person. Vision includes one eye examination and one pair of lenses or contacts per Plan Year, up to $150.

§3.4 Prescription Benefits
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $30 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $50 copayment. A 90-day supply through the fictional mail program costs two times the retail copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§4.1 Deductibles and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The individual deductible is $1,500 per Plan Year and the family deductible is $3,000. The out-of-pocket maximum is $5,000 per person and $10,000 per family. Once the out-of-pocket maximum is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§4.2 Copayments
A $25 copayment applies to each in-network office visit for illness or injury. The copayment does not count toward the deductible but does count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Preventive visits under §3.1 are not subject to any copayment.

§4.3 Lifetime Maximums
The lifetime maximum for all medical benefits is $2,000,000 per Covered Person. The lifetime maximum for dental benefits under §3.3 is $10,000 per person. Amounts paid by the plan, not member copayments, count toward these maximums.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Certain services require prior approval, including inpatient admissions, MRI scans, and specialty drugs. The fictional utilization reviewer must respond within 3 business days of a complete request. Emergency admissions require notice within 48 hours or as soon as reasonably possible.

§5.2 Exclusions
Benefits are not payable for cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, or services rendered by an immediate family member. Weight-loss surgery is excluded unless the body mass index exceeds 40 and a six-month supervised program is documented. Dental work related to a covered accidental injury is payable despite the general dental exclusions in §3.3.

§5.3 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or a documented mastectomy is payable even though cosmetic surgery is excluded under §5.2. Hearing aids, normally excluded, are covered once every 36 months up to $1,000 per ear. Charges for a personal comfort item remain excluded in all cases.

§5.4 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has other coverage, this plan pays according to the fictional birthday rule for dependents. Payments made here will be reduced so that total payments do not exceed the Negotiated Rate. The plan may recover overpayments from future claim payments.

§6.1 Claim Filing
Claims must be filed within 12 months of the date of service. The fictional claims administrator will pay or deny each claim within 30 days of receipt. A complete claim must include the provider statement and the member identifier assigned by the demo system.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must be in writing and will be decided by a different fictional reviewer within 60 days. A second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first appeal decision.

§6.3 Provider Disputes
Disputes over the Negotiated Rate are resolved between the provider and the fictional payer network. A Covered Person is not liable for the difference between billed charges and the Negotiated Rate for in-network services. This protection does not apply to out-of-network services described in §3.1.

§7.1 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment ends or the required premium is not paid. Dependent coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the dependent no longer qualifies under §2.1. Continued coverage for 18 months may be elected at 102 percent of full premium following qualifying termination events.

§7.2 Administration
The plan is administered by a fictional benefits department using demo records only. Premiums are collected through payroll deduction over 12 months. Amendments to this document take effect on the first day of the Plan Year following written notice to all enrolled members.
