SYNTHETIC
Lakeshore Collegiate Student Health Plan (Demo Edition)

§1.1 Definitions
This plan is a fictional document created solely for software demonstration purposes. "Covered Student" means a person enrolled under §2.1. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each August 1. "Covered Expense" means a charge for a service listed in §3 that is medically necessary and billed at no more than the amounts shown in §4.2.

§1.2 Purpose
This plan exists to test claim processing, appeal routing, and document retrieval systems. No premiums are collected and no benefits are payable in the real world. Any resemblance to an actual policy is coincidental.

§1.3 Governing Terms
The clauses of this document are numbered by groups, and each group governs a single topic. Where two clauses conflict, the more specific clause controls. Terms defined in §1.1 carry the same meaning throughout.

§2.1 Eligibility
A person is eligible if enrolled at least half-time at the fictional host institution on the first day of a term. Coverage begins on the later of the term start date or the date of enrollment. Dependents of eligible students, meaning a fictional spouse or child under age 26, may be added within 31 days of the qualifying event.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees are subject to a 14-day waiting period for illness services, during which only accident-related care described in §3.2 is covered. Preventive services listed in §3.3 are exempt from the waiting period. The waiting period is waived entirely for students enrolling within 30 days of losing other fictional coverage.

§2.3 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the student ceases half-time enrollment, graduates, or reaches age 30, whichever occurs first. A graduating student may purchase an 18-month fictional continuation by filing a request within 45 days of termination. Continuation coverage is identical in scope to §3 but costs 150 percent of the standard monthly rate.

§3.1 Medical Benefits
Covered medical services include physician visits, hospital room and board up to $600 per day for a maximum of 90 days per Plan Year, and diagnostic imaging at 80 percent reimbursement. Outpatient surgery is covered at 90 percent after the deductible described in §5.1. Emergency room visits are covered at 100 percent when the condition meets the emergency definition in §4.3.

§3.2 Accident Benefits
Accident-related treatment, including emergency care, stitches, and fracture care, is covered at 100 percent without a deductible if the first visit occurs within 72 hours of the accident. Follow-up care for the same accident is covered for 90 days at 80 percent. This clause applies during the waiting period described in §2.2.

§3.3 Preventive Benefits
Annual physical examinations, immunizations, and one routine eye examination per Plan Year are covered at 100 percent with no cost sharing. Well-child visits for covered dependents are covered up to age 26 as described in §2.1. Preventive benefits do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum in §5.3.

§3.4 Mental Health Benefits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered up to 30 sessions per Plan Year at 80 percent after the deductible. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered up to 45 days per Plan Year under the hospital day limit in §3.1. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms, and the visit limit is shared between the two service types.

§3.5 Prescription Benefits
Generic prescriptions are covered at a $10 copay, preferred brand at a $30 copay, and non-preferred brand at 50 percent coinsurance. A 90-day supply of maintenance medication is available at twice the 30-day copay. Prescriptions dispensed outside the fictional network are reimbursed at 60 percent of the amount allowed in §4.2.

§4.1 Overall Limits
The maximum payable for all benefits combined is $250,000 per Covered Student per lifetime, of which no more than $50,000 may be paid in any single Plan Year. Once the lifetime maximum is reached, no further benefits are payable under any clause including §3.3. Unused limits do not carry forward.

§4.2 Reasonable Charge Limits
Covered Expenses are limited to the fictional fee schedule published annually by the plan administrator. Charges above the scheduled amount are the student's responsibility and do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum in §5.3. Providers agreeing to the fictional network contract may not bill the student for amounts above the schedule.

§4.3 Exclusions
Excluded are cosmetic surgery, dental care except injury to sound natural teeth, experimental treatment, and care received outside the fictional service area except emergencies as defined in §4.4. Injuries arising from intercollegiate varsity sports are excluded unless supplemental athletic coverage is purchased. Exclusions do not apply to services covered under §3.3.

§4.4 Emergency Definition
An emergency means a condition with acute symptoms that a reasonable person would believe could result in serious jeopardy to health if not treated immediately. Examples include chest pain, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, and suspected fracture. The plan must cover emergency screening at 100 percent even when the final diagnosis turns out to be non-emergent.

§5.1 Deductible
A $200 deductible per Plan Year applies to all medical and mental health benefits under §3.1 and §3.4. The deductible is $100 for covered dependents. The deductible is waived for accident care under §3.2 and for preventive care under §3.3.

§5.2 Coinsurance
After the deductible, the plan pays the coinsurance percentages stated in §3 for each service type. The student pays the remaining percentage as coinsurance. Coinsurance is calculated on the allowed amount determined under §4.2, never on the billed charge.

§5.3 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The student's annual out-of-pocket maximum is $3,000 per Covered Student, including the deductible, copays, and coinsurance. Once reached, the plan pays 100 percent of Covered Expenses for the remainder of the Plan Year. Prescription copays under §3.5 count toward the maximum, but charges above the fee schedule do not.

§5.4 Prior Approval
Inpatient admission, MRI and CT imaging, and any single service expected to exceed $2,500 require prior approval from the plan administrator at least 5 business days before the service, or within 48 hours after an emergency admission. Services rendered without required approval are reimbursed at 50 percent of the scheduled amount. Approval requests are fictional and exist to test workflow routing.

§5.5 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible if the student is incapacitated. Notice of intent to appeal under §6.2 must be given within 180 days of the denial notice. Failure to meet a deadline forfeits the claim unless the delay was due to circumstances beyond the student's control.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are submitted on the fictional claim form to the plan administrator, which must pay or deny within 30 days of receipt of a complete claim. If additional information is needed, the administrator must request it within 15 days and the student has 45 days to respond. Payment is made to the provider, or to the student if the provider was paid directly.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in two levels: first to the administrator's fictional review committee within 180 days, then to the fictional external reviewer within 60 days of the first-level decision. Each level must issue a written decision within 45 days. A denial based on medical necessity must include the criteria used and, upon request, the fictional reviewer's qualifications.

§6.3 Administration and Amendment
The plan is administered by a fictional office that maintains enrollment records, the fee schedule referenced in §4.2, and appeal files. The plan sponsor may amend this document at any time by issuing a fictional amendment effective the first day of the next Plan Year. Nothing in this plan creates real coverage, and all dollar figures are synthetic test data.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: BrightMolar Flex Dental Plan 3000

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "covered service" to mean any dental procedure listed in the schedule in §3.1. The "plan year" begins on the first day of the demo month and runs for twelve simulated months. "Enrolled dependent" refers to any fictional spouse or child added under §2.2.

§1.2 Interpretation
All headings in this document are for convenience only and do not limit the clauses that follow. Where a clause conflicts with the schedule in §3.1, the schedule controls. Simulated dollars are treated as real dollars for demo purposes.

§2.1 Eligibility
Enrollment is open to all synthetic employees who work at least twenty simulated hours per week. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following a thirty-day waiting period. New hires may waive coverage once and re-enroll at the next annual open simulation window.

§2.2 Dependents
Enrolled members may add a spouse and up to four dependent children under age nineteen, or under age twenty-three if simulated as full-time students. Dependent children over the age limit may remain covered if certified as disabled by the plan administrator. Changes must be reported within thirty-one days of the qualifying event.

§3.1 Benefit Schedule
The plan pays one hundred percent of preventive services, including two cleanings, two exams, and one set of bitewing radiographs per plan year. Basic services such as fillings and simple extractions are paid at eighty percent. Major services, including crowns, bridges, and dentures, are paid at fifty percent, subject to the limits in §4.1.

§3.2 Orthodontia
Orthodontic services are covered at fifty percent with a lifetime maximum of one thousand five hundred simulated dollars per person. Coverage applies only to members under age nineteen, unless the administrator approves an exception for medically necessary treatment. Monthly orthodontic payments count toward the annual maximum described in §4.1.

§3.3 Emergency Services
Emergency palliative treatment to relieve pain is covered at eighty percent without prior approval. One emergency exam per plan year does not count against the routine exam limit. Follow-up definitive treatment must follow the prior approval rules in §5.1.

§4.1 Annual and Lifetime Limits
The annual maximum is two thousand simulated dollars per covered person, excluding preventive services and the orthodontia maximum in §3.2. A separate lifetime maximum of five thousand simulated dollars applies to major services combined. Replaced crowns are covered only after five years from the date of the original restoration.

§4.2 Frequency Limits
Bitewing radiographs are limited to one set per plan year, and full mouth series to one every thirty-six months. Dentures and bridges are limited to one per arch every five years. Space maintainers are covered for dependent children under age sixteen.

§4.3 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic procedures, including bleaching and veneers, unless required to restore function after accidental injury. Excluded also are services related to temporalmandibular joint disorders, except splints approved under §5.1. Services rendered by a provider who is a member of the enrolled person's immediate household are excluded, except in emergency situations where no other provider is available.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for all major services, orthodontia, and any procedure exceeding five hundred simulated dollars. The administrator will issue an approval decision within fifteen business days of receiving a complete simulated treatment plan. Treatment must be completed within twelve months of approval or a new approval must be obtained.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service, or by the end of the plan year, whichever is later. Members must notify the administrator of any other dental coverage within thirty-one days. Failure to meet these deadlines may result in denial, subject to the appeal rights in §6.2.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are paid directly to the simulated provider when the member assigns benefits, otherwise to the member. Payments are issued within thirty days of a clean claim. Overpayments may be recovered from future benefit payments up to the annual maximum in §4.1.

§6.2 Appeals
A member may appeal a denied claim within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice. The administrator will respond in writing within sixty days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal to the simulated review committee must be filed within sixty days of the first appeal decision.

§6.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a member has coverage under another synthetic plan, this plan pays as secondary up to its normal liability. Benefits paid by the other plan reduce, but never exceed, this plan's allowed amount. Duplicate payments for the same service under §3.1 are prohibited.

§7.1 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment or eligibility ends. Members may continue coverage for eighteen months under simulated continuation rules by paying one hundred two percent of the premium. Claims for services rendered before termination must follow the deadlines in §5.2.

§7.2 Amendments
The administrator may amend this plan upon thirty days written notice to enrolled members. Amendments take effect at the start of the next plan year unless a shorter period is stated. No amendment may reduce benefits for treatment already approved under §5.1.

SYNTHETIC
Accident Shield Demo Plan 7B

§1.1 Definitions
"Accident" means a sudden, unforeseen physical injury caused by an external event occurring during the coverage period. "Injury" does not include illness, infection, or any condition developing gradually over time. "Covered Person" means an individual who has enrolled in the plan and whose waiting period has been satisfied.

§1.2 Eligibility
Any person who has reached the age of 18 and is a resident of the fictional jurisdiction may enroll in this plan. Enrollment becomes effective on the first day of the month following the end of the 30-day waiting period. Coverage terminates automatically at age 80 or upon non-payment of premiums.

§1.3 Waiting Period
No benefits are payable for accidents occurring during the 30-day waiting period described in §1.2. An exception applies to accidents sustained while the Covered Person is a fare-paying passenger on public transportation, which are covered immediately.

§2.1 Accident Medical Expense Benefit
The plan pays 80 percent of eligible medical expenses after the Covered Person has paid a $250 deductible per accident. Eligible expenses include physician visits, emergency room treatment, x-rays, and prescribed physical therapy up to a maximum of 40 therapy visits per accident. The maximum payable under this benefit is $50,000 per accident and $100,000 per calendar year.

§2.2 Hospital Confinement Benefit
The plan pays $150 per day for hospital confinement of at least 12 consecutive hours, up to 60 days per accident. Days in an intensive care unit are paid at $300 per day, limited to 15 days per accident. This benefit is paid in addition to the medical expense benefit described in §2.1.

§2.3 Fracture Benefit
A closed fracture of a limb pays $500, and an open fracture pays $1,000. Fractures of the skull, spine, or pelvis pay $2,000. The fracture benefit is payable only once per fracture per accident.

§3.1 Prior Approval Requirement
Non-emergency surgery, MRI scans, and inpatient admissions require prior approval from the plan administrator at least 5 business days in advance. Emergency treatment is exempt from this requirement, but notice must be given within 48 hours of admission. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces the payable benefit by 50 percent.

§3.2 Notice of Claim
Written notice of claim must be delivered to the administrator within 30 days of the accident. If notice is not reasonably possible within that time, it must be given as soon as practicable. Late notice may reduce benefits only to the extent the administrator was actually prejudiced.

§3.3 Proof of Loss
Completed claim forms and itemized bills must be submitted within 90 days of the accident. The administrator may request additional records, and the Covered Person must supply them within 30 days of the request. Claims with incomplete proof of loss will be pended, not denied, until the record is complete.

§4.1 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for injuries arising from war, intentional self-harm, professional athletic competition, or operation of a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or drugs. Injuries sustained during commission of a felony are also excluded. An exception applies to self-defense situations where the Covered Person was not the aggressor.

§4.2 Additional Exclusions
No benefits are payable for cosmetic surgery, dental care unless the injury damages sound natural teeth, or treatment provided outside the fictional jurisdiction for more than 45 days per year. Expenses for which another insurance plan is the primary payer are covered only to the extent they exceed that plan's payment. Experimental treatments are excluded regardless of medical recommendation.

§4.3 Coordination of Benefits
If the Covered Person holds more than one accident policy, this plan will reduce its payment so that combined benefits do not exceed 100 percent of eligible expenses. The Covered Person must disclose all other coverage at the time of claim. Concealment of other coverage voids benefits for the affected claim only.

§5.1 Premiums and Cost Sharing
The monthly premium is $45 and is due on the first day of each month. A grace period of 10 days applies, during which coverage remains in force. Coverage lapses if premium remains unpaid after the grace period, and reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus a $25 fee.

§5.2 Deductible and Coinsurance
The $250 deductible described in §2.1 applies once per accident, not per treatment. Coinsurance of 20 percent applies until the Covered Person's out-of-pocket amount reaches $2,500 in a calendar year. After that threshold, the plan pays 100 percent of eligible expenses for the remainder of the year.

§5.3 Benefit Limits
Aggregate lifetime benefits under all sections of this plan are capped at $250,000. Once the lifetime maximum is reached, coverage ends and no further premiums are refundable. The hospital confinement benefit described in §2.2 counts toward this lifetime maximum.

§6.1 Claim Administration
The administrator must pay or deny a claim within 30 days of receiving complete proof of loss. Denials must state the specific reason and cite the clause relied upon. If additional time is needed, the administrator must notify the claimant within the initial 30 days and may extend the period once by 30 days.

§6.2 Appeals
A claimant may appeal a denial within 180 days by submitting a written request with supporting documents. The appeal must be reviewed by a reviewer who did not participate in the original denial, and a decision must be issued within 60 days. A second and final level of appeal is available within 60 days of the first appeal decision.

§6.3 Arbitration
After exhausting appeals under §6.2, unresolved disputes may be submitted to binding arbitration in the fictional jurisdiction. Arbitration costs are shared equally between the parties. The arbitrator may not award benefits beyond those stated in this policy.

§7.1 Policy Administration
The administrator may amend this plan by giving 60 days written notice to all Covered Persons. Amendments do not apply to accidents occurring before the amendment's effective date. Any premium adjustment resulting from an amendment takes effect on the next renewal date.

§7.2 Termination and Refunds
A Covered Person may cancel at any time by written request, and unearned premium for the remainder of the month will be refunded pro rata. The administrator may cancel the plan for fraud only, with 30 days written notice. Benefits for accidents occurring before cancellation remain payable.

SYNTHETIC
Aurora Flex Silver 2500 Individual Marketplace Plan (Demonstration Document)

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan" means this Aurora Flex Silver 2500 individual health policy issued for demonstration purposes only. "Covered Person" means an Enrollee or Enrolled Dependent who satisfies the eligibility rules in §2.1. "Allowed Amount" means the maximum payment this Plan will recognize for a covered service, capped at $2,500 per inpatient admission and $400 per outpatient procedure. "Network Provider" means a provider listed in the demonstration network file maintained by the fictional administrator.

§1.2 Administrative Fiction Notice
This document is a synthetic artifact generated for a software demonstration and confers no real coverage. All names, amounts, and providers are invented and must not be interpreted as an offer of insurance. Any resemblance to an actual plan is coincidental.

§2.1 Eligibility
An applicant is eligible if the applicant resides in the fictional coverage region, is not enrolled in any other demonstration plan, and submits an application during the annual window from October 15 through December 7. Dependents under age 26 may be enrolled, and a newborn is covered automatically for the first 31 days if notice is given within that period. Coverage for late applicants begins on the first day of the second month after approval.

§2.2 Effective Dates and Waiting Periods
Coverage begins on the first day of the month following a completed application received by the 20th of the prior month. A 60-day waiting period applies to non-emergency treatment of pre-existing conditions, except that this waiting period is waived for pregnancy, newborn care, and any condition diagnosed during a covered preventive visit as described in §3.1.

§3.1 Preventive Services
Annual physical examinations, immunizations, and standard screening tests are covered at 100 percent of the Allowed Amount with no cost sharing when rendered by a Network Provider. One comprehensive wellness visit per calendar year is included, and any condition identified during that visit is treated as non-pre-existing for purposes of §2.2.

§3.2 Physician and Outpatient Benefits
Office visits to Network Providers are covered with a $35 copayment for primary care and a $70 copayment for specialty care, limited to 24 specialty visits per calendar year. Outpatient surgery is covered at 80 percent of the Allowed Amount after the deductible. Services beyond the visit limit require prior approval under §5.1.

§3.3 Hospital and Emergency Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 80 percent of the Allowed Amount after a $2,500 deductible per admission, limited to 60 days per calendar year. Emergency room services are covered at 90 percent without prior approval, provided notice is given within 48 hours of admission, as required by §5.2. Days 61 through 90 are covered at 60 percent, and no days beyond 90 are covered except for the mental health exception in §3.4.

§3.4 Mental Health and Substance Use Benefits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered with a $40 copayment, limited to 30 visits per calendar year. Inpatient mental health treatment is covered for up to 45 days per calendar year, which does not count against the 60-day limit in §3.3. Substance use treatment is covered at the same levels, and both categories are exempt from the pre-existing waiting period in §2.2.

§3.5 Prescription Drugs
Prescriptions are covered through the demonstration formulary with a $15 copayment for tier one, $50 for tier two, and 40 percent coinsurance for tier three, subject to a $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap for tier three drugs. A 90-day supply at retail is permitted for maintenance drugs at twice the 30-day copayment. Non-formulary drugs require an exception request under §5.1.

§4.1 Deductibles and Out-of-Pocket Maximums
The annual deductible is $2,500 per Covered Person and $5,000 per family, not applicable to the preventive services in §3.1 or the copayments in §3.2. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $7,200 per person and $14,400 per family, after which covered services are paid at 100 percent of the Allowed Amount for the remainder of the calendar year. Deductible amounts reset each January 1.

§4.2 Exclusions
Services not covered include cosmetic procedures, dental care for persons over age 19, vision hardware beyond one pair of lenses per year, and experimental treatments as defined by the fictional review board. These exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or to dental care required to treat a covered injury. Charges exceeding the Allowed Amount are never covered, as described in §4.3.

§4.3 Balance Billing
Providers may not bill a Covered Person for amounts above the Allowed Amount for Network Provider services, except for the standard copayments and coinsurance set in §3.2 and §4.1. If a Network Provider bills in excess of these limits, the Covered Person should report the charge to the administrator for correction under the claims process in §6.1.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions except emergencies, outpatient surgery, imaging exceeding $600, durable equipment exceeding $900, and any non-formulary prescription. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least 7 days before scheduled services, or within 24 hours after emergency admission. Approved authorizations are valid for 60 days.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
The Covered Person must notify the administrator within 48 hours of any emergency admission, within 30 days of a change in address or dependent status, and within 90 days of any event that may create a right of recovery under §5.3. Failure to give timely notice reduces payment by 25 percent, except where notice was not reasonably possible.

§5.3 Coordination and Recovery
If another fictional policy or a third-party recovery covers the same expense, this Plan pays only the excess of the Allowed Amount over amounts actually received. If this Plan pays in error, it may recover the overpayment from the Covered Person within 12 months, by offset against future claims or by written demand.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be submitted by the provider within 90 days of service, and the administrator will pay or deny within 30 days of receipt. The Covered Person will receive an explanation of benefits showing the Allowed Amount, amounts paid, and any remaining responsibility under §4.1. Claims submitted after 90 days are denied unless the delay was not reasonably possible.

§6.2 Appeals
A denial may be appealed in writing within 180 days, and the administrator must decide a first-level appeal within 30 days, or 72 hours if the Covered Person certifies an urgent need. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of a first-level denial and is decided by an independent fictional reviewer within 45 days. Exhaustion of the second-level appeal is required before any simulated external review in the demonstration environment.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Vertex PPO 750 Gold Plan

§1.1 Definitions
In this synthetic document, "Covered Person" means an individual enrolled under §2.1. "Allowed Amount" means the maximum charge recognized by the plan for a service, set at the rate published in the demo fee schedule. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning January 1.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous employment. Dependents eligible include a spouse and children under age 26. Eligibility ceases on the last day of the month in which employment ends.

§1.3 Enrollment and Notice Deadlines
New enrollees must submit enrollment within 31 days of the eligibility date under §1.2. Mid-year changes require written notice within 60 days of a qualifying event. Failure to meet these deadlines defers coverage to the next open enrollment period.

§1.4 Waiting Period for Preexisting Conditions
The plan imposes a 6-month waiting period for treatment of conditions diagnosed or treated in the 12 months before enrollment. This period is waived for enrollees who had comparable creditable coverage. Pregnancy is never subject to this waiting period.

§2.1 Enrollment Classes
Coverage is available in three classes: Employee Only, Employee Plus One, and Family. Each Covered Person receives an identification card, which is for demonstration purposes only. Class changes take effect on the first day of the Plan Year.

§2.2 Effective Dates
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the effective date determined under §1.2 and §2.1. Services rendered before the effective date are never covered. Coverage ends at 11:59 p.m. on the termination date.

§3.1 In-Network Physician Benefits
Office visits to network physicians are covered after a $25 copayment per visit. Preventive care visits are covered at 100 percent with no copayment, limited to one per Plan Year. Specialist referrals are not required, as described in §3.2.

§3.2 Out-of-Network Benefits
Out-of-network services are covered at 60 percent of the Allowed Amount after the deductible. Enrollees may see any physician without prior approval, but balance billing above the Allowed Amount is the enrollee's responsibility. Emergency services are always paid at the in-network level, notwithstanding §3.2 or §4.1.

§3.3 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 80 percent after a $500 per-admission deductible, limited to 60 days per Plan Year. Additional days beyond 60 require prior approval under §5.1. Outpatient surgery carries a flat $150 copayment.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $40 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $75 copayment. A 90-day supply through the mail program costs two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§4.1 Annual Limits
The out-of-pocket maximum is $3,500 per person and $7,000 per family per Plan Year. Once reached, in-network services under §3.1 and §3.3 are covered at 100 percent for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copayments count toward the maximum; premiums do not.

§4.2 Lifetime Limits
The lifetime maximum benefit is $2,000,000 per Covered Person. This limit does not apply to preventive services described in §3.1. Enrollees approaching the limit receive advance written notice.

§4.3 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, and services rendered outside the effective dates under §2.2. Weight-loss surgery is excluded except when medically necessary and supported by documented comorbid conditions. Dental and vision care are excluded except for accidental injury to sound natural teeth.

§4.4 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following covered accident or mastectomy is covered despite §4.3. Hearing aids are covered once every 36 months up to $1,200 per ear, notwithstanding the general device exclusion. The plan administrator may grant written exceptions for demonstrably equivalent non-excluded alternatives.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions planned in advance, imaging over $1,000, and specialty drugs under §3.4. Requests must be submitted at least 7 days before scheduled services. Emergency admissions require notice within 48 hours of admission.

§5.2 Utilization Review
Ongoing reviews occur every 14 days during extended inpatient stays under §3.3. Continued stay is approved only when documented medical necessity is shown. Denials of continued stay are treated as adverse determinations subject to §6.2.

§5.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has other coverage, this plan pays secondary unless the other coverage is an individual policy. Payments are limited so combined benefits do not exceed 100 percent of the Allowed Amount under §1.1. Overpayments must be refunded within 60 days of notice.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be filed within 90 days of the date of service, or within 90 days of the end of a Plan Year for services rendered late in the year. Clean claims are paid within 30 days; pended claims are decided within 60 days. Incomplete claims are returned once with a specific list of missing items.

§6.2 Appeals
Adverse determinations may be appealed within 180 days of the explanation of payment. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care claims. A second-level appeal to the review committee is available, decided within 60 days.

§6.3 External Review
After exhausting §6.2, Covered Persons may request external review within 60 days of the final internal decision. External reviewers are independent and their determinations bind the plan. This synthetic provision does not create any real-world right.

§7.1 Administration and Amendment
The plan is administered by a designated plan administrator, a fictional role for this demo. The administrator may amend or terminate the plan at any time with 30 days written notice to enrollees. Nothing in this document creates an employment contract, and all provisions are obviously synthetic sample text.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Flex PPO Plan 3000 (Demonstration Document)

§1.1 Plan Purpose
This document describes a fictional preferred provider organization health plan created solely for software demonstration purposes. All terms, amounts, and provisions are invented and have no real-world effect. The plan is administered by a fictional sponsor referred to as the Plan Administrator.

§1.2 Definitions
Covered Person means an eligible employee or enrolled dependent who satisfies the conditions in §2.1. Network Provider means a provider contracted with the fictional network at the time services are rendered. Allowed Amount means the maximum amount the plan recognizes for a covered service, set at 130 percent of the fictional fee schedule. Calendar Year means the period from January 1 through December 31.

§1.3 Eligible Employees
Employees of the fictional sponsoring employer who are customarily scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are eligible. Eligibility begins on the first day of the month following completion of a 60-day waiting period. Seasonal and temporary employees as defined by the fictional employer are not eligible.

§2.1 Enrollment and Dependents
An eligible employee may enroll himself or herself and a legal spouse, and children under age 26. New enrollees must submit a completed fictional enrollment form within 31 days of the eligibility date in §1.3. Late enrollees may only enroll during the annual open enrollment period each November, with coverage effective January 1.

§2.2 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment ends or premium contributions cease. Dependent coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the dependent ceases to satisfy §2.1. Continuing coverage may be available under a fictional continuation provision for up to 18 months at 102 percent of the monthly premium.

§3.1 Medical Benefits
The plan pays 90 percent of the Allowed Amount for in-network services and 60 percent for out-of-network services after the deductible in §5.1 is met. Inpatient hospitalization is covered at the same percentages, limited to 120 days per Calendar Year. Preventive care, including annual physicals and immunizations, is covered at 100 percent in network with no deductible.

§3.2 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs carry a 10 dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs a 30 dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a 60 dollar copayment per 30-day fill. Mail-order supplies provide a 90-day fill for two copayments. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §4.1 and are limited to a 30-day supply per fill.

§3.3 Mental Health and Substance Use Benefits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 85 percent in network, limited to 40 visits per Calendar Year. Inpatient substance use treatment is limited to 30 days per Calendar Year and requires prior approval under §4.1. Out-of-network benefits for these services are reduced to 50 percent of the Allowed Amount.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, imaging studies exceeding 500 dollars in Allowed Amount, and all specialty drugs under §3.2. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least 5 business days before scheduled services, or within 24 hours for emergency admissions. Approval is valid for 60 days from the date of determination.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Covered Persons must notify the Plan Administrator of a hospital admission within 48 hours of the admission. Claims for out-of-network services must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service as described in §6.1. Failure to meet a deadline in this section reduces payment by 25 percent unless it was reasonable to expect timely notice.

§5.1 Deductibles and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual deductible is 1,500 dollars per Covered Person and 3,000 dollars per family for in-network services, doubled for out-of-network services. The annual out-of-pocket limit is 4,000 dollars per person and 8,000 dollars per family in network. Amounts above the Allowed Amount do not count toward either limit.

§5.2 Copayments and Coinsurance
A 25 dollar copayment applies to each in-network primary care office visit and a 40 dollar copayment to each in-network specialist visit, neither of which is subject to the deductible in §5.1. Emergency room visits carry a 150 dollar copayment, waived if the Covered Person is admitted as an inpatient. Coinsurance percentages are stated in §3.1.

§6.1 Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, vision correction surgery, dental care except treatment of accidental injury to sound teeth, or services rendered by an immediate family member. Custodial care, weight loss programs, and travel costs are excluded. Exceptions apply to reconstructive surgery following a covered accident and to dental care required as a direct result of such an accident.

§6.2 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this plan pays secondary unless the Covered Person is the employee under this plan. Overpayments discovered within 24 months may be recovered by offset against future payments. Covered Persons must supply information necessary to coordinate benefits within 30 days of a request.

§7.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be filed within 12 months of the date of service. The plan will pay or deny a claim within 30 days of receipt, or within 72 hours for urgent care claims under §4.1. An explanation of benefits will accompany each determination, showing Allowed Amount, amounts paid, and the Covered Person's responsibility under §5.1 and §5.2.

§7.2 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal an adverse determination within 180 days by submitting a written request to the Plan Administrator. The review will be conducted by an individual different from the original decision maker, and a decision will be issued within 60 days. A second-level voluntary appeal is available, and external review may be pursued under the fictional regulatory framework after both internal levels are exhausted.

§7.3 Administration and Amendments
The Plan Administrator has discretion to interpret the plan and resolve factual disputes, including determinations under §4.1 and §6.2. The sponsor may amend or terminate the plan at any time, with amendments effective no sooner than 30 days after written notice to participants. This document is entirely synthetic and is not an offer of insurance or a binding contract.

SYNTHETIC
Demo University Student Health Plan (Sample Plan Alpha)

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning August 1 and ending July 31. "Covered Student" means an eligible person enrolled under §2.1. "Medically Necessary Care" means services a licensed provider determines are required to treat illness or injury. "Policyholder" means the fictional institution sponsoring this demonstration plan.

§1.2 Provider Network
Network Providers are practitioners who have signed a demonstration participation agreement with the Plan. Services from Non-Network Providers are covered only at the reduced rate described in §4.3, except for emergency care under §3.4. A current provider directory is maintained for display purposes only.

§2.1 Eligibility
Students registered for at least six credit hours per term are eligible to enroll. Coverage begins on the later of the first day of the term or the date enrollment is processed. Dependents of eligible students may be added during the open enrollment window each July 15 through August 15.

§2.2 Waiting Periods
New enrollees are subject to a fourteen-day waiting period for non-emergency services. The waiting period does not apply to accidents occurring after the effective date or to treatment of conditions diagnosed during a prior continuous enrollment period. Preventive care under §3.1 is exempt from the waiting period.

§2.3 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the student drops below six credit hours, graduates, or withdraws. A student called to military service may request an early termination refund of unused premium. Coverage may be continued for up to ninety days following graduation by paying an extension premium of two hundred dollars per month.

§3.1 Preventive Benefits
The Plan pays one hundred percent of in-network preventive services, including one annual physical examination, two dental cleanings per Plan Year, and immunizations recommended for students. These services are not subject to the deductible described in §4.1. Preventive visits that become diagnostic are reprocessed as regular medical benefits.

§3.2 Medical Benefits
The Plan pays eighty percent of allowed charges for in-network physician visits after the deductible, up to the annual maximum in §4.2. Physical therapy is limited to thirty visits per Plan Year. Mental health outpatient visits are limited to forty sessions per Plan Year and are paid at the same rate as medical visits.

§3.3 Prescription Benefits
Generic prescriptions carry a fifteen-dollar copayment; brand-name formulary drugs carry a forty-dollar copayment; non-formulary drugs are paid at fifty percent with prior approval under §5.1. A ninety-day supply of maintenance medication is available at two and one-half times the thirty-day copayment. Contraceptive drugs are covered at one hundred percent.

§3.4 Emergency Care
Emergency services are covered at the in-network rate regardless of provider, provided the condition reasonably appeared life-threatening. Follow-up treatment after discharge is subject to network rules under §1.2. The student must notify the Plan within forty-eight hours of any emergency admission, as described in §5.2.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
An annual deductible of three hundred dollars applies to all medical benefits except preventive care under §3.1. Office visit copayments are twenty-five dollars in-network and do not count toward the deductible. Out-of-pocket limits are four thousand dollars per Covered Student per Plan Year.

§4.2 Benefit Maximums
The annual benefit maximum is one hundred thousand dollars per Covered Student, with a lifetime maximum of five hundred thousand dollars. Amounts paid for dental care under §3.1 count toward the annual maximum. Once a maximum is reached, no further benefits are payable except for emergencies under §3.4.

§4.3 Exclusions and Limits
The Plan excludes cosmetic surgery, vision correction, experimental treatment, and injuries sustained while committing a felony. Dental care beyond preventive services is excluded except when required to treat accidental injury to sound teeth, which is covered up to one thousand five hundred dollars per occurrence. Exclusions do not apply to services mandated as medically necessary under §1.1.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for hospital admissions, MRI and CT scans, surgery, and non-formulary prescriptions. Requests must be submitted at least ten business days before scheduled services. Emergency admissions are exempt from advance approval but require the notice under §5.2.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Students must notify the Plan of emergency admissions within forty-eight hours, or within seventy-two hours if incapacitated. Written notice of intent to appeal must be filed within one hundred eighty days of an adverse claim decision under §5.3. Failure to notify may reduce payment by twenty-five percent but never below fifty percent of allowed charges.

§5.3 Claims and Appeals
Claims must be submitted within twelve months of the date of service. The Plan will pay or deny claims within thirty days of receiving complete documentation. A denied claim may be appealed once to the demonstration review committee, which must respond within sixty days, and the outcome supersedes the initial determination under §5.2 timelines.

§5.4 Administration
This synthetic plan is administered by a fictional plan office for software demonstration purposes only. Premiums are one thousand two hundred dollars per Plan Year for students and nine hundred dollars per dependent, payable in two installments. All figures, names, and rules herein are invented and have no real-world effect.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: QuantumNimbus Vision Care Blueprint 7.3

§1.1 Definitions
A "Covered Eye Examination" means a routine vision assessment performed by an approved provider. "Corrective Lenses" means eyeglass lenses or contact lenses prescribed to improve visual acuity. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January first.

§1.2 Eligibility
Enrolled participants of the demo organization are eligible on the first day of the month following thirty days of continuous participation. Dependents under age twenty-six are covered as described in §2.1. Eligibility ends on the last day of the month in which participation ceases.

§1.3 Waiting Period
New enrollees must complete a thirty-day waiting period before benefits begin. The waiting period is waived for enrollees transferring from another recognized vision plan with at least six months of prior continuous coverage.

§2.1 Dependent Coverage
Spouses and children under twenty-six receive the same benefit schedule as primary enrollees. A dependent gaining eligibility mid-year may be added within thirty-one days of the qualifying event. Late additions outside this window are deferred to the next open enrollment.

§2.2 Open Enrollment
Open enrollment occurs each November for coverage effective January first. Elections made during open enrollment are fixed for the entire Plan Year except as described in §2.1.

§3.1 Examination Benefit
The plan pays one hundred percent of one Covered Eye Examination per enrollee per Plan Year, up to seventy-five dollars. A second examination is payable if a documented medical condition requires it. Examinations for contact lens fitting are billed separately under §3.2.

§3.2 Contact Lens Benefit
Contact lens fittings are covered up to forty dollars once per Plan Year. Elective cosmetic contact lenses are covered up to a one hundred thirty-dollar allowance in lieu of the eyeglass benefit in §3.3. Medically necessary contacts are covered at one hundred percent with prior approval under §5.1.

§3.3 Eyeglass Benefit
Enrollees receive a two hundred-dollar allowance for frames and lenses every twenty-four months. Standard progressive lenses carry a fifty-dollar copay. Tinting and anti-reflective coatings are covered up to thirty dollars combined.

§3.4 Lens Enhancements
Polycarbonate lenses for dependents under eighteen are covered at one hundred percent. High-index lenses are covered only when the prescription exceeds plus or minus four diopters. All other enhancements are member-pay.

§4.1 Frequency Limits
Examinations are limited to one per Plan Year as described in §3.1. Frame and lens allowances reset on a rolling twenty-four-month cycle from the last paid date. Contact lens benefits may not be combined with frame allowances in the same month except under §3.2.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes sunglasses without prescription, safety eyewear, vision therapy, and refractive surgery. An exception applies when safety eyewear is prescribed following a documented workplace eye injury, in which case a one-time one hundred-dollar allowance is paid.

§4.3 Out-of-Network Benefits
Out-of-network claims are reimbursed at eighty percent of the in-network allowance up to the same dollar maximums. Reimbursement never exceeds the amount actually paid by the member.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Medically necessary contact lenses and any service expected to exceed three hundred dollars require prior approval. Requests must be submitted at least ten business days before the service date. Approval is valid for sixty days.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be filed within ninety days of the service date. Claims filed after ninety days but within one hundred eighty days are reduced by twenty-five percent. Claims filed after one hundred eighty days are denied.

§6.1 Cost Sharing
Enrollees pay the copays listed in §3.3 at the point of service. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is three hundred fifty dollars per enrollee, after which covered services are paid at one hundred percent for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§6.2 Plan Maximums
Total plan payments are capped at five hundred dollars per enrollee per Plan Year. Amounts exceeding the cap are member responsibility. Unused benefit amounts do not roll over.

§7.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within thirty days of receipt. Members receive an explanation of benefits showing amounts paid and member responsibility. Incomplete claims suspend the processing clock until documentation arrives.

§7.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within one hundred eighty days by submitting a written request to the plan administrator. First-level appeals are decided within thirty days. A second-level appeal may be filed within sixty days of a first-level denial and is decided by an independent reviewer within forty-five days.

§7.3 Provider Disputes
Disputes between providers and the plan are resolved through the administrator's reconciliation process and do not affect member cost sharing. Members are held harmless for approved amounts.

§8.1 Coordination of Benefits
When another plan is primary, this plan pays the lesser of its allowance or the unpaid balance. Duplicate payments for the same service are prohibited and subject to recovery under §8.2.

§8.2 Recovery of Overpayments
The plan recovers overpayments by offsetting future payments or invoicing the member within twelve months of discovery. Members may request a hardship schedule of up to six monthly installments.

§9.1 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month of ineligibility. Services rendered before termination but billed after it remain payable if filed within the deadlines in §5.2. Frames ordered before termination but delivered after it are not covered.

§9.2 Continuation
A member losing eligibility may continue coverage for up to eighteen months by paying the full monthly premium of twenty-two dollars plus a two percent administrative charge. Election must occur within forty-five days of the loss of eligibility.

§10.1 Administration
The plan administrator maintains enrollment records, processes claims under §7.1, and issues an annual benefit summary each December. The administrator may amend this plan with thirty days written notice, and amendments apply prospectively only.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Grove Flex Advantage Small-Business Health Plan

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this demonstration document, the Plan refers to the Meridian Grove Flex Advantage Small-Business Health Plan. A Covered Person means an Enrolled Employee or an enrolled Dependent. The Calendar Year means January 1 through December 31 of each year.

§1.2 Eligibility
Enrolled Employees must work at least 30 hours per week for a participating employer. New employees become eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous employment. Dependents include a legal spouse and children under age 26.

§1.3 Enrollment Windows
Employees must enroll within 31 days of first becoming eligible. Outside of initial enrollment, changes are permitted only during the annual open period from November 1 to December 15, or within 31 days of a qualifying life event such as marriage or loss of other coverage.

§2.1 Preventive Care Benefits
The Plan pays 100 percent of eligible preventive services, including annual physical examinations, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings, with no deductible applied. Well-child visits are covered through age 18 at up to six visits per Calendar Year. Routine mammograms and colonoscopies are covered once every 12 months.

§2.2 Hospital and Surgical Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, subject to a limit of 60 days per Calendar Year. Outpatient surgery is covered at 80 percent after a separate $500 facility copayment. As described in §3.1, non-emergency inpatient admission requires prior approval.

§2.3 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs carry a $15 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $40 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $75 copayment per 30-day supply. A 90-day supply is available through the mail-order channel at 2.5 times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval and are limited to $10,000 per Calendar Year.

§2.4 Mental Health and Substance Use Benefits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 100 percent for the first 20 visits per Calendar Year, then at 70 percent. Inpatient substance use treatment is limited to 30 days per Calendar Year. Emergency stabilization services are covered without prior approval, as noted in §3.2.

§3.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval must be obtained before scheduled inpatient admissions, imaging studies over $1,500, and specialty drug therapy. The requesting provider must submit documentation at least 10 business days before the service. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment by 50 percent, except where the Covered Person was physically unable to provide notice.

§3.2 Emergency Care
Emergency services are covered at the in-network level regardless of facility, subject to a $250 emergency room copayment that is waived if the visit results in a direct admission. The Covered Person or a representative must notify the Plan Administrator within 48 hours of any emergency admission. Follow-up care after stabilization is subject to §3.1.

§3.3 Notification Deadlines
Claims for out-of-network services must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Notice of an intended appeal must be filed within 180 days of the denial. Failure to meet these deadlines voids the claim or appeal unless the delay was due to circumstances beyond the Covered Person's reasonable control.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
The annual deductible is $1,500 per Covered Person and $3,000 per family. The out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 per Covered Person and $12,000 per family, after which the Plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the remainder of the Calendar Year. Copayments described in §2.3 do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.2 Annual Limits
Physical therapy is limited to 30 visits per Calendar Year, chiropractic care to 20 visits, and speech therapy to 40 sessions. Durable medical equipment is covered up to $2,500 per Calendar Year. Any limits stated in §2 supersede more general limits in this clause.

§4.3 Exclusions
The Plan excludes cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, weight-loss programs, and services rendered by a household member. Exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following trauma or mastectomy, or to treatments prescribed for a documented medical condition that are generally accepted by the relevant professional community.

§4.4 Preexisting Conditions
No preexisting condition exclusion applies to Covered Persons who have maintained continuous creditable coverage. If there is a break in coverage of more than 63 days, conditions diagnosed or treated in the prior 12 months may be excluded for up to 6 months of enrollment.

§5.1 Claims Administration
In-network providers submit claims directly to the Plan. Covered Persons using out-of-network providers must submit an itemized claim form within the deadline stated in §3.3. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 calendar days of receipt.

§5.2 Denials and Appeals
A denial notice will state the reason, the specific provision relied upon, and the appeal procedure. A first-level appeal is reviewed by a reviewer not involved in the original decision within 45 calendar days. A second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided within 60 calendar days.

§5.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment ends, unless the employer elects continuation coverage. A Covered Person may continue coverage for up to 18 months following termination of employment at 102 percent of the full monthly premium. Continuation coverage ends early if premiums are more than 30 days delinquent.

§5.4 Plan Administration
The Plan Administrator maintains enrollment records, issues identification cards within 15 days of enrollment, and publishes an annual summary of benefits each January. The Administrator may amend this document upon 60 days written notice to participating employers. This document is synthetic and is intended solely for software demonstration purposes.

SYNTHETIC
Aurora Shield Critical Illness Plan (Demo Document)

§1.1 Definitions
A Covered Illness means cancer, heart attack, stroke, kidney failure, or major organ transplant as further described in §1.2. A Qualifying Diagnosis means a diagnosis made by a licensed physician and confirmed by laboratory or imaging evidence. The Benefit Year begins on the first day of the month following acceptance of the application.

§1.2 Illness Criteria
A heart attack must show elevation of cardiac enzymes of at least twice the normal laboratory upper limit. Stroke means a cerebrovascular event producing neurological deficit persisting at least 30 days. Kidney failure means permanent dependence on dialysis or a transplant.

§1.3 Eligibility
Applicants must be at least 18 years old and reside in a jurisdiction where the plan is administered. Dependent coverage extends to a spouse and children under age 19, or under age 26 if enrolled full-time in school. Coverage may not be issued to any person currently under treatment for a Covered Illness.

§2.1 Waiting Period
No benefit is payable for an illness diagnosed during the first 90 days following the Effective Date. An illness diagnosed between day 91 and day 180 pays 50 percent of the scheduled benefit. After day 180, the full benefit described in §3.1 applies.

§2.2 Eligibility Review
Eligibility is reconfirmed annually on the anniversary of the Effective Date. If employment or residency status changes, the Member must notify the Administrator within 30 days. Failure to notify may result in retroactive premium adjustment as described in §5.3.

§3.1 Scheduled Benefits
The plan pays a lump sum of 25,000 dollars per Covered Illness, payable once per illness per lifetime. A second and unrelated Covered Illness pays 15,000 dollars if diagnosed at least 180 days after the first. No benefit is payable for recurrence of the same illness within 180 days.

§3.2 Supplementary Benefits
A Hospital Confinement Benefit of 200 dollars per day is payable for up to 30 days per Benefit Year for treatment of a condition described in §1.2. A Recovery Benefit of 1,000 dollars is payable once per lifetime after the lump sum in §3.1 has been paid. Supplementary benefits are not payable during the waiting period in §2.1.

§3.3 Benefit Coordination
Benefits are reduced by amounts actually received under any other critical illness policy for the same diagnosis. If the reduction exceeds 50 percent of the scheduled benefit, only the unreduced amount is payable. Coordination does not apply to the Hospital Confinement Benefit.

§4.1 Exclusions
No benefit is payable for illnesses caused by self-inflicted injury, war, or active participation in a riot. Illnesses arising from illegal drug use are excluded, except where the drug was prescribed by a physician and taken as directed. Non-melanoma skin cancer is excluded unless it invades beyond the dermis.

§4.2 Prior Approval
Elective organ transplant procedures require prior approval from the Administrator at least 14 days before hospital admission. Emergency transplants are exempt from prior approval, but notice must be given within 72 hours of admission. Approval under this section does not guarantee payment, which remains subject to §4.1.

§4.3 Notice Deadlines
The Member must give written notice of a Qualifying Diagnosis within 60 days of the diagnosis date. Proof of loss must be submitted within 90 days of notice, or as soon as reasonably possible. Late proof may be accepted where the delay was outside the Member's control.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
Members pay a monthly premium of 45 dollars for individual coverage and 80 dollars for family coverage. A claims administration fee of 25 dollars is deducted from each lump sum payment under §3.1. No deductible or coinsurance applies to supplementary benefits under §3.2.

§5.2 Premium Grace Period
Premiums are due on the first day of each month with a 31-day grace period. Coverage remains in force during the grace period. If premiums remain unpaid after the grace period, coverage terminates and any pending claim under §3.1 is denied.

§5.3 Reinstatement
Coverage terminated under §5.2 may be reinstated within 90 days by paying all arrears plus a 50 dollar reinstatement fee. Reinstated coverage is subject to a new 60-day waiting period for any illness first diagnosed after termination. Benefits for illnesses diagnosed before termination are unaffected.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted on the Administrator's standard claim form with physician certification of the diagnosis. The Administrator will acknowledge receipt within 10 business days. A decision is issued within 30 days of receiving complete proof of loss.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal is reviewed by a reviewer independent of the original decision within 45 days. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first appeal decision.

§6.3 Overpayments
If a benefit is paid in excess of the amount payable under §3.1 or §3.2, the Administrator may recover the excess. Recovery may be made by offset against future benefits or by refund within 12 months. Amounts recovered under this section are not subject to the fee described in §5.1.

§6.4 Administration and Termination
The Administrator may amend premiums upon 60 days written notice to Members. The plan terminates entirely if fewer than 100 Members remain enrolled at any annual review. Upon termination, claims for illnesses diagnosed before the termination date remain payable under §3.1.

SYNTHETIC
Plan name: DemoCare Flex 90 Sample Benefit Plan (Fictional Illustration Only)

§1.1 Definitions
This plan is a fictional short-term medical product created solely for software demonstration purposes. The term "Covered Person" means a demo enrollee whose enrollment record exists only within the demonstration environment. The term "Benefit Period" means the ninety-day coverage window selected at enrollment. The term "Allowable Charge" means the fictional provider charge recorded in the demo claim file.

§1.2 Eligibility
Demo enrollees must be simulated residents of a fictional state and between the ages of eighteen and sixty-four as recorded in the demo profile. Enrollment requires completion of a synthetic application and selection of a Benefit Period of thirty, sixty, or ninety days. A waiting period of five days applies to illness benefits, except that accident benefits are covered from day one. Dependents under age twenty-six may be added to a demo profile at any time during the Benefit Period.

§2.1 Covered Benefits
The plan pays sixty percent of Allowable Charges for inpatient hospital stays, up to a limit of thirty days per Benefit Period. Outpatient physician visits are reimbursed at fifty dollars per visit, limited to eight visits per Benefit Period. Emergency room services are paid at one hundred percent of Allowable Charges, subject to a two-hundred-dollar demo copayment per visit. Prescription drugs are covered at twenty dollars per fill, with a maximum of six fills per Benefit Period.

§2.2 Preventive Services
Two preventive wellness visits per Benefit Period are paid at one hundred dollars each. Preventive visits are not subject to the deductible described in §3.1. Preventive services are not subject to the waiting period described in §1.2.

§3.1 Cost Sharing
A deductible of one thousand five hundred dollars per Covered Person applies to all benefits except preventive services and emergency room care. After the deductible, the plan pays the percentages stated in §2.1. The maximum out-of-pocket amount for a demo enrollee is four thousand dollars per Benefit Period. Cost sharing amounts are reset to zero at the start of each new Benefit Period.

§3.2 Limits
Aggregate benefits are capped at one hundred thousand dollars per Covered Person per Benefit Period. The maximum inpatient stay payable is thirty days, as described in §2.1. No benefits are payable after the ninetieth day of the Benefit Period, regardless of when treatment began.

§4.1 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for pre-existing conditions, meaning any condition for which a demo enrollee received advice or treatment during the twenty-four months before the effective date. Cosmetic procedures, weight-loss treatment, and routine dental care are excluded. The pre-existing condition exclusion does not apply to accidental injuries occurring after the effective date. Benefits for pregnancy-related care are excluded except for complications of pregnancy, which are covered as described in §2.1.

§4.2 Additional Exclusions
No benefits are payable for self-inflicted injuries, war-related events, or treatment received outside the fictional service area. Experimental treatments not listed in the demo fee schedule are excluded. Habilitative therapy is covered only when authorized under §5.1.

§5.1 Prior Approval Rules
Prior approval is required for all inpatient admissions, imaging services over five hundred dollars, and habilitative therapy. Requests for prior approval must be submitted at least three days before scheduled services, except in emergencies where notice is permitted within two days after the event. If prior approval is not obtained, benefits are reduced by fifty percent.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service. Written notice of intent to appeal must be received within sixty days of the date on the demo claim decision. Failure to meet the deadlines in this clause or §5.1 may result in denial of benefits.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed in the order received within the demonstration environment, with decisions issued within fifteen business days of a complete synthetic claim file. A claim is considered complete when it includes the fictional provider charge, the date of service, and the demo diagnosis code. Payment is recorded against the cost-sharing ledger described in §3.1.

§6.2 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denied claim by submitting a written statement through the demo interface within the deadline stated in §5.2. Appeals are reviewed by a simulated review panel within thirty days. The panel may uphold, reverse, or modify the original decision, and the outcome is recorded in the demo claim history.

§6.3 Administration and Termination
The plan administrator maintains the synthetic enrollment records and processes changes to Benefit Periods. A demo enrollee may terminate coverage at any time by submitting a termination request, with no refund of the fictional premium. The administrator may terminate the entire demonstration plan at any time, and all records are then cleared from the demo environment. Nothing in this plan creates real coverage or real obligations of any kind.

SYNTHETIC
Zephyra Silver Compass Health Plan 47B

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "covered service" to mean a health care item or service that is medically necessary and listed in §3.1 through §3.6. The term "network provider" means a provider who has signed a participation agreement with the plan's administrator as of the date of service. The term "plan year" begins on the first day of the month following enrollment approval and lasts twelve consecutive months.

§1.2 Eligibility
Enrollment is open to residents of the demo region who are at least eighteen years old and not enrolled in any other individual market plan. A dependent may be added within thirty days of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, or adoption. Coverage for a newly enrolled member begins at 12:01 a.m. on the first day of the month after the first premium payment is received.

§1.3 Waiting Periods
Maternity benefits under §3.3 are subject to a ten-month waiting period from the effective date, except that this waiting period is waived for members transferring from another individual market plan without a gap of more than fourteen days. Dental coverage under §3.5 has a six-month waiting period. No waiting period applies to emergency services or to preventive care described in §3.1.

§2.1 Cost Sharing
The member pays a $45 copayment for primary care visits and a $75 copayment for specialist visits under §3.2. The annual deductible is $3,200 per member and $6,400 per family, after which the plan pays 70 percent of allowed charges for most covered services. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $7,900 per member; once reached, the plan pays 100 percent of allowed charges for the remainder of the plan year, excluding premiums.

§2.2 Premiums and Termination
The base monthly premium is $512 for a single adult and $1,140 for a family of two or more. Premiums are due by the fifth day of each month, and a grace period of thirty days applies before termination. If coverage is terminated for nonpayment, the member may reinstate within sixty days by paying all past-due premiums plus a $25 reinstatement fee.

§2.3 Prior Approval
Certain services require prior approval, including inpatient admissions, imaging beyond plain films, and specialty drugs listed in §3.4. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least ten business days before a scheduled service or within five business days after an emergency admission. Approval is valid for sixty days from the date of issuance.

§2.4 Notice Deadlines
Members must notify the plan of a hospital admission within forty-eight hours or the claim will be reduced by 20 percent, except where the member was incapacitated. Written notice of intent to appeal under §5.2 must be postmarked within 180 days of the denial notice. Change-of-address notices must be received before the end of the month in which the change occurs.

§3.1 Preventive Care
The plan covers in-network preventive services at 100 percent with no deductible, including annual physical examinations, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings. One routine physical is allowed per member per plan year. Services performed during a preventive visit that are not preventive, such as treatment of a new condition, are subject to the cost sharing in §2.1.

§3.2 Physician and Outpatient Services
Covered office visits include evaluation and management, minor procedures, and telehealth, with telehealth copayments set at $25. Physical therapy is limited to thirty visits per plan year, and occupational therapy to twenty visits, with additional visits allowed if prior approval under §2.3 is granted. Chiropractic care is limited to twelve visits per plan year with a $30 copayment.

§3.3 Inpatient and Maternity
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 70 percent after the deductible, limited to sixty days per plan year except for maternity stays, which are not counted toward this limit. Maternity coverage includes prenatal visits, delivery, and one inpatient postpartum stay of up to four days for vaginal delivery and six days for cesarean delivery. Newborns are covered automatically for the first thirty-one days under the parent's policy.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
The plan covers a three-tier formulary: $15 generic, $45 preferred brand, and $90 non-preferred brand copayments for a thirty-day supply. Specialty drugs require prior approval under §2.3 and carry a 20 percent coinsurance with a $250 monthly cap per drug. A ninety-day supply may be obtained through the maintenance program for two and one-half times the thirty-day copayment.

§3.5 Dental and Vision
Pediatric dental is covered with a $1,300 annual maximum per child. Adult dental is limited to two cleanings per year and one set of bitewing films, with major restorative work covered at 50 percent after the six-month waiting period in §1.3. Vision covers one eye examination and one pair of standard lenses with frames every plan year, with a $150 allowance for contact lenses in lieu of glasses.

§3.6 Emergency and Urgent Care
Emergency room services are covered at in-network cost sharing regardless of provider network status, subject to a $250 copayment that is waived if the member is admitted as an inpatient. Urgent care visits carry a $50 copayment. Follow-up care after an emergency discharge should be obtained from a network provider as described in §3.2.

§4.1 Limits and Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments not approved by the plan's medical review process, or services rendered by providers outside the network except as provided in §3.6. Weight-loss surgery is covered only when the member has a documented body mass index over 40 for at least twelve months and completes a supervised program of at least six months. Hearing aids are excluded, except one device per ear every thirty-six months for members under age nineteen.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following trauma or a covered mastectomy is not considered cosmetic and is covered under §3.3 cost sharing. Experimental treatments may be approved on an exception basis when the treating provider certifies that no standard therapy is appropriate and prior approval under §2.3 is obtained. Out-of-network services are covered at in-network levels when no network provider capable of rendering the service is available within fifty miles.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be filed within twelve months of the date of service, and network providers generally file on the member's behalf. The plan will issue an explanation of benefits within thirty days of receiving a complete claim. Members may submit claims for out-of-network emergency services directly, using the standard claim format, and will be reimbursed at the in-network rate described in §3.6.

§5.2 Appeals and Grievances
A member may appeal a denial in two stages: an internal review decided within thirty days, and an external review by an independent entity decided within sixty days. Urgent care denials receive an expedited internal decision within seventy-two hours as required by §2.4 notice rules. If the external review overturns the denial, the plan will pay the claim within ten business days and may not re-den it on the same grounds.

§5.3 Administration and Records
The plan administrator maintains enrollment records and issues identification credentials within fourteen days of the effective date. Members must report any duplicate coverage within thirty days, and benefits will be coordinated so that total payments do not exceed the allowed charge. The administrator may amend this policy at renewal with sixty days written notice, except that changes to §2.1 cost sharing take effect only at the start of a plan year.
