SYNTHETIC
SampleDemo Plan: the "MeridianCare Critical Illness Prototype Policy"

§1.1 Purpose and Scope
This policy is a fictional document created solely for software demonstration purposes. It describes a critical illness insurance product that pays a lump-sum benefit upon diagnosis of a covered condition. Nothing in this document constitutes a real offer of insurance.

§1.2 Definitions
"Covered Condition" means cancer, heart attack, stroke, or kidney failure as further described in §2.1. "Diagnosis Date" means the date a licensed physician confirms the condition in writing. "Waiting Period" means the continuous period of active coverage that must elapse before benefits are payable, as set out in §3.2.

§1.3 Eligibility
An insured must be at least 18 years old and reside in a fictional jurisdiction of issue. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following acceptance of the application. Persons already diagnosed with a Covered Condition during the two years before the application date are not eligible.

§2.1 Covered Conditions
Cancer means a malignant tumor confirmed by histological evidence, excluding non-invasive stages. Heart attack means death of heart muscle evidenced by elevated biomarkers and electrocardiogram changes. Stroke means a cerebrovascular event producing neurological deficit lasting more than 30 days. Kidney failure means permanent end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation.

§2.2 Benefit Amount
The base benefit is 50,000 dollars per insured person per lifetime. An optional child rider adds 10,000 dollars per covered child, limited to three children. The benefit is paid once per lifetime and is not reduced by other insurance.

§2.3 Cost Sharing
The insurer pays 90 percent of the approved benefit amount and the insured bears the remaining 10 percent as a co-payment, except that no co-payment exceeds 2,500 dollars. Preventive screening benefits described in §4.1 are paid at 100 percent with no co-payment.

§3.1 Prior Approval
Non-emergency transplant procedures listed under §2.1 require prior approval submitted at least 10 business days before the scheduled procedure. Emergency admissions are exempt from prior approval, but notice must follow under §3.3.

§3.2 Waiting Period
Benefits are payable only after a Waiting Period of 90 days of continuous coverage has elapsed. Conditions first diagnosed during the Waiting Period are excluded, except that accidental strokes occurring after day 30 are covered if documented by imaging.

§3.3 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of a claim must be provided within 30 days of the Diagnosis Date. Failure to provide timely notice relieves the insurer of liability only if the insurer demonstrates prejudice from the delay. Notices sent to the address of record are deemed received five business days after mailing.

§3.4 Documentation
A claim must include the physician's written confirmation, diagnostic test results, and a completed claim form. The insurer may request one additional independent medical examination, scheduled within 30 days and at the insurer's expense.

§4.1 Preventive Screening Benefit
The policy pays up to 300 dollars per calendar year for covered screening examinations, subject to the co-payment rules in §2.3. Unused amounts do not carry forward. Screening benefits do not reduce the lifetime benefit in §2.2.

§4.2 Exclusions
No benefit is payable for conditions caused by war, self-inflicted injury, or participation in professional athletics, except that strokes caused by an athletic aneurysm are covered. Conditions diagnosed within the Waiting Period are excluded as described in §3.2.

§4.3 Limits
The aggregate lifetime benefit under this policy is 60,000 dollars including any rider amounts. Benefits cease entirely at age 75. Only one Covered Condition per insured is payable regardless of the number of diagnoses.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt of complete documentation under §3.4. Incomplete claims receive a written deficiency notice within 10 business days, and the claimant has 60 days to cure the deficiency. Payment is made by a single lump-sum transfer.

§5.2 Appeals
A denial may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. Appeals are reviewed by a reviewer independent of the original adjudication, and a decision is issued within 45 days. A second-level appeal may be requested once, with a decision within 60 days.

§5.3 Administration and Records
The insurer maintains claim records for seven years after final payment. Policy documents are provided in the jurisdiction's official languages. All communications under this policy use the fictional contact channels maintained for this demonstration environment.

§5.4 Termination and Portability
Coverage terminates upon non-payment of premium after a 31-day grace period. Terminated insureds may reinstate within 12 months by paying all overdue premiums, subject to a new 60-day Waiting Period under §3.2.

SYNTHETIC
Plan: Medigap Demo Plan Z-Orbit

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this synthetic plan, "Plan" means the fictional Medigap Demo Plan Z-Orbit created solely for software demonstration. "Eligible Expense" means a charge for a covered service that is reasonable and customary within the demo region. "Benefit Year" means each twelve-month period beginning on the first day of the month in which the fictional effective date occurs.

§1.2 Administrator
The Administrator is a fictional entity responsible for processing claims and handling appeals under this Plan. The Administrator operates only within the demonstration environment and has no real-world authority. All references to the Administrator shall be interpreted as references to demo data and demo workflows.

§2.1 Eligibility
An individual is eligible if they are a fictional enrollee who has reached simulated age 65 or is recorded as eligible for demo disability benefits. Enrollment must be requested within six months of the simulated Part B enrollment date, or during the demo open enrollment window. A late enrollment request is subject to a 20 percent surcharge on the monthly premium for each year of delay, capped at 60 percent.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees with fewer than six months of simulated prior credible coverage are subject to a waiting period of up to six months for pre-existing conditions. The waiting period is waived entirely if the enrollee had continuous demo coverage for 90 days or more immediately before the effective date. During the waiting period, non-pre-existing conditions are covered without restriction.

§3.1 Hospital Benefit
The Plan pays the full demo daily coinsurance amount for hospital stays from day 61 through day 90 of a simulated benefit period. For each of the 60 demo lifetime reserve days, the Plan pays 50 percent of the recorded reserve-day charge. After all reserve days are exhausted, the Plan pays 100 percent of eligible hospital expenses for 365 additional days per benefit period.

§3.2 Skilled Nursing Benefit
The Plan pays the daily coinsurance for skilled nursing facility care from day 21 through day 100 of a simulated spell of illness, up to 100 days per benefit period. No benefit is payable for days 1 through 20, which are covered under the base demo coverage. Care beyond day 100 is excluded, except when the Administrator grants an extension for documented rehabilitation need, as described in §4.1.

§3.3 Physician and Outpatient Benefit
The Plan pays 20 percent of eligible physician charges after the base demo coverage pays its share, subject to an annual outpatient stop-loss of 1,500 demo dollars. The Plan also pays the first three pints of simulated blood per benefit period unless the blood is replaced. Annual wellness visits are covered at 100 percent with no limit on the number of visits.

§3.4 Foreign Travel Benefit
The Plan pays 80 percent of eligible emergency care charges incurred during simulated travel outside the demo country, after a 250 demo dollar deductible per benefit year. The lifetime maximum for this benefit is 50,000 demo dollars. Charges arising from travel undertaken against demo medical advice are excluded, except when the travel is for an emergency evacuation arranged before departure.

§4.1 Prior Approval and Extensions
Certain services, including skilled nursing extensions and durable equipment costing more than 2,000 demo dollars, require prior approval from the Administrator. Requests must be submitted at least five business days before the service, or within two business days in emergencies. Approval may be granted for up to 30 additional days of skilled nursing care when progress is documented, as described in §3.2.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be filed within 12 months of the date of service, and notices of appeal must be filed within 60 days of a denial. Enrollees must report any change in simulated coverage status within 30 days. Failure to meet a deadline may be excused upon a showing of good cause, such as a documented demo system outage.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
The monthly premium is 165 demo dollars for the standard tier and 210 demo dollars for the enhanced tier. There is no annual deductible under this Plan, except as stated in §3.4. Cost-sharing amounts are fixed for the first benefit year and may be adjusted annually by no more than 8 percent upon 90 days notice.

§5.2 Excess Charges
The Plan pays 100 percent of simulated excess charges above the demo-approved amount for physician services under the enhanced tier. Under the standard tier, excess charges are payable up to a cap of 15 percent above the approved amount. Excess charges for equipment and supplies are excluded under both tiers.

§6.1 Limits and Exclusions
The Plan does not cover dental care, vision refractions, hearing aids, or long-term custodial care, except that dental care related to a covered accident is payable up to 1,000 demo dollars per benefit year. Cosmetic procedures are excluded unless needed to repair damage from a covered injury. Experimental treatments are excluded unless the Administrator confirms they are approved under the demo coverage rules.

§6.2 Coordination of Benefits
If an enrollee has other simulated coverage, this Plan pays only the amounts not payable by the other coverage. The Plan is always secondary to the base demo coverage and to liability coverage for accident-related care. Overpayments discovered within 24 months must be refunded to the Administrator within 60 days of notice.

§7.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within 30 days of receipt of a complete submission in the demo system. The Administrator issues an explanation of benefits for every processed claim, showing paid amounts, denials, and the appeal window. Incomplete claims are returned once with instructions and may be resubmitted without penalty.

§7.2 Appeals
A denial may be appealed in three levels: reconsideration by the Administrator, review by the fictional demo review board, and a final simulated hearing. Each level must be completed within 30 days, and the enrollee may submit written statements at any level. If the Administrator fails to decide within the deadline, the appeal advances automatically to the next level, as described in §7.1.

§7.3 Termination and Administration
The Plan terminates automatically at the end of the software demonstration session or upon deletion of the demo dataset. No real premiums are collected, no real benefits are payable, and no real personal data is used at any point. Any resemblance to an actual insurance product is entirely coincidental.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Flex Small-Business Health Plan (Demo Document)

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this demonstration document, "Enrolled Employee" means a worker of a participating fictional employer who has completed the synthetic enrollment process. "Covered Service" means a medically necessary service rendered by a licensed provider, as described in §2.2. All names, amounts, and procedures in this document are invented for software demonstration only.

§1.2 Plan Year
The Plan Year begins on the first day of the demo calendar and ends twelve months later. Deductibles and accumulators reset on that date. A Participant who joins mid-year receives prorated limits as described in §4.3.

§2.1 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible for coverage. Enrollment must occur within 31 days of the hire date or during the annual synthetic open period. Dependents eligible for coverage include a spouse and children under age 26.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees are subject to a 60-day waiting period before benefits begin, except that coverage for accidental injury begins on day one. Preventive care described in §3.1 is also exempt from the waiting period.

§3.1 Preventive Benefits
The Plan pays 100 percent of the allowed amount for annual physical examinations, routine immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings, with no cost sharing. One wellness visit per Enrolled Employee per Plan Year is covered, plus two dental cleanings per dependent under age 19.

§3.2 Hospital and Surgical Benefits
Inpatient hospital care is covered at 80 percent of the allowed amount after the deductible, with a limit of 45 days per Plan Year. Outpatient surgery is covered at 80 percent with no day limit. An additional 10 percent coinsurance applies to non-emergency admissions without prior approval, as described in §4.1.

§3.3 Prescription Benefits
Generic drugs are covered at a 10 dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs at a 40 dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs at 50 percent coinsurance. A 90-day supply of maintenance medication is available at twice the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval under §4.1 and are limited to a 5,000 dollar annual maximum.

§3.4 Mental Health and Therapy
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at a 25 dollar copayment for the first 20 visits per Plan Year and 50 percent coinsurance thereafter. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered for up to 30 days per Plan Year at the hospital benefit level described in §3.2.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, imaging exceeding 1,500 dollars in allowed amount, and all specialty drugs. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before the scheduled service, except in emergencies where notice is required within 48 hours. Denials of prior approval may be appealed under §5.2.

§4.2 Exclusions
The Plan does not cover cosmetic procedures, experimental treatments, services rendered by out-of-network providers except emergencies, or injuries sustained during paid professional athletics. Excluded services do not include reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or mastectomy, which are covered as described in §3.2.

§4.3 Cost Sharing Limits
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is 6,500 dollars per Enrolled Employee and 13,000 dollars per family. Once the maximum is reached, the Plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copayments for prescription drugs under §3.3 do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.4 Notice Deadlines
Claims for out-of-network services must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Notice of a dependent status change must be provided within 31 days of the event. Late claims are honored only if the Participant shows the delay was beyond reasonable control.

§5.1 Claims Administration
The fictional administrator processes clean claims within 30 days of receipt and issues an explanation of benefits to the Participant. Claims missing information are pended for up to 45 days while the administrator requests the missing items. Electronic submission is the default method in this demo environment.

§5.2 Appeals
A Participant may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial by submitting a written request with supporting documentation. The administrator issues a first-level decision within 30 days, and a second-level review by an independent reviewer is available within 60 days of the first decision. Exhaustion of both appeal levels is a condition of any further simulated review.

§5.3 Plan Administration
The Plan is governed by the participating employer's benefits committee, which may amend terms upon 30 days written notice to Participants. This document is a synthetic artifact and confers no actual coverage, rights, or obligations. Any resemblance to a real plan, living or simulated, is coincidental.

SYNTHETIC
NovaCare Select HMO — Demonstration Plan 2025

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January 1. "Network Provider" means a physician, facility, or pharmacy that has executed a participation agreement with the plan sponsor. "Medically Necessary Care" means services that a Network Provider certifies as reasonable and required to treat a covered condition.

§1.2 Eligibility
Enrollment is open to employees of participating demo employers who work at least 30 hours per week. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following a 45-day waiting period from the date of hire. Dependents may be added within 31 days of a qualifying life event.

§1.3 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment terminates. A member may continue coverage for up to 18 months by paying the full monthly premium of 612 dollars plus a 2 percent administrative charge.

§2.1 Physician Services
Primary care visits are covered at 100 percent after a 25 dollar copayment. Specialist visits require a 50 dollar copayment and a referral from the primary care physician, as described in §4.2. Telehealth visits carry a 15 dollar copayment with no referral requirement.

§2.2 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospitalization is covered at 80 percent after the annual deductible. The deductible is 1,500 dollars per member and 3,000 dollars per family per Plan Year. Semi-private room and board is covered for up to 60 days per Plan Year, with additional days approved only under §4.1.

§2.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a 10 dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs a 35 dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a 60 dollar copayment. A 90-day supply is available through the network mail-order pharmacy for twice the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior authorization under §4.1.

§2.4 Preventive Care
Annual physical examinations, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings are covered at 100 percent with no cost sharing. One routine vision examination per Plan Year is included, with lenses covered up to 150 dollars. Mammography and colorectal screening follow the preventive schedule published by the plan sponsor each January.

§3.1 Emergency Services
Emergency care is covered at the in-network level regardless of provider network status. A 150 dollar emergency room copayment applies, waived if the member is admitted as an inpatient within 24 hours. Members must notify the plan within 48 hours of any emergency admission, as required by §4.3.

§3.2 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient behavioral health visits are covered at 100 percent after a 30 dollar copayment, limited to 30 visits per Plan Year. Inpatient substance use treatment is covered for up to 28 days per Plan Year at the inpatient level under §2.2. Intensive outpatient programs require prior authorization as described in §4.1.

§3.3 Exclusions
Cosmetic surgery, weight-loss supplements, and experimental treatments are excluded. Dental care is excluded except for accidental injury to sound natural teeth, which is covered at the hospital benefit level under §2.2. Fertility services are excluded except diagnostic testing, which is covered at the specialist level under §2.1.

§3.4 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is 6,500 dollars per member and 13,000 dollars per family. Copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance all count toward the maximum. Once the maximum is reached, covered services are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the Plan Year, excluding services denied under §3.3.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, advanced imaging, physical therapy beyond 12 visits, and all specialty drugs. Requests are decided within 5 business days, or 72 hours for urgent requests. A denied request may be appealed under §5.2.

§4.2 Referral Rules
A referral from the primary care physician is required for all specialist care except emergency services under §3.1 and annual women's health examinations. Referrals are valid for 90 days and up to 3 visits. Obstetricians and dermatologists may be seen once per Plan Year without a referral.

§4.3 Notice Deadlines
Members must notify the plan within 48 hours of emergency admission, 30 days before planned non-emergency inpatient care, and 60 days of a change in dependent status. Failure to provide timely notice may reduce benefits by 25 percent, except where notice was impossible due to incapacity.

§5.1 Claims
Network Providers submit claims directly, and payment is made within 30 days of receipt of a clean claim. Members using out-of-network emergency providers may submit claims within 180 days of service. Claims must include the date of service, diagnosis, and itemized charges.

§5.2 Appeals
A member may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial notice. The plan issues a written decision within 30 days for standard appeals and 72 hours for expedited appeals. A second-level review by an independent clinician may be requested within 60 days of the first denial, and the outcome of that review is final.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: NovaShield Short-Term Medical Plan 90X (Demo Sample)

§1.1 Definitions
Covered Person means an individual who has enrolled and whose premium payments are current. Medically Necessary means a service that a licensed provider determines is required to treat an illness or injury covered under this plan. Eligible Expense means the allowed amount shown in the Schedule of Benefits.

§1.2 Plan Purpose
This plan provides temporary coverage for unexpected illness and injury. It is not designed to cover preventive care, routine checkups, or pre-existing conditions. This document is a fictional sample created for a software demonstration only.

§2.1 Eligibility
Applicants must be between 18 and 64 years of age at the time of application. Coverage may be issued for initial terms of 30, 60, or 90 days. Only one covered person per application is permitted under this demo plan.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the day after the application is approved, subject to a five-day waiting period for illness benefits. Injury benefits have no waiting period. No benefits are payable for any condition arising before the effective date.

§2.3 Pre-Existing Conditions
A pre-existing condition is any condition for which advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was sought during the 24 months before the effective date. Expenses related to pre-existing conditions are excluded for the entire term. This exclusion does not apply to accidental injuries, which are always covered regardless of prior history.

§3.1 Hospital Benefits
The plan pays 80 percent of eligible hospital room and board expenses up to 1,200 dollars per day, for a maximum of 30 days per term. Intensive care is covered up to 2,500 dollars per day for a maximum of 10 days. All hospital stays require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§3.2 Physician and Urgent Care Benefits
Covered visits to a physician are paid at 80 percent after the deductible, with a limit of 12 visits per term. Urgent care visits are covered at 90 percent with no visit limit. Emergency room visits are covered as described in §3.3.

§3.3 Emergency Care
Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, with a 250 dollar copayment waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient. Emergency care does not require prior approval. Notification must still be given within the deadlines stated in §5.2.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Prescription drugs are covered at 100 percent after a 15 dollar copayment for generic drugs and a 40 dollar copayment for brand-name drugs. The plan pays a maximum of 1,000 dollars for prescriptions per term. Drugs administered during a hospital stay are paid under §3.1 instead.

§4.1 Deductibles and Coinsurance
The deductible is 500 dollars per covered person per term. The deductible does not apply to urgent care visits or prescription copayments. After the deductible, coinsurance percentages in §3.1 through §3.4 apply.

§4.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The out-of-pocket maximum is 5,000 dollars per covered person per term. Once this amount is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of eligible expenses for the remainder of the term. Copayments do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.3 General Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, dental care, vision care, maternity care, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, and experimental procedures. Expenses arising from war, self-inflicted injury, or participation in professional athletics are also excluded. An exception applies to reconstructive surgery following a covered accidental injury.

§4.4 Term and Renewal Limits
Coverage under this plan may not exceed 90 days in any 12-month period. The plan may be renewed once for an additional term not exceeding 90 days. A renewed term is treated as a new term for deductible and limit purposes.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for all hospital admissions, imaging services exceeding 500 dollars, and any single procedure exceeding 1,000 dollars. The attending provider must submit a request at least three business days before the scheduled service. Emergency admissions are exempt but must be reported as described in §5.2.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of any hospital admission must be given within 48 hours of admission, or within 48 hours of an emergency admission. Notice of a planned delivery of services under §5.1 must be given at least three business days in advance. Failure to provide timely notice reduces payable benefits by 25 percent.

§5.3 Claim Submission
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Claims received later than 90 days will be denied unless it was not reasonably possible to submit them earlier. Completed claims are paid within 30 days of receipt of all required documentation.

§5.4 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must include a written statement explaining why the denial is believed to be incorrect. A decision on the appeal will be issued within 60 days of receipt, and that decision is final under this demo plan.

§6.1 Administration
Premiums are due on the first day of each covered month, and a grace period of 10 days applies before termination. Termination of coverage ends all benefits, except that claims for services rendered before termination will be honored if submitted within the deadline in §5.3. This entire document is synthetic sample content intended solely for demonstration of software functionality.

SYNTHETIC
Demo Sample University Student Health Plan (Illustration Only)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Student" means an individual enrolled at the fictional Demo Sample University who has paid the student health fee for the current term. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each August 1. "Medically Necessary Service" means care that a licensed provider determines is reasonable and required to treat an illness or injury.

§1.2 Purpose
This document is a synthetic sample created solely for software demonstration purposes. It describes fictional benefits, limits, and procedures that do not apply to any real institution or person. All names, amounts, and provisions are invented for testing.

§2.1 Eligibility
Students enrolled in at least six credit hours per term are eligible for coverage under this plan. Coverage begins on the first day of the term following a waiting period of fourteen days after enrollment. Students who withdraw from all courses lose eligibility on the date of withdrawal.

§2.2 Dependent Coverage
Eligible students may enroll a spouse or domestic partner and children under age nineteen. Dependent enrollment must be completed within thirty-one days of the qualifying event. Dependent premiums are set at two hundred dollars per dependent per term for this fictional illustration.

§3.1 Covered Benefits
The plan covers physician office visits up to twenty visits per Plan Year, with a twenty-dollar copayment per visit. Inpatient hospital care is covered up to sixty days per Plan Year at a rate of one hundred percent after a two hundred fifty dollar deductible. Emergency room visits are covered with a one hundred dollar copayment, waived if the student is admitted as an inpatient as described in §3.2.

§3.2 Mental Health and Preventive Care
Outpatient mental health counseling is covered up to thirty sessions per Plan Year with a fifteen-dollar copayment. Preventive services, including annual physical examinations and immunizations, are covered at one hundred percent with no copayment. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered up to twenty days per Plan Year.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic prescriptions are covered with a ten-dollar copayment and brand-name prescriptions with a thirty-dollar copayment. A thirty-day supply limit applies per fill, with a maximum of three refills per prescription. Mail-order fills of a ninety-day supply carry a copayment of twenty-five dollars for generics.

§4.1 Annual and Lifetime Limits
The plan's annual benefit maximum is one hundred fifty thousand dollars per Covered Student. There is no lifetime maximum for services covered under §3.2. Physical therapy is limited to thirty combined visits per Plan Year.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, and care received outside the fictional service area except for emergencies. Dental care is excluded except for injury to sound natural teeth, which is covered up to five hundred dollars per occurrence. Exclusions do not apply to services mandated under §3.2 preventive care.

§4.3 Pre-Existing Conditions
A pre-existing condition is any condition for which care was received during the six months before the coverage effective date. Such conditions are excluded for the first twelve months of continuous coverage. This exclusion is waived for students who were covered under a prior comparable plan without a break of more than sixty-three days.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, elective surgery, and imaging studies exceeding five hundred dollars require prior approval from the plan administrator. Requests must be submitted at least seven days before scheduled services. Emergency admissions require notice within forty-eight hours of admission.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service. Students must report changes in enrollment status within thirty-one days of the change. Failure to meet the deadline in §5.1 may result in a reduction of benefits by twenty-five percent.

§6.1 Cost Sharing
Cost sharing consists of copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance as specified in §3.1 and §3.3. Coinsurance for out-of-network services is thirty percent of allowed amounts. Annual out-of-pocket maximums are three thousand dollars for in-network and six thousand dollars for out-of-network services.

§6.2 Premiums
Student premiums are one thousand two hundred dollars per Plan Year, payable in two installments due August 15 and January 15. A late payment grace period of thirty days applies, after which coverage is suspended. Reinstatement requires payment of all amounts due plus a fifty-dollar reinstatement fee.

§7.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within thirty days of receipt of complete documentation. Students receive an explanation of benefits describing amounts paid, applied to cost sharing, and denied. Claims denied for missing information may be resubmitted within the deadline stated in §5.2.

§7.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice. The plan administrator must issue a written appeal decision within sixty days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal may be filed within sixty days of a first-level denial and is reviewed by an independent fictional review panel.

§7.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a student has other coverage, this plan pays secondary to any parent plan for dependents and primary for the student's own enrollment. Overpayments must be refunded to the plan within sixty days of notice. Benefits are coordinated so that total payments do not exceed one hundred percent of covered expenses.

§8.1 Termination and Continuation
Coverage ends on the last day of the term in which the student ceases to be eligible. A continuation option allows coverage for up to ninety days after graduation at a monthly rate of three hundred dollars. Continuation is not available to students terminated for nonpayment under §6.2.

§8.2 Administration of the Plan
The plan is administered by a fictional office within Demo Sample University that maintains enrollment records and processes appeals under §7.2. Plan documents are available to Covered Students upon request at the campus administrative office. Any amendment to this synthetic plan takes effect on the first day of the next Plan Year.

§8.3 Demonstration Disclaimer
This entire plan is fabricated for software demonstration and contains no legally binding terms. All dollar amounts, deadlines, and provisions are arbitrary test values. No real coverage, entitlement, or obligation is created by this document.

SYNTHETIC

§1.1 Definitions
The word "Plan" means this fictional document and nothing else. "Covered Service" means a service listed in Section 3 that a Network Provider renders. "Benefit Period" means the 90-day span beginning on the Member's effective date. "Network Provider" means a demo provider listed in the fictional directory. §1.2 Fictional Purpose
This plan is generated for demonstration of claims-processing software. It does not insure anyone and must not be read as an offer of coverage. Any resemblance to a real product is unintentional. Users should treat every clause as sample text.

§1.3 Interpretation
Headings are for convenience only and do not affect meaning. Where a clause conflicts with another clause, the clause with the higher section number controls. Singular includes plural and vice versa. The word "may" means permissive and "must" means mandatory.

§2.1 Eligible Members
A person is eligible if they are between 18 and 64 fictional years old and reside in the demo service area. Eligibility requires completion of a short synthetic questionnaire with no underwriting. Dependents under 26 may be added during the demo enrollment window. No real personal data may be entered into the enrollment screen.

Accidental injuries, as described in §4.3, are an exception and are covered from day one. The waiting period is waived entirely for members transferring from another demo plan.

§2.3 Effective Date and Termination
The effective date is the first day after the waiting period. Coverage terminates after 90 days, which may be extended once by 30 days in the demo interface. Termination also occurs if the member cancels through the demo dashboard. Claims for services before the effective date are automatically denied by the test engine.

§3.1 Physician Office Visits
The Plan pays 80 percent of allowed charges for network office visits after the member pays a 25 dollar copay per visit. Visits are limited to 6 per Benefit Period. Specialist visits require the same copay but count toward the same 6-visit limit. Out-of-network visits are covered at 50 percent with no copay, subject to §5.1.

§3.2 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 90 percent of allowed charges after a 500 dollar per-admission deductible. Stays are limited to 30 days per Benefit Period. The daily room allowance is 900 dollars for a private room and 600 dollars for a semi-private room. Emergency admissions are covered even when the admission occurs during the waiting period, per §2.2.

§3.3 Emergency Care
Emergency room visits are covered with a 150 dollar copay, waived if the member is admitted within 24 hours. There is no network requirement for emergency services. Ambulance transport to the nearest fictional facility is covered at 100 percent up to 1,200 dollars per trip. Follow-up visits after an emergency are subject to §3.1 limits.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a 10 dollar copay, preferred brands a 30 dollar copay, and non-preferred brands a 60 dollar copay. A 30-day supply is the standard fill limit. Maintenance drugs may be filled for 90 days at twice the standard copay. All drug pricing is synthetic and generated by the demo formulary service.

§3.5 Diagnostic and Lab Services
Laboratory tests performed at a network draw site are covered at 100 percent with no member cost. Advanced imaging such as synthetic MRI requires prior approval as described in §6.2. Outpatient imaging is covered at 80 percent after approval. Repeat imaging within 30 days of an identical study is excluded unless the provider documents a change in condition.

§3.6 Preventive Services
Annual preventive visits are covered at 100 percent with no deductible. These visits do not count against the 6-visit limit in §3.1. Immunizations listed in the demo schedule are covered at 100 percent. Preventive services are covered even during the waiting period.

§4.1 Annual Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The member's out-of-pocket maximum is 4,000 dollars per Benefit Period. Once reached, covered services are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the period. Copays, deductibles, and coinsurance all accumulate toward the maximum. Penalties described in §5.4 do not count toward the maximum.

§4.2 Lifetime Maximum
The Plan has a fictional lifetime maximum of 250,000 dollars in paid benefits. Once exhausted, no further benefits are payable. The demo interface displays remaining lifetime benefits on the member summary screen. Because this is synthetic data, the counter resets on each demo reset.

§4.3 Accident Exception
Services for accidental injury are covered from day one, overriding the waiting period in §2.2. An accident is defined in this document as sudden bodily damage caused by an external demo event. The accident exception does not extend to accidents occurring during excluded activities listed in §5.2. Providers must note the accident date on the synthetic claim.

§5.1 Out-of-Network Services
Out-of-network services are covered only when no network provider is available within 30 demo miles. Members may be balance-billed by out-of-network providers up to 20 percent above allowed charges. Emergency services are exempt from this clause entirely. Out-of-network claims process 10 business days slower than network claims in the demo pipeline.

§5.2 Activity Exclusions
Injuries sustained during fictional extreme sports such as demo skydiving are excluded. Professional athletic competition is excluded. Racing of any motorized or non-motorized vehicle is excluded. These exclusions do not apply to emergency treatment needed to stabilize the member, which remains covered under §3.3.

§5.3 Cosmetic and Convenience Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures are excluded unless required to repair damage from a covered accident. Convenience items such as demo television rentals during hospital stays are excluded. Travel costs other than covered ambulance transport are excluded. Experimental treatments are excluded unless the demo flag "researchOverride" is enabled by an administrator.

§5.4 Noncompliance Penalties
Failure to obtain prior approval where required reduces the payable amount by 25 percent. Failure to file within the deadline in §6.1 results in denial without penalty appeal rights beyond §6.3. Providing knowingly false synthetic data voids coverage for the related claim only. Penalties are displayed in red in the adjudication screen.

§5.5 Substance and Mental Health Limits
Outpatient mental health visits are covered with a 30 dollar copay, limited to 12 visits per Benefit Period. Inpatient substance treatment is limited to 14 days per Benefit Period. Crisis evaluations are covered at 100 percent and do not count toward the visit limit. These limits are synthetic and exist to exercise limit-tracking code.

§6.1 Claim Filing
Claims must be filed within 90 days of the date of service. Late claims are denied automatically by the demo adjudicator. Clean claims are paid within 14 simulated business days. Members may submit claims through the demo portal using only test data.

§6.2 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, advanced imaging under §3.5, and any service exceeding 2,000 dollars in allowed charges. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before non-urgent services. Urgent requests are decided within 24 simulated hours. Approval is valid for 60 days from the decision date.

§6.3 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. First-level appeals are decided within 30 simulated days by a different demo reviewer. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first decision. While an appeal is pending, related claims continue to process normally.

§6.4 Administration
This plan is administered entirely within the demonstration environment. No payment instruments, real identifiers, or live records are involved. Administrators may reset all member data at any time. Questions about this document should be directed to the demo documentation, not to any real party.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Valley Select HMO — Silverleaf Plan

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January 1. "Covered Service" means a medically necessary service listed in this document. "Primary Care Physician" or "PCP" means the network provider designated to coordinate a member's care. "Copayment" means the fixed dollar amount a member pays at the time of service.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees working at least twenty hours per week may enroll after a thirty-day waiting period. New dependents acquired through birth or legal custody may be added within sixty days of the qualifying event. Coverage ends on the last day of the month following termination of employment.

§1.3 Effective Date
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the first day of the month following the waiting period described in §1.2. Late enrollees must wait until the next open enrollment period. Open enrollment occurs each November.

§2.1 Primary Care Benefits
Office visits to the PCP require a twenty-dollar copayment. Preventive visits including annual physicals are covered at one hundred percent with no copayment. Well-child visits are covered up to twelve visits before age two.

§2.2 Specialist and Hospital Benefits
Specialist visits require a forty-dollar copayment and a referral from the PCP as described in §3.1. Inpatient hospitalization is covered at ninety percent after a two-hundred-fifty-dollar per-admission deductible, limited to sixty days per Plan Year. Emergency room visits carry a one-hundred-fifty-dollar copayment, waived if the member is admitted.

§2.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a ten-dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs thirty dollars, and non-preferred brand drugs sixty dollars. A ninety-day supply through the mail-order program costs two times the thirty-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §3.2.

§3.1 Referrals
Members must obtain a written or electronic referral from their PCP before seeing a specialist. Referrals are valid for ninety days and may specify a limited number of visits. Self-referrals to obstetricians and dermatologists are permitted once per Plan Year without a referral.

§3.2 Prior Approval
Certain services, including MRI, CT scans, and inpatient surgery, require prior approval submitted at least five business days before the service. Emergency admissions require notification within forty-eight hours of admission. Services rendered without required prior approval are excluded except as described in §4.2.

§3.3 Notice Deadlines
Claims for out-of-network emergency services must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service. Members must notify the Plan of address changes within thirty days. Failure to meet a notice deadline voids the related claim unless it was reasonable not to have known the deadline applied.

§4.1 Limits
Physical therapy is limited to thirty visits per Plan Year. Chiropractic care is limited to twenty visits per Plan Year. Speech therapy is limited to sixty visits per Plan Year for members under age nineteen.

§4.2 Exclusions
Cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, and services outside the network are excluded. The out-of-network exclusion does not apply to emergency care or services approved under §3.2. Hearing aids are excluded except one pair per Plan Year for members under age eighteen.

§4.3 Dental and Vision Exclusions
Routine dental care is excluded except accident-related tooth repair within twelve months of injury. Eyeglasses and contact lenses are excluded except one pair per Plan Year for members under age nineteen. Orthodontia is excluded entirely.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is three thousand dollars per member and six thousand dollars per family. Copayments and deductibles count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Once the maximum is reached, Covered Services are paid at one hundred percent for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§5.2 Coordination of Benefits
When a member has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays secondary according to standard coordination rules. Members must disclose other coverage upon enrollment. Overpayments must be refunded within sixty days of notice.

§5.3 Premiums
Monthly premiums are one hundred eighty dollars for member-only coverage and four hundred ten dollars for family coverage. Premiums are due by the fifth of each month. Coverage lapses if premiums are more than thirty days late, and reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus a fifty-dollar fee.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be filed by network providers on the member's behalf. Members receive an explanation of benefits within thirty days of claim processing. Claims are considered denied if no payment or notice is issued within sixty days of submission.

§6.2 Appeals
Members may appeal a denial within one hundred eighty days by submitting a written request. The Plan must respond to a first-level appeal within thirty days. A second-level appeal may be requested within sixty days of a first-level denial and is reviewed by a committee not involved in the original denial.

§6.3 External Review
If a second-level appeal under §6.2 is denied, the member may request independent external review within four months. External review decisions are binding on the Plan. The Plan pays the cost of the external reviewer.

§6.4 Grievances
Grievances about quality of care, distinct from coverage denials under §6.2, may be filed at any time. The Plan must acknowledge a grievance within five business days and resolve it within forty-five days. Members may request an expedited grievance process when waiting would jeopardize health.

§7.1 Termination and Continuation
Members losing eligibility may continue coverage for up to eighteen months by paying the full premium plus a two-percent administrative charge. Election of continuation must be made within sixty days of the loss notice. Continuation coverage ends early if premiums are not paid as required under §5.3.

§7.2 Amendment
The Plan may amend this document annually before each open enrollment period. Members receive written notice of amendments at least thirty days before they take effect. No amendment reduces benefits mid-year except as required by law.

SYNTHETIC
Accident Shield Demo Plan 3000 — Sample Coverage Document for Software Demonstration

§1.1 Definitions
"Accident" means a sudden, unintended physical event occurring while this policy is in force that directly causes bodily injury to the insured person. "Injury" means harm requiring treatment by a licensed healthcare provider within 72 hours of the event. "Benefit period" means the 52 weeks following an accident during which covered treatment may be reimbursed. All defined terms are used with initial capital letters throughout this document.

§1.2 Eligibility
Any resident of the fictional jurisdiction of Sampleland between ages 18 and 70 may enroll in this plan. Enrollment takes effect on the first day of the month following a completed application. Persons employed in hazardous demonstration occupations, such as fictional volcano guides, are eligible only under the rider described in §2.4.

§1.3 Waiting Period
A 14-day waiting period applies from the effective date before any benefit under §3.1 becomes payable. Injuries caused by accidents occurring during the waiting period are not covered. The waiting period is waived for enrollees transferring from another synthetic plan with at least 6 months of continuous comparable coverage.

§1.4 Dependents
Enrollees may add a spouse or up to three dependent children to the policy at an additional monthly charge of 9.00 demo units per dependent. Dependent children are covered until age 19, or until age 23 if enrolled full-time in a fictional educational institution. Dependent coverage terminates automatically when the enrollee's coverage ends.

§2.1 Monthly Premium
The base premium is 24.50 demo units per month for individual coverage. Premiums are due on the first calendar day of each month, and a grace period of 10 days applies before termination for nonpayment. Premiums are adjusted annually by the fictional index described in §6.2.

§2.2 Deductible
The insured must pay an annual deductible of 150.00 demo units before benefits are payable in any policy year. The deductible applies per insured person, not per accident. Payments made under other fictional coverage may count toward the deductible, subject to §4.3.

§2.3 Coinsurance
After the deductible is satisfied, the plan pays 80 percent of covered expenses and the insured pays 20 percent. The coinsurance rate rises to 30 percent for treatment received from providers outside the fictional Samplecare network. Out-of-network coinsurance does not apply to emergency treatment under §3.2.

§2.4 Out-of-Pocket Limit
The annual out-of-pocket limit is 1,200.00 demo units per insured person, after which the plan pays 100 percent of covered expenses for the remainder of the policy year. Premiums, deductible amounts, and the charges excluded under §4.1 do not count toward this limit. The limit resets on each January 1 of the fictional calendar.

§3.1 Medical Expense Benefit
The plan reimburses covered medical expenses for treatment of an injury as described in §1.1, up to a maximum of 25,000.00 demo units per accident. Covered expenses include physician visits, diagnostic imaging, prescription drugs, and physical therapy. Reimbursement is subject to the deductible in §2.2 and the coinsurance in §2.3.

§3.2 Emergency Treatment Benefit
Emergency room treatment for an accident is covered without prior approval, up to 3,500.00 demo units per event. A 150.00 demo units emergency room copayment applies in place of the coinsurance in §2.3. Follow-up visits within 30 days of the emergency event are covered as ordinary medical expenses under §3.1.

§3.3 Hospital Confinement Benefit
The plan pays 200.00 demo units per day of hospital confinement resulting from a covered accident, for up to 30 days per accident. A benefit of 400.00 demo units per day applies in an intensive care unit, for up to 10 days. Confinement must begin within 30 days of the accident to qualify.

§3.4 Accidental Death and Dismemberment Benefit
The plan pays 10,000.00 demo units for accidental death occurring within 90 days of a covered accident. Loss of a hand or foot pays 5,000.00 demo units, and loss of sight in one eye pays 5,000.00 demo units. No more than 100 percent of the principal sum is payable for all losses from one accident, and this benefit is not subject to the deductible in §2.2.

§3.5 Dental Injury Benefit
Injury to natural teeth caused by an accident is covered up to 1,500.00 demo units per accident. Repair or replacement must be completed within 12 months of the accident. Damage arising from chewing or biting, however forceful, is excluded except as provided in §4.2.

§3.6 Fracture Benefit
A scheduled benefit of 100.00 demo units is payable for a simple fracture of a limb and 250.00 demo units for a compound fracture, payable once per bone per policy year. A fracture must be confirmed by diagnostic imaging. This benefit is paid in addition to the medical expense benefit in §3.1.

§4.1 General Exclusions
The plan does not cover injuries arising from war, self-inflicted harm, commission of a fictional felony, or professional athletic competition. Injuries sustained while operating a fictional aircraft as a crew member are excluded. Treatment that is not medically necessary, as determined under §5.3, is excluded.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
The professional athletic exclusion in §4.1 does not apply to recreational league play, provided the enrollee discloses participation at enrollment. Self-inflicted harm is covered if resulting from a documented involuntary reflex event certified by two providers. The felony exclusion does not apply where the enrollee was a victim of the offense.

§4.3 Coordination of Benefits
If the insured holds other valid accident coverage, this plan pays only the portion of the expense not payable by the other coverage, up to 100 percent of the expense in total. The insured must disclose other coverage at enrollment and upon any change. Failure to disclose may result in recovery of overpaid benefits under §5.2.

§4.4 Prior Approval Rules
Non-emergency treatment expected to exceed 1,000.00 demo units requires prior approval from the plan administrator. Prior approval requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before the treatment date. Emergency treatment is exempt from this rule but must be reported within the notice period in §5.1.

§5.1 Notice and Proof of Claim
Written notice of an accident must be given within 20 days of the event, or as soon as reasonably possible. Proof of claim, including itemized provider statements, must be submitted within 90 days of the accident. The plan may extend the deadline where the delay was beyond the insured's reasonable control.

§5.2 Claim Payment and Recovery
Approved claims are paid within 30 days of receiving complete proof of claim. Benefits are paid to the insured, or to a designated beneficiary under §3.4 in the event of death. Overpayments must be refunded within 60 days of written demand, and the plan may offset future benefits to recover them.

§5.3 Utilization Review
The plan may review treatment records to confirm that care is medically necessary and consistent with the definitions in §1.1. Review decisions are made within 10 business days of receiving the requested records. Treatment denied as unnecessary may still qualify for the scheduled fracture benefit in §3.6 if imaging confirms the fracture.

§5.4 Appeals
A claimant may appeal an adverse decision within 180 days by submitting a written appeal to the plan administrator. A first-level appeal is decided by a different reviewer within 30 days, and a second-level appeal by the fictional independent Review Board within 45 days. Exhaustion of both appeal levels is required before any fictional arbitration under §6.3.

§6.1 Policy Term and Renewal
The policy runs for 12-month terms beginning on the effective date. The plan renews automatically unless either party gives 30 days written notice of nonrenewal. Benefits payable for accidents occurring during a policy term continue under §3.1 until the end of the benefit period, even if the policy later terminates.

§6.2 Changes to Terms
The plan may change premiums or benefit schedules upon 60 days written notice before renewal. No change may reduce benefits for accidents that have already occurred. The annual premium adjustment uses the fictional Sampleland Medical Cost Index, capped at 8 percent per year.

§6.3 Dispute Resolution
Disputes not resolved through the appeal process in §5.4 are submitted to binding arbitration in the fictional city of Port Sample. Arbitration is conducted under the fictional Sampleland Arbitration Code, and each party bears its own costs. This clause survives termination of the policy.

§6.4 Administration
The plan is administered by the fictional Demo Assurance Authority, which maintains enrollment records and processes claims under §5.2. Enrollees must notify the administrator of address or dependent changes within 30 days. This document is a synthetic sample generated solely for software demonstration and confers no actual coverage.

SYNTHETIC
Demo Silver Horizon HMO 4200 Plan (Sample Plan Document — Not a Real Product)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an individual enrolled under this plan whose coverage is in active status. "Network Provider" means a provider contracted with the plan's demo network as of the date of service. "Deductible" means the amount a Covered Person must pay each plan year before the plan pays most benefits.

§1.2 Plan Year
The plan year runs from the first day of the demo calendar year through the last day of that year. All deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, and visit limits reset on the first day of each plan year. Services rendered before the effective date of coverage are never counted toward the current plan year.

§2.1 Eligibility
An applicant must reside in the fictional demo service area and be a lawful resident of the demo jurisdiction. Dependent children may remain on the policy until the end of the plan year in which they turn 26. Enrollment during the annual open period becomes effective on the first day of the following plan year.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees are subject to a 30-day waiting period for non-emergency services, except that preventive services described in §3.1 are covered from day one. Emergency services are never subject to the waiting period. Maternity care is covered from the effective date of coverage regardless of the waiting period.

§3.1 Preventive Services
The plan covers in-network preventive services at 100 percent of the allowed amount with no cost sharing, including annual physicals, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings. Screening mammograms are covered once per plan year. Diagnostic follow-up services resulting from a preventive screening are subject to the cost sharing described in §4.1.

§3.2 Hospital and Emergency Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered after the deductible at 80 percent of the allowed amount, limited to 60 days per plan year. Emergency room visits are covered at the in-network level regardless of provider network status, subject to a $350 copayment that is waived if the visit results in a direct inpatient admission. Outpatient surgery is covered at 80 percent after the deductible.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
The plan uses a three-tier drug schedule: $15 for tier one, $45 for tier two, and 40 percent coinsurance for tier three, with a tier-three maximum of $150 per fill. A 90-day supply at tier one or two is available through the demo mail program for two copayments. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
The individual deductible is $4,200 per plan year, and the family deductible is $8,400, any two family members' combined payments satisfying the family amount. The out-of-pocket maximum is $8,700 per individual and $17,400 per family, after which the plan pays 100 percent of in-network covered services for the remainder of the year. Copayments do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.2 Mental Health and Therapy
In-network outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent after the deductible, limited to 30 visits per plan year. In-network substance use treatment is covered for up to 28 inpatient days per plan year. Intensive outpatient programs require prior approval under §5.1.

§4.3 Rehabilitation and Therapy Limits
Physical, occupational, and speech therapy are each limited to 25 combined visits per plan year, except that visits following a covered inpatient stay within 60 days of discharge are not counted against this limit. Home health care is limited to 40 visits per plan year. Hospice care is covered without a visit limit.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions (except emergencies, which require notice within 48 hours), imaging such as MRI and CT, specialty drugs under §3.3, and all procedures valued above $2,500 on the demo schedule. Requests are decided within 5 business days, or 72 hours when expedited for urgent care. Failure to obtain required approval reduces payment for the service by 50 percent but never results in complete denial when the service itself is covered.

§5.2 Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, dental care for persons over age 19, vision hardware beyond one pair of standard lenses per plan year, or services received outside the demo service area except for emergencies. Experimental treatments are excluded unless the treatment is part of a covered clinical trial for a life-threatening condition. Weight-loss surgery is covered only when the Covered Person has documented medical necessity and has completed a 6-month supervised program.

§5.3 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service. Covered Persons must notify the plan of an inpatient admission within 48 hours, or the next business day for weekend admissions. Appeals of denied claims must be filed within 180 days of the denial notice, as described in §6.2.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Network providers submit claims directly, and the plan pays or denies them within 30 days of receipt. Covered Persons who pay out of pocket at a network provider may seek reimbursement by submitting an itemized receipt and claim form. Payment is made at the in-network allowed amount, less any applicable cost sharing under §4.1.

§6.2 Appeals
A first-level appeal is reviewed by a reviewer who was not involved in the original denial, with a decision issued within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent appeals. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of a first-level denial and includes the right to submit additional documentation. External review is available after both internal levels are exhausted, and the external decision is binding on the plan.

§6.3 Termination and Continuation
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the Covered Person ceases to be eligible under §2.1 or fails to pay premiums by the 31-day grace period deadline. Claims for services rendered before termination are payable if submitted within the deadline in §5.3. Continuing coverage options follow the demo continuation rules applicable to the plan's fictional sponsor.

SYNTHETIC.

Made-up plan name: Luminar Flex Group Health Plan (Demo Edition)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an enrolled employee or enrolled dependent whose coverage is active under this plan. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each March 1. "Negotiated Rate" means the pre-set discount schedule used by this demo plan, which is 40 percent below the published Demo Fee Schedule. "Medically Necessary" means a service that a licensed provider documents as required to treat a diagnosed condition.

§1.2 Definitions continued
"Prior Approval" means written confirmation issued by the plan administrator before certain services are received. "Out-of-Pocket Maximum" means the most a Covered Person pays in cost sharing during a Plan Year, set at $6,000 per person and $11,500 per family. "Urgent Care Facility" means a licensed walk-in clinic that treats conditions requiring attention within 24 hours.

§2.1 Eligibility
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible for coverage. New employees enter coverage on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous employment. Seasonal workers and independent contractors are not eligible, except that contractors retained for at least 9 months may enroll by paying the full monthly premium of $780 plus a 10 percent administrative load.

§2.2 Dependent eligibility
Dependents include a legal spouse and children under age 26. A child who is disabled before age 26 may remain covered indefinitely if the disability is documented annually. Dependents of ineligible contractors may not enroll separately.

§2.3 Enrollment windows
Initial enrollment must be completed within 31 days of eligibility. Open enrollment runs each January 15 through February 15, with changes effective March 1. Outside these windows, changes require a qualifying life event reported within 30 days, such as marriage, birth, or involuntary loss of other coverage.

§3.1 Medical benefits
The plan pays 80 percent of the Negotiated Rate for physician visits after a $25 copayment per office visit. Preventive care is covered at 100 percent with no copayment. Hospital inpatient care is covered at 70 percent after Prior Approval, as described in §6.1, with a $500 per-admission deductible.

§3.2 Prescription benefits
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $35 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $60 copayment. A 90-day mail supply costs two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require Prior Approval and are limited to a $2,500 per-fill charge to the member.

§3.3 Mental health and therapy
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent after a $20 copayment, limited to 30 visits per Plan Year. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered for up to 45 days per Plan Year at 70 percent. Additional visits beyond the 30-visit limit may be approved for documented severe conditions, as described in §7.2.

§3.4 Dental and vision
Dental coverage includes two cleanings per Plan Year at 100 percent, fillings at 70 percent, and orthodontia at 50 percent capped at $1,500 per lifetime. Vision includes one exam per Plan Year with a $15 copayment and $150 toward frames or contact lenses every 24 months.

§4.1 Annual limits
Combined inpatient hospital days are limited to 90 per Plan Year per Covered Person. Physical therapy is limited to 40 visits per Plan Year, occupational therapy to 30, and speech therapy to 30. Chiropractic care is limited to 20 visits with a $15 copayment each.

§4.2 Exclusions
Excluded are cosmetic surgery, weight-loss supplements, experimental treatments not approved by two independent reviewers, and services received outside the demo service area except emergencies. Excluded also are injuries sustained during paid amateur athletics, except that routine treatment of such injuries is covered when the member holds the optional rider described in §5.3.

§4.3 Exclusion exceptions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or a documented mastectomy is not considered cosmetic and is covered at 80 percent. Emergency care received outside the service area is covered at in-network levels if the member could not reasonably reach a network facility. Hearing aids, otherwise excluded, are covered up to $1,000 every 36 months for members under age 18.

§4.4 Coordination of benefits
When a Covered Person has other coverage, this plan pays secondary unless this plan is the primary plan under standard order-of-benefits rules. Payments made by this plan will not exceed the amount it would have paid as primary. Overpayments must be refunded within 60 days of notice.

§5.1 Cost sharing summary
The annual deductible is $1,500 per person and $2,800 per family, except that preventive care, the copayments in §3.1 through §3.4, and prescription copayments in §3.2 are not subject to the deductible. Once the Out-of-Pocket Maximum is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of covered services for the rest of the Plan Year.

§5.2 Premium contributions
Employees contribute $120 per month for single coverage, $240 for employee plus one, and $330 for family coverage. Contributions are deducted pre-tax from each paycheck. Premiums are due by the 10th of each month; coverage lapses if payment is more than 30 days late, and reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus a $50 fee.

§5.3 Optional riders
Members may purchase an athletics injury rider for $18 per month, which lifts the exclusion in §4.2 for paid amateur athletics. A dental upgrade rider costing $25 per month raises the orthodontia lifetime cap to $3,000. Riders may be added only during open enrollment.

§6.1 Prior approval rules
Prior Approval is required for inpatient admissions, surgery, imaging over $1,000, specialty drugs, and durable medical equipment over $500. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before scheduled services, or within 48 hours after emergency admissions. Approval is valid for 60 days from issuance.

§6.2 Notification deadlines
Members must notify the administrator of a new dependent within 31 days of the qualifying event. Notice of intent to appeal under §8.2 must be filed within 180 days of the adverse decision. Failure to meet a deadline in this section forfeits the related right, except where the member shows the delay was reasonable.

§6.3 Emergency procedures
Emergency admissions must be reported to the administrator within 48 hours of admission or as soon as reasonably possible. If the member is incapacitated, a family member or treating facility may report on the member's behalf. Late reporting reduces payment by 10 percent but never below 60 percent of covered charges.

§7.1 Claims submission
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. Claims filed after that date are denied, except in the case of mental incapacity or a documented natural disaster. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt.

§7.2 Medical review
The plan may refer any claim for medical review by an independent reviewer. Reviews under §3.3 for visits beyond the 30-visit mental health limit require documentation from the treating provider of medical necessity. Review decisions are issued within 15 business days and include the specific reason and the member's appeal rights.

§8.1 Claims appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. The administrator issues a first-level decision within 30 days. The member may submit additional records, and the reviewer may not defer entirely to the original denial.

§8.2 Second-level appeals and external review
A second-level appeal must be requested within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided by a reviewer with no prior role in the matter, within 30 days. If the second appeal is denied, the member may request external review by an independent entity within 4 months. External review decisions are binding on the plan.

§9.1 Administration
The plan is administered by the sponsoring employer's benefits office, which maintains enrollment records, issues Prior Approvals, and processes claims and appeals under §§7.1 through 8.2. SYNTHETIC
DemoCare Silver Compass Plan 4500, a fictional individual marketplace health plan generated solely for software demonstration purposes.

§1.1 Defined Terms
Throughout this synthetic document, "Plan" refers to DemoCare Silver Compass Plan 4500. "Covered Person" means an enrollee or enrolled dependent. "Allowable Amount" means the maximum payment this Plan recognizes for a covered service, as published in the fictional demonstration fee schedule.

§1.2 Purpose of Document
This document is synthetic and does not describe any real insurance product. It exists to exercise software that parses, validates, and displays policy text. Any resemblance to actual plans or provisions is coincidental.

§1.3 Interpretation
Ambiguities in this demonstration text shall be resolved in favor of the sample data set. Nothing here creates rights, obligations, or coverage of any kind.

§2.1 Eligibility
A fictional applicant must be at least 18 years old, reside in the demonstration service area, and not be incarcerated. Dependents are eligible until the end of the month in which they turn 26, except dependents who are permanently disabled, for whom eligibility continues indefinitely.

§2.2 Effective Dates and Waiting Periods
Coverage begins on the first day of the month following plan selection. A 30-day waiting period applies to elective surgery, except surgery necessitated by accidental injury, which has no waiting period.

§2.3 Open Enrollment and Special Enrollment
The demonstration open enrollment window runs from October 1 through December 15. A qualifying life event, such as marriage or loss of other fictional coverage, triggers a 60-day special enrollment window.

§3.1 Preventive Services
In-network preventive care, including one annual physical, age-appropriate screenings, and immunizations, is covered at 100 percent with no cost sharing. Screening mammograms are included, but diagnostic mammograms are subject to the cost sharing described in §5.1.

§3.2 Physician and Specialist Visits
Primary care visits carry a $25 copayment and specialist visits a $50 copayment when rendered in network. Out-of-network visits are covered at 60 percent of the Allowable Amount after the deductible in §5.2 is met.

§3.3 Hospital and Emergency Services
Inpatient hospitalization is covered at 80 percent after deductible, limited to 90 days per calendar year. Emergency room visits carry a $350 copayment, waived if the visit results in a direct inpatient admission.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
The fictional formulary has three tiers: generic drugs at a $15 copayment, preferred brand at $45, and non-preferred brand at 40 percent coinsurance. A 90-day supply of maintenance medications is available at twice the 30-day copayment through the demonstration mail-order channel.

§3.5 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at a $30 copayment, limited to 30 visits per year. Inpatient substance use treatment is covered for up to 28 days per admission, with a maximum of two admissions per year.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Elective inpatient admissions, imaging such as MRI and CT, and durable medical equipment exceeding $1,000 require prior approval. Requests must be submitted at least 10 business days before the service, except in emergencies where notice within 48 hours suffices.

§4.2 Exclusions
Excluded services include cosmetic surgery, weight loss drugs, vision hardware for adults, and dental care, except dental care required to treat accidental injury to sound natural teeth. Experimental treatments are excluded unless the demonstration review board grants an exception under §4.3.

§4.3 Exceptions Process
A Covered Person may request an exception to an exclusion by submitting a supporting statement from the treating provider. The fictional review board must respond within 15 calendar days, or 72 hours if delay would seriously jeopardize health.

§4.4 Out-of-Network Balance Billing
Providers outside the demonstration network may bill amounts above the Allowable Amount. Such balance billing is the Covered Person's responsibility and does not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum described in §5.2.

§5.1 Cost Sharing Overview
In-network cost sharing consists of the copayments and coinsurance stated in §3.1 through §3.5. Out-of-network cost sharing is calculated against the Allowable Amount and is always higher.

§5.2 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The annual in-network deductible is $4,500 per person and $9,000 per family. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $8,700 per person and $17,400 per family; once reached, in-network covered services are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the calendar year.

§5.3 Premium Payment
Fictional premiums are due by the first of each month. If payment is not received within 30 days of the due date, coverage is suspended retroactively to the due date, and reinstatement requires payment of all missed premiums plus a $25 administrative fee.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Participating providers submit claims electronically within 90 days of service. Covered Persons submitting paper claims must do so within 180 days of the date of service, using the fictional claim form included in the sample data.

§6.2 Claims Payment and Denial
Clean claims are paid within 30 calendar days of receipt. Denials must state the specific reason and the clause relied upon, such as §4.2, and must be issued within 15 calendar days of the determination.

§6.3 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denial within 180 days of the denial notice. Level one appeals are decided within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care matters, and a second-level appeal to the fictional appeals panel is available.

§6.4 External Review
After exhausting appeals under §6.3, the Covered Person may request external review by an independent fictional reviewer. The external decision is binding on the Plan but not on the Covered Person.

§6.5 Records and Coordination
The Plan may request medical records reasonably necessary to adjudicate claims, limited to records relevant to the service at issue. Coordination of benefits applies when another fictional coverage exists, with this Plan secondary when the other coverage is primary.

§7.1 Termination
Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which the Covered Person no longer meets §2.1 eligibility, fails to pay premiums under §5.3, or requests termination in writing at least 15 days before the intended end date.

§7.2 Continuation of Coverage
Terminated enrollees may purchase 90 days of transitional fictional coverage at full premium cost, provided the request is made within 30 days of termination. Transitional coverage may not be renewed.

§7.3 Amendment and Severability
This synthetic document may be amended only through updates to the demonstration data set. If any clause is held inconsistent with the demonstration rules, the remaining clauses continue in effect for testing purposes.
