SYNTHETIC
Nimbus Small Business Health Plan, Demonstration Edition

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an Eligible Employee or enrolled Dependant who has satisfied all conditions of §2.1 and §2.2. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the first day of March. "Qualifying Expense" means a medically necessary charge for Covered Services that does not exceed the Reasonable and Customary amount determined by the Plan Administrator.

§1.2 Plan Administrator
The Plan Administrator is a fictional entity created solely for this software demonstration. It processes claims, maintains enrollment records, and issues written determinations within thirty (30) days of receiving complete documentation. All references to notices sent by the Administrator are deemed delivered five (5) business days after mailing.

§2.1 Eligibility
An Eligible Employee is any person employed at least thirty (30) hours per week by a Participating Employer. Eligibility begins on the first day of the month following ninety (90) days of continuous employment. Temporary and seasonal workers are not Eligible Employees regardless of hours worked.

§2.2 Dependants and Enrollment
Eligible Employees may enroll a spouse and dependent children under age twenty-six (26). Enrollment must be completed within thirty-one (31) days of the date eligibility begins or of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, or adoption. Late enrollees must wait until the next annual open enrollment period, except as provided in §2.1 for new hires.

§3.1 Medical Benefits
The Plan pays eighty percent (80%) of Reasonable and Customary charges for physician visits, hospitalization, and surgery, subject to the annual deductible of one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) per Covered Person. After the Covered Person's out-of-pocket amount reaches six thousand dollars ($6,000) in a Plan Year, the Plan pays one hundred percent (100%) of Qualifying Expenses. Prior approval under §4.1 is required for inpatient admissions and elective surgery.

§3.2 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs are covered at one hundred percent (100%) after a fifteen dollar ($15) copayment, and brand-name drugs at eighty percent (80%) after a forty dollar ($40) copayment. A thirty-day supply is the maximum dispensed per fill, except for maintenance medications, which may be filled for ninety (90) days at double the copayment. No deductible applies to prescription drugs.

§3.3 Mental Health and Preventive Services
The Plan covers up to twenty (20) outpatient mental health visits per Plan Year at the cost-sharing rate described in §3.1. Preventive services, including annual physicals, immunizations, and screening tests, are covered at one hundred percent (100%) with no deductible. One routine eye examination and one routine dental cleaning per Covered Person are covered each Plan Year.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval must be requested at least ten (10) business days before scheduled inpatient admissions, elective surgery, and imaging exceeding five hundred dollars ($500). Emergency admissions require notification within seventy-two (72) hours of admission. Failure to obtain required prior approval reduces payment for the related claim by fifty percent (50%), except in emergencies where timely notice was given.

§4.2 Exclusions
The Plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, dental care beyond that described in §3.3, or services received outside the service area unless authorized under §4.3. Injuries sustained while committing a felony or during paid professional athletics are excluded. Work-related injuries covered by statutory workers' compensation are excluded to the extent benefits are actually payable under that coverage.

§4.3 Out-of-Area and Emergency Exceptions
Emergency services received outside the service area are covered at the in-network rate for the first seventy-two (72) hours of treatment. Elective treatment outside the service area is covered only if the Covered Person obtains written authorization before receiving care. This exception operates independently of the notice rules in §4.1.

§5.1 Cost Sharing and Premiums
Employees contribute twenty-five percent (25%) of the monthly premium through payroll deduction, and the Participating Employer pays the remainder. Premiums are due on the first day of each month, with a ten-day grace period before coverage lapses. Coverage lapsed for nonpayment may be reinstated within thirty (30) days upon payment of all overdue amounts.

§5.2 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays as secondary unless it is the plan covering the person as an employee. Payments under this Plan shall not exceed the amount it would have paid as primary payer. The Administrator may recover overpayments made because of unreported other coverage.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within ninety (90) days of the date of service using forms provided by the Administrator. Complete claims are paid or denied within thirty (30) days of receipt, and partial payments may be issued while documentation is pending. Claims submitted more than twelve (12) months after the date of service are denied as untimely.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within one hundred eighty (180) days of the denial notice. The Administrator issues a written appeal decision within sixty (60) days, and a second-level review may be requested within sixty (60) days of that decision. The second-level decision is final for purposes of this Plan.

§6.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment terminates, the premium is not paid after the grace period in §5.1, or the Participating Employer withdraws from the Plan. Enrolled Dependants lose coverage on the date they no longer meet the definition in §1.1. Nothing in this section limits the appeal rights described in §6.2.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: AuroraFlex HMO Silver 700

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this plan, "Network Provider" means a practitioner or facility contracted with the plan's provider network. "Medically Necessary Care" means services that a Network Provider certifies as appropriate for diagnosis or treatment under accepted clinical standards. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning January 1 and ending December 31.

§1.2 Eligibility
Coverage is available to members and their enrolled dependents who reside within the plan's designated service area. New dependents acquired by birth or adoption must be enrolled within 45 days of the qualifying event. Coverage for newly hired members begins after a 30-day waiting period from the first day of employment.

§2.1 Primary Care Physician
Each member must select a Primary Care Physician from the network directory upon enrollment. The Primary Care Physician coordinates all routine care and issues referrals for specialty services. Members may change their selection once per Plan Year without cause.

§2.2 Referrals
Specialist visits require a referral from the Primary Care Physician except for emergency care as described in §3.2. Referrals remain valid for 90 days or three visits, whichever occurs first. Care delivered by an out-of-network specialist without a referral is not covered except as described in §2.3.

§2.3 Direct Access Exceptions
Members may access network obstetricians, dermatologists for up to two visits per Plan Year, and behavioral health providers without a referral. Annual vision examinations at network providers are also exempt from the referral requirement. All other specialty care requires referral as described in §2.2.

§3.1 Hospital Benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 100 percent after a $250 per-admission copayment, subject to a 60-day annual limit. Semiprivate accommodations are the standard covered level of care. Private rooms are covered only when medically necessary, as certified under §1.1.

§3.2 Emergency Care
Emergency services at any facility are covered at the in-network cost sharing level regardless of location. The $150 emergency room copayment is waived if the member is admitted as an inpatient under §3.1. Members must notify the plan within 48 hours of any emergency admission, or as soon as reasonably possible.

§4.1 Outpatient Benefits
Office visits to Primary Care Physicians carry a $20 copayment, and specialist visits carry a $40 copayment. Outpatient surgery is covered at 90 percent after the plan's deductible of $700 per member per Plan Year. Diagnostic imaging such as MRI or CT scans requires prior approval as described in §5.1.

§4.2 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs a $35 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $60 copayment. Mail-order supplies provide a 90-day fill for the price of two monthly copayments. Specialty drugs require prior approval and are limited to a 30-day supply per fill.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions other than emergencies, advanced imaging, physical therapy beyond the 12th visit, and durable medical equipment exceeding $1,000 in value. Requests must be submitted by the Network Provider at least 10 business days before the scheduled service. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment by 50 percent but does not void coverage entirely.

§5.2 Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures, weight-loss surgery without documented medical necessity, and experimental treatments are excluded from coverage. Dental care for members over age 19 is excluded, except for treatment of accidental injury to sound natural teeth within 90 days of the injury. Excluded services do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum described in §6.2.

§5.3 Annual Limits
Physical therapy is limited to 20 visits per Plan Year, and chiropractic care to 12 visits per Plan Year. Speech therapy is limited to 30 sessions per Plan Year for members under age 18. Services beyond these limits may be reviewed under the medical necessity process described in §5.1.

§6.1 Cost Sharing Summary
The plan's annual deductible is $700 per member and $1,400 per family. Copayments for office visits under §4.1 apply before the deductible is satisfied. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $4,000 per member and $8,000 per family.

§6.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
Once a member reaches the out-of-pocket maximum, the plan covers all covered services at 100 percent for the remainder of the Plan Year. Copayments for prescription drugs under §4.2 count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Amounts for non-covered services, including those listed in §5.2, do not count toward this maximum.

§7.1 Claims Administration
Network Providers submit claims directly to the plan and may not bill members beyond applicable cost sharing. Clean claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt. Members using out-of-network emergency services under §3.2 are responsible only for submitting the itemized bill within 120 days of service.

§7.2 Appeals
Members may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial notice. The plan issues a written decision within 30 days for standard appeals and within 72 hours for expedited appeals involving urgent care. A second-level external review is available after exhaustion of the internal process described in this section.

§7.3 Termination and Continuation
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which membership ceases. Members losing eligibility may continue coverage for up to 18 months by paying the full premium plus a 2 percent administrative charge. Election of continuation must be made within 60 days of the termination notice.

§7.4 Notices
All plan notices are delivered to the member's address of record. Members must report address changes within 30 days. Failure to receive a notice due to an unreported address change does not extend any deadline stated in this plan, including those in §7.1 and §7.2.

SYNTHETIC
Plan name: Bluegate Flexible Health Shield (Demo Plan 47)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an enrolled employee or enrolled dependent as described in §2.1. "Eligible Expense" means a medically necessary charge for a Covered Service rendered by a Provider while coverage is in force. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning January 1.

§1.2 Definitions continued
"Copayment" means the fixed dollar amount the Covered Person owes at the time of service. "Deductible" means the amount of Eligible Expenses a Covered Person must pay each Plan Year before the Plan pays benefits. "Negotiated Rate" means the amount the Plan has agreed to pay a Network Provider.

§1.3 Interpretation
Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of any clause. Where a clause conflicts with the Summary of Benefits, this document controls. All dollar amounts are stated in United States dollars.

§2.1 Eligibility
An employee of the sponsoring firm who is customarily scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week is eligible for coverage. Eligibility begins after a 90-day waiting period measured from the first day of active employment. Seasonal and contract workers are not eligible.

§2.2 Dependent coverage
A Covered Employee may enroll a spouse or registered domestic partner and dependent children up to age 26. New dependents must be reported within 31 days of the qualifying event. A dependent gaining coverage by birth is covered from the moment of birth if reported within the 31-day window.

§2.3 Open enrollment and special enrollment
Open enrollment runs each November 1 through November 30 for coverage effective January 1. Outside that window, enrollment is permitted only within 31 days of a qualifying event such as marriage, birth, or involuntary loss of other coverage. Late enrollees who miss the 31-day deadline must wait for the next open enrollment period.

§3.1 Benefits schedule
The Plan pays 80 percent of Negotiated Rates for in-network Covered Services after the Deductible, which is $1,500 per Covered Person per Plan Year, capped at $3,000 per family. Out-of-network Covered Services are paid at 60 percent of usual and customary charges after a separate $3,000 Deductible.

§3.2 Physician services
Primary care visits require a $25 Copayment and specialist visits require a $50 Copayment, with no Deductible applied. Preventive services, including annual physicals and immunizations, are covered at 100 percent in network with no Copayment. Telehealth visits carry a $15 Copayment.

§3.3 Hospital and emergency benefits
Inpatient hospital stays are covered up to 60 days per confinement, subject to a $250 per day copay for the first five days. Emergency room visits require a $150 Copayment, waived if the visit results in a direct hospital admission. Ambulance transport to the nearest appropriate facility is covered at 90 percent.

§3.4 Prescription drugs
Generic drugs carry a $10 Copayment, preferred brand drugs a $40 Copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a $75 Copayment. A 90-day supply at retail costs two times the 30-day Copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.2.

§3.5 Mental health and maternity
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at the same cost sharing as §3.2, limited to 30 visits per Plan Year. Inpatient mental health care is covered up to 30 days per Plan Year. Maternity care is covered the same as any other condition, with a $500 flat copay per admission for delivery.

§3.6 Dental and vision riders
A voluntary dental rider pays 80 percent of Eligible Expenses up to a $1,500 annual maximum, with a $50 separate Deductible. A vision rider covers one eye examination and one pair of corrective lenses per Plan Year with a $20 Copayment. These riders are not included in base coverage.

§4.1 Annual limits and general exclusions
Out-of-pocket costs for in-network services are capped at $6,000 per Covered Person per Plan Year. Cosmetic surgery is excluded unless required to repair an injury or a congenital defect. Weight loss programs, cosmetic dental bleaching, and over-the-counter drugs without a prescription are excluded.

§4.2 Exclusions continued
Services rendered before the effective date or after the termination date of coverage are excluded. Experimental treatments not generally accepted by the medical community are excluded, except that off-label use of an approved drug is covered when supported by recognized clinical literature. Injuries sustained during paid professional athletics are excluded.

§4.3 Pre-existing conditions
The Plan imposes no pre-existing condition exclusion, except that pregnancy within the first 60 days of a Covered Employee's coverage is subject to a 60-day waiting period. This exception does not apply to newborns covered under §2.2. After the waiting period, pregnancy is covered without restriction.

§5.1 Prior approval requirements
Inpatient admissions, MRI and CT scans, and any procedure expected to exceed $2,500 require prior approval from the Plan administrator. The administrator must respond within 5 business days of receiving complete documentation. Services rendered without required prior approval are reduced by 50 percent, except in a medical emergency.

§5.2 Prior approval exceptions and specialty drugs
Emergency admissions must be reported to the administrator within 48 hours or the next business day, whichever is later. Specialty drugs listed in the formulary require prior approval before the first fill only. Continuing treatment previously approved need not be reapproved within the same Plan Year unless the dosage changes.

§5.3 Notice deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service; claims received later are denied without appeal rights. Written notice of intent to appeal must be filed within 180 days of the denial notice. Coverage changes reported under §2.2 must be submitted within the 31-day window described there.

§6.1 Cost sharing rules
Cost sharing amounts are due at the time of service and may not be billed later by a Provider. Copayments do not count toward the Deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum described in §4.1. A Covered Person reaching the out-of-pocket maximum pays no further cost sharing for in-network services that Plan Year.

§6.2 Coordination of benefits
If a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays second for the employee and first for dependents when the other plan is the employee's own. Overpayments must be refunded to the Plan within 60 days of notice. The Plan will not pay more than it would have paid as primary payer.

§7.1 Claims administration
Claims should be submitted on a standard claim form within the deadline in §5.3. The administrator must pay or deny a claim within 30 days of receipt, or within 72 hours for urgent care claims. A denial notice must state the specific reason and the clause relied upon.

§7.2 Appeals
A first-level appeal must be filed within 180 days of denial and will be decided by a reviewer who did not participate in the original denial, within 30 days of receipt. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first appeal decision and is decided within 45 days. Exhaustion of both appeal levels is required before any external review.

§7.3 Administration and termination
The Plan is administered by the sponsoring firm through its appointed administrator. Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment ends, except that a Covered Employee may continue coverage for 18 months by paying the full premium plus a 2 percent administrative charge. The Plan may amend benefits at the start of any Plan Year with 60 days advance written notice.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: DriveSafe Auto Shield 3000

§1.1 Definitions
The term "Covered Vehicle" means the private passenger automobile identified in the schedule attached to this policy. The term "Named Insured" means the individual listed on the declarations page as the primary policyholder. The term "Occurrence" means a single accident or event resulting in loss covered under this policy.

§1.2 Eligibility
Coverage is available to individuals who hold a valid driver's license and reside within the service territory. Vehicles must be registered for personal use and not used for commercial delivery or rideshare purposes. Applicants must pass a synthetic risk assessment administered at enrollment.

§1.3 Waiting Period
Coverage for collision losses begins thirty days after the effective date of the policy. Liability coverage begins immediately at the effective date. No waiting period applies to roadside assistance benefits described in §2.3.

§2.1 Liability Coverage
The policy will pay damages for bodily injury and property damage for which the Named Insured becomes legally responsible arising from the use of a Covered Vehicle. The limit is fifty thousand dollars per person and one hundred thousand dollars per Occurrence for bodily injury. The property damage limit is twenty-five thousand dollars per Occurrence.

§2.2 Collision and Comprehensive
Collision coverage pays for damage to the Covered Vehicle from contact with another object, subject to a five hundred dollar deductible per Occurrence. Comprehensive coverage pays for theft, fire, glass damage, and animal strikes, subject to a two hundred fifty dollar deductible. Glass-only repair is paid with no deductible.

§2.3 Roadside Assistance
The policy provides up to three roadside assistance dispatches per policy year. Each dispatch covers towing up to fifty miles, battery jump, tire change, and fuel delivery up to two gallons. Dispatches require prior approval through the administrator's automated line.

§3.1 Exclusions
Coverage does not apply to loss arising from intentional acts, racing, or operation of the Covered Vehicle by an unlicensed driver. Exclusion for commercial use does not apply to occasional volunteer errand driving up to four hours per week. Loss caused by wear and tear or mechanical breakdown is excluded regardless of other provisions.

§3.2 Excluded Drivers
Any driver with a suspension in the thirty-six months before enrollment is excluded from coverage. The Named Insured may request removal of an excluded driver after twenty-four months of clean driving record. Removal requires underwriter approval as described in §5.2.

§4.1 Notice Requirements
The Named Insured must report any Occurrence within seven days of learning of it. Late notice may reduce the claim payment by ten percent unless the delay was reasonable. Notice of a total theft must be given within twenty-four hours and confirmed to local authorities.

§4.2 Prior Approval
Repairs exceeding one thousand dollars require prior written approval from the claims administrator. Emergency repairs needed to make the vehicle safe to drive may proceed without approval, but itemized invoices must be submitted within fourteen days. Rental vehicle benefits of up to thirty dollars per day for a maximum of ten days require approval under this section.

§5.1 Claims Administration
Claims must be filed using the administrator's designated claim form with supporting estimates. The administrator will acknowledge receipt within three business days and issue a decision within twenty days. Payment is issued within ten business days of a decision.

§5.2 Appeals
A claimant may appeal an adverse decision within thirty days of the decision date. Appeals are reviewed by a separate synthetic review unit that did not handle the original claim. A final appeal decision must be issued within forty-five days, and the decision is binding under this policy.

§5.3 Premium Adjustments
Premiums are payable in twelve monthly installments of the amount shown on the declarations page. A late payment grace period of ten days applies before suspension of coverage. A surcharge of twenty percent applies after two at-fault Occurrences within a policy year.

§6.1 General Provisions
This policy is a synthetic document created solely for software demonstration purposes. It confers no real coverage and no premium is due. All references to dollar amounts, deadlines, and limits are fictional test data.

SYNTHETIC
Zorblife Short-Term Flex Medical Plan (Demo Edition)

§1.1 Definitions
The term "Covered Person" means an individual whose enrollment has been accepted under this plan and whose premium payments are current. "Eligible Expense" means a charge for a covered service that is reasonable, customary, and billed by a licensed provider. The "Benefit Year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the effective date shown on the enrollment confirmation.

§1.2 Eligibility
Applicants must be between 18 and 64 years old and lawfully resident in the demonstration jurisdiction. Enrollment is not available to persons already enrolled in any other medical plan, and no evidence of insurability is required. Coverage may not be renewed more than twice, for a maximum total duration of 270 days.

§1.3 Waiting Period
Coverage for illness begins on the fifteenth day after the effective date. Coverage for accidental injury begins immediately on the effective date. Preventive services described in §2.1 begin on the effective date without any waiting period.

§2.1 Preventive Benefits
The plan pays 100 percent of the allowed amount for one annual wellness examination per Benefit Year, up to 200 dollars. One routine vision screening and one basic blood panel per Benefit Year are also covered at 100 percent. Services beyond these limits are subject to the cost sharing described in §2.2.

§2.2 Physician and Hospital Benefits
Covered physician visits are paid at 80 percent of the allowed amount after the Covered Person satisfies a 150 dollar calendar deductible. Inpatient hospital stays are covered at 70 percent of the allowed amount for up to 30 days per Benefit Year. Emergency room visits are paid at 80 percent without deductible, provided the visit is not excluded under §4.2.

§2.3 Prescription Benefits
Generic prescriptions are covered at 75 percent, preferred brand-name drugs at 50 percent, and non-preferred brand-name drugs are excluded. A 30-day supply limit applies per fill, and no more than 12 fills per Benefit Year are covered. Specialty drugs, including injectable biologics, are excluded entirely.

§3.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for any inpatient admission, any imaging study exceeding 500 dollars, and any surgical procedure. Requests must be submitted at least five business days before the service, except in emergencies where notice within 48 hours after the service is sufficient. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces the payable benefit by 50 percent, as applied before the cost sharing in §2.2.

§3.2 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of a claim must be received within 90 days of the date of service. If notice is not reasonably possible within that period, it must be given as soon as practicable and in no event later than 365 days. Claims for services excluded under §4.1 need not be noticed.

§3.3 Cost Sharing Administration
The deductible applies once per Benefit Year and is not pro-rated for partial years. Copayments and coinsurance amounts do not accrue toward the deductible. The total out-of-pocket maximum is 5,000 dollars per Covered Person per Benefit Year, after which covered services are paid at 100 percent of the allowed amount.

§4.1 General Exclusions
The plan does not cover pre-existing conditions, defined as any condition for which advice, diagnosis, or treatment was received during the 24 months preceding the effective date. Cosmetic services, dental care, and routine maternity care are excluded. An exception applies where a pre-existing condition has remained untreated and symptom-free for 12 consecutive months, after which it is treated as a new condition.

§4.2 Specific Exclusions
Injuries sustained while the Covered Person is operating a motor vehicle without a valid license are excluded, as are self-inflicted injuries and injuries arising from amateur or professional athletic competition. Emergency room visits that are not attributable to a sudden, unexpected condition are excluded. Substance use disorder treatment and experimental procedures are excluded without exception.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted on the plan's standard claim form within 90 days of the date of service, consistent with the notice deadline in §3.2. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt. Incomplete claims will be rejected with a written statement of the missing information.

§5.2 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal an adverse benefit determination within 180 days of the explanation of payment. Appeals are reviewed by a reviewer who was not involved in the original determination, and a decision is issued within 60 days. A second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first-level decision, and its outcome is final.

§5.3 Premiums and Termination
Premiums are due on the first day of each month, with a 10-day grace period. Coverage terminates if premium remains unpaid after the grace period, upon reaching the 270-day maximum duration in §1.2, or upon written request of the Covered Person. No premium refund is issued after the first 10 days of coverage except where the application is declined or rescinded.

§5.4 Identification and Records
Covered Persons will receive a digital confirmation of enrollment that is not an insurance identification card and confers no independent rights. Providers may request verification of coverage, which the administrator will supply in writing within three business days. Records supporting a claim must be retained by the Covered Person for at least one year after the Benefit Year ends.

§5.5 Administrative Authority
The plan administrator has discretionary authority to interpret the terms of this document and resolve factual disputes. No agent or provider may alter these terms orally. This plan is a synthetic demonstration document and provides no actual coverage of any kind.

§5.6 Governing Construction
Headings are for convenience and do not affect interpretation. If any clause is held unenforceable, the remaining clauses continue in effect. Cross-references, including those in §3.1 and §3.2, refer to clauses as they appear in this edition and are not affected by future revisions.

SYNTHETIC
Fictional Demo Plan: Horizon Flex Silver 700 Sample Policy

§1.1 Definitions
In this sample policy, "plan" means the Horizon Flex Silver 700 Sample Policy issued for demonstration purposes only. "Covered person" means an enrollee and any dependent enrolled under the same contract. "Plan year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the first day of the month in which coverage takes effect.

§1.2 Eligibility
An applicant must reside in the fictional service area and be at least eighteen years of age to enroll as a primary member. Dependents may be covered until the end of the month in which they turn twenty-six, except that a dependent who is permanently disabled before that age may remain enrolled indefinitely. Enrollment is effective on the first day of the month following approval of the application.

§1.3 Waiting Periods
Coverage for non-preventive services begins after a thirty-day waiting period from the effective date. No waiting period applies to preventive care, emergency services, or accidental injury treatment. Maternity benefits are subject to a ninety-day waiting period unless the enrollee had creditable coverage within the previous sixty days.

§2.1 Preventive Benefits
The plan pays one hundred percent of allowed charges for in-network preventive services, including annual physical examinations, immunizations, and routine screenings listed in the plan's schedule. One preventive dental cleaning per covered person per plan year is covered up to one hundred twenty dollars. Out-of-network preventive services are covered at fifty percent after the deductible.

§2.2 Physician and Hospital Benefits
Primary care visits are covered with a twenty-dollar copayment, and specialist visits require a fifty-dollar copayment. Inpatient hospital stays are covered at eighty percent after the deductible, limited to ninety days per plan year. Emergency room visits are covered at one hundred percent, with a two-hundred-fifty-dollar copayment waived if the visit results in inpatient admission.

§2.3 Prescription Benefits
Generic drugs carry a ten-dollar copayment, preferred brand drugs a forty-dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs seventy-five dollars per thirty-day supply. A ninety-day supply at a network pharmacy is available for two and one-half times the thirty-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §4.1.

§3.1 Deductibles and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual deductible is three thousand dollars per covered person and six thousand dollars per family, except that copayments for physician visits and prescriptions apply without satisfying the deductible. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is six thousand five hundred dollars per person and thirteen thousand dollars per family. Once the out-of-pocket maximum is reached, the plan pays one hundred percent of covered in-network services for the remainder of the plan year.

§3.2 Lifetime and Annual Limits
No lifetime dollar limit applies to essential health benefits. Annual rehabilitation services are limited to thirty combined physical, occupational, and speech therapy visits per plan year. Home health care is limited to sixty visits per plan year, and skilled nursing facility care is limited to one hundred days per lifetime, with each stay beyond thirty days requiring recertification.

§3.3 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, weight loss surgery without documented medical necessity, fertility treatment beyond one diagnostic cycle, and experimental or investigational procedures. Dental and vision care for adults is excluded except as described in §2.1. Exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following trauma, infection, or congenital anomalies that restore normal body function.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Certain services require prior approval from the plan's utilization review department, including inpatient admissions, imaging such as magnetic resonance scans, specialty drugs, and durable medical equipment exceeding one thousand dollars in value. Requests must be submitted by the treating provider at least five business days before scheduled services. Approval is valid for sixty days from the date of issuance.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Enrollees must notify the plan of hospital admissions within seventy-two hours, or by the next business day when the admission occurs on a weekend. Notice of a change of address, dependent status, or other eligibility event must be given within thirty days. Failure to provide timely notice may reduce benefits by up to twenty-five percent but never results in denial of otherwise covered emergency care.

§5.1 Cost Sharing Administration
Copayments and coinsurance are due at the time of service for in-network providers. The plan will apply payments first to the deductible, then to coinsurance, in the order that benefits the covered person. Refunds of overpayments are issued within forty-five days of discovery and credited against future cost sharing as described in §3.1.

§5.2 Claims Submission
Providers generally submit claims directly to the plan within ninety days of service. Covered persons who pay out of pocket may submit a claim on the plan's standard form within one hundred eighty days of the date of service. Claims for out-of-network emergency services are processed at in-network benefit levels as described in §2.2.

§5.3 Claims Decisions
The plan will pay or deny claims within thirty days of receipt of a clean claim. Denials must state the specific reason, the plan provision relied upon, and the covered person's appeal rights. Partial payments may be issued when documentation is incomplete, with the balance payable within thirty days after the missing information is received.

§5.4 Appeals
A covered person may appeal an adverse claim decision within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice. The plan must issue a first-level appeal decision within thirty days, and a second-level decision by an independent reviewer within forty-five days of a second-level request. Exhaustion of the appeal process described in this section is required before pursuing external review.

§6.1 Termination and Continuation
Coverage terminates at the end of a month in which premiums remain unpaid after the thirty-one-day grace period. A covered person may voluntarily terminate coverage effective the first day of any month upon thirty days written notice. Dependents who lose eligibility due to age as described in §1.2 may continue coverage for up to eighteen additional months by paying the full group rate.

§6.2 Plan Administration
The plan is administered by a fictional administrative office maintained solely for this demonstration. Premiums are due on the first day of each month, and coverage will not be retroactively canceled except for fraud or intentional misrepresentation. Any amendment to this policy requires thirty days written notice to enrollees and takes effect only at the start of a plan year unless more favorable to covered persons.

DemoShield Personal Auto Plan (Sample Only — For Software Demonstration)

§1.1 Definitions
As used in this demonstration policy, "covered auto" means the fictional vehicle listed on the sample declarations page. "Collision" means contact between the covered auto and another object, as described in §3.1. "Premium" means the fictional monthly amount shown in the demo, set at 92 dollars.

§1.3 Effective Dates

§2.1 Liability Benefits

§2.2 Medical Benefits

§5.1 Claims Administration

§5.2 Appeals

§5.3 Policy Administration
The demo insurer may non-renew this synthetic plan only with 60 days of simulated notice, except for nonpayment of the fictional premium in §1.3, which requires 10 days notice. Changes to limits under §2.1 take effect only at renewal. This policy is a fabrication and provides no actual coverage.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: Quantum Shield HDHP Option Zeta (Demo Plan)

§1.1 Definitions
The term "covered person" means an individual enrolled under this plan who has satisfied the eligibility rules in §1.2. The term "network provider" means a provider who has a contractual relationship with the demonstration network described in §2.1. The term "allowed amount" means the maximum dollar figure the plan recognizes for a given service, which shall not exceed 130 percent of the demonstration fee schedule.

§1.2 Eligibility
An individual may enroll if the account is registered in the demo system and a simulated enrollment event has been triggered. Coverage begins on the first day of the simulated month following a waiting period of 30 synthetic days. Enrollment changes caused by a simulated qualifying event must be recorded within 31 demo days of the event.

§1.3 Plan Year
The plan year runs from the first simulated day of January through the last simulated day of December. Deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, and visit limits reset at the start of each plan year. Any reference to a year elsewhere in this document means the plan year as defined here.

§2.1 Network Access
Covered persons may use any provider in the demonstration network without a referral. Services rendered outside the network are reimbursed at the out-of-network levels described in §4.2. If no network provider is available within 50 simulated miles for a required service, out-of-network costs are processed at network levels as an exception under §5.3.

§2.2 Primary Care Visits
Covered persons receive up to 12 primary care visits per plan year that are payable before the deductible is met. Visits beyond the twelfth are subject to the full deductible. Each visit is reimbursed at 100 percent of the allowed amount up to a cap of 180 demo dollars per visit.

§2.3 Specialist Visits
Specialist visits are subject to the deductible and then paid at 80 percent in network and 60 percent out of network. A specialist visit requires a simulated referral recorded in the demo system, except for visits to behavioral health providers as described in §3.2. The plan covers no more than 24 specialist visits per plan year.

§3.1 Preventive Services
Preventive services on the demonstration preventive list are covered at 100 percent with no deductible, limited to one occurrence per service per plan year. Preventive services rendered out of network are paid at 70 percent of the allowed amount. Preventive care that becomes diagnostic during the same visit is split-billed, with the diagnostic portion subject to the deductible under §4.1.

§3.2 Behavioral Health
In-network outpatient behavioral health visits are covered at 90 percent after deductible, with no visit limit for the first 20 visits per plan year. Visits 21 through 40 are paid at 80 percent, and visits beyond 40 require prior approval under §5.1. Inpatient behavioral health stays are limited to 45 days per plan year, with days beyond that covered only under the exception process in §5.3.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
Prescription drugs are tiered as follows: tier one at 15 demo dollars, tier two at 45 demo dollars, tier three at 30 percent coinsurance, and specialty tier at 25 percent coinsurance with a 250 demo dollar per-fill maximum. Drug copays do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum described in §4.3. A 90-day supply is available for tier one and tier two drugs at three times the 30-day cost.

§4.1 Deductible
The in-network deductible is 1,650 demo dollars per covered person and 3,300 demo dollars per simulated family per plan year. The out-of-network deductible is 3,000 demo dollars per covered person. Amounts applied to the in-network deductible do not reduce the out-of-network deductible, except as allowed under §2.1 for unavailable network providers.

§4.2 Coinsurance
After the deductible is met, the plan pays 80 percent of the allowed amount in network and 60 percent out of network. Emergency services are always paid at the in-network level of 80 percent regardless of provider status, as required by §5.2. Coinsurance rates for preventive services are governed by §3.1.

§4.3 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The in-network out-of-pocket maximum is 4,500 demo dollars per covered person and 9,000 demo dollars per simulated family per plan year. Once the maximum is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of the allowed amount for the remainder of the plan year. Copays, coinsurance, and deductible amounts all count toward the maximum, but amounts above the allowed amount under §1.1 never count.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, imaging studies above 750 demo dollars in allowed amount, and any item on the demonstration prior-approval list. Requests must be submitted in the demo system at least 5 simulated business days before scheduled services or within 48 demo hours for urgent cases. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment by 25 percent but never results in denial of a covered service.

§5.2 Emergency Services
Emergency services are covered without prior approval at the in-network level described in §4.2. A follow-up visit within 72 demo hours of an emergency discharge is processed as part of the emergency episode. Emergency transportation is covered up to 1,200 demo dollars per occurrence.

§5.3 Exceptions and Overrides
A covered person may request an exception to any limit or exclusion in this plan by submitting a simulated exception request through the demo system. Exceptions must be decided within 14 demo days, or 72 demo hours if urgent. Approved exceptions apply for the remainder of the plan year unless the request specified a single occurrence.

§6.1 Exclusions
This plan does not cover cosmetic services, services rendered by an excluded provider list maintained in the demo system, or items already paid by another simulated plan. Exclusions do not apply to reconstructive services following a covered injury, which are paid at the rates in §4.2. Experimental treatments are excluded unless approved under the exception process in §5.3.

§6.2 Limits and Caps
Durable medical equipment is covered up to 2,500 demo dollars per plan year, with rentals counted against the same cap. Physical, occupational, and speech therapy are each limited to 30 combined visits per plan year. Chiropractic care is limited to 12 visits per plan year, after which visits require prior approval under §5.1.

§6.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a covered person has coverage under another simulated plan, this plan pays the difference between its allowed amount and the other plan's payment, up to the full allowed amount. The covered person must report other coverage within 31 demo days of its start. Payments made in error must be returned to the plan within 60 demo days.

§7.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 180 demo days of the date of service, except that claims for services in the final quarter of the plan year may be submitted through the last day of the following plan year. Clean claims are simulated to be processed within 14 demo days. Incomplete claims are returned once with a statement of missing items, and the submission deadline is extended by 30 demo days upon resubmission.

§7.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 demo days of the denial notice. Level one appeals are decided within 30 demo days, and a further level two appeal must be filed within 60 demo days of the level one decision. During an appeal, the covered person may submit additional documentation, and an approved appeal results in simulated reprocessing under §7.1.

§7.3 Notices
All notices under this plan are delivered through the demo messaging system. Notice of a denial must include the reason, the clause relied upon, and instructions for appeal under §7.2. Notice of any change to cost sharing under §4.1, §4.2, or §4.3 is provided at least 60 demo days before it takes effect.

§7.4 Administration
The plan is administered by a simulated administrative engine that applies these clauses in numeric order where conflicts arise. Records of enrollment, claims, and appeals are retained for the duration of the demonstration session only. This document is synthetic and creates no real coverage, obligation, or entitlement of any kind.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Flex PPO 2500 Sample Health Plan

§1.1 Plan Name and Purpose
This document describes the Meridian Flex PPO 2500 Sample Health Plan, a fictional preferred provider organization plan created solely for software demonstration purposes. All terms, amounts, and entities described herein are invented and have no real-world application.

§1.2 Definitions
For purposes of this plan, "Network Provider" means a fictional provider listed in the sample demonstration directory. "Calendar Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each January first. "Covered Person" means an eligible employee or enrolled dependent as described in §2.1. "Medical Necessity" means a service that the plan's fictional review entity determines is appropriate for the demonstrated condition.

§1.3 Plan Administrator
The plan is administered by the fictional administrative entity named in the demonstration materials. All references to notices, claims, and appeals in §§8.1 through 8.3 are directed to that entity.

§2.1 Eligibility
Employees of the fictional demonstration employer are eligible if scheduled to work at least twenty-four hours per week. A waiting period of the first of the month following sixty days of employment applies. Eligible dependents include a fictional spouse and children under age twenty-six.

§2.2 Enrollment Deadlines
A newly eligible person must enroll within thirty-one days of the eligibility date described in §2.1. Late enrollment is permitted only during the fictional annual open enrollment window or within thirty-one days of a qualifying fictional life event.

§2.3 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the employee's fictional employment ends. Dependent coverage ends when the dependent no longer meets the criteria in §2.1.

§3.1 Cost Sharing Overview
The plan pays eighty percent of Network Provider charges and sixty percent of out-of-network charges after the deductible described in §3.2. In-network preventive care is covered at one hundred percent with no deductible, as described in §4.1.

§3.2 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual deductible is 2,500 fictional currency units per person and 5,000 per family. The annual out-of-pocket limit is 6,500 per person and 13,000 per family; once reached, the plan pays one hundred percent of covered services for the remainder of the Calendar Year.

§3.3 Copayments
A 30-unit copayment applies to each Network Provider office visit, and a 75-unit copayment applies to each fictional urgent care visit. Copayments do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket limit in §3.2.

§3.4 Prescription Drug Benefits
Generic drugs carry a 15-unit copayment, preferred brand drugs a 40-unit copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs a 75-unit copayment. A ninety-day supply of maintenance medication is available at three times the retail copayment through the fictional mail-order channel.

§4.1 Covered Services
Covered services include physician visits, hospital care, emergency services, maternity care, mental health services, physical therapy, and preventive screenings. Preventive services are covered at one hundred percent in network, consistent with §3.1.

§4.2 Mental Health and Substance Use
In-network outpatient mental health visits are covered at a 30-unit copayment, with a limit of forty visits per Calendar Year. Inpatient substance use treatment is covered for up to thirty days per Calendar Year and is subject to the prior approval rule in §5.1.

§4.3 Emergency Services
Emergency room services are covered at a 250-unit copayment, waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient within twenty-four hours. Emergency care is covered at the in-network level regardless of provider network status.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Certain services, including inpatient admissions, imaging exceeding 1,500 units in cost, and the treatments referenced in §4.2, require prior approval from the fictional review entity at least five business days before the service. Emergency admissions must be reported within forty-eight hours or the next business day.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines for Claims
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service. Proof of loss documentation must be provided within sixty days of a request from the administrator described in §1.3.

§6.1 Limits
The plan limits physical therapy to thirty visits per Calendar Year, chiropractic care to twenty visits, and speech therapy to twenty visits. Durable medical equipment is covered up to 4,000 units per Calendar Year.

§6.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, dental care for persons over age nineteen, vision hardware, and weight-loss surgery unless the person has a documented body mass index above forty and completes a six-month supervised program. Services related to injuries arising from fictional war or armed conflict are also excluded.

§6.3 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident is not excluded under §6.2, provided it occurs within twelve months of the accident. Dental care is covered when required to treat a accidental injury to sound natural teeth, subject to the claims rules in §5.2.

§7.1 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under another fictional plan, this plan pays the excess of its normal benefit over the amount payable by the primary plan. Determination of primary status follows the standard fictional ordering rules described in the demonstration materials.

§7.2 Subrogation
If a Covered Person recovers damages for an injury for which the plan paid benefits, the plan has the right to recover up to the amount paid. The Covered Person must notify the administrator within thirty days of any settlement or judgment.

§8.1 Claims Submission and Payment
Claims should be submitted on the fictional claim form or through the demonstration portal. The administrator will pay or deny a claim within thirty days of receipt; if additional time is needed, written notice of extension will be provided.

§8.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days by submitting a written appeal to the administrator described in §1.3. The appeal will be reviewed by a fictional reviewer independent of the original decision, and a written decision will be issued within sixty days.

§8.3 External Review
If an appeal under §8.2 is denied, the Covered Person may request fictional external review within sixty days of the denial notice. The external reviewer's decision is final for purposes of this demonstration plan.

SYNTHETIC
DemoCare Pet Protection Plan — "PawShield Premier"

§1.1 Definitions
"Insured Pet" means the dog or cat named on the enrollment record, aged between eight weeks and fourteen years at the time of enrollment. "Veterinarian" means any licensed animal health practitioner, including specialists and emergency clinics. "Benefit Year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the policy effective date and each anniversary thereafter.

§1.2 Eligibility
Coverage is available to any resident of a participating region who owns a dog or cat meeting the age criteria in §1.1. Pets with a terminal diagnosis at the time of application are not eligible, though pets with managed chronic conditions may enroll subject to the exclusions in §3.4. Enrollment must be completed before the pet's fifteenth birthday for renewal to continue.

§1.3 Waiting Periods
Accident coverage begins five days after the effective date. Illness coverage begins fourteen days after the effective date. Coverage for orthopedic conditions, including hip dysplasia and ligament tears, begins six months after the effective date unless the pet passed a qualifying orthopedic examination within thirty days before enrollment.

§2.1 Accident Benefit
The plan pays eighty-five percent of eligible accident expenses after the annual deductible. Covered accidents include fractures, lacerations, toxin ingestion, and foreign object removal. The annual accident benefit maximum is twelve thousand dollars.

§2.2 Illness Benefit
The plan pays eighty percent of eligible illness expenses after the annual deductible. Covered illnesses include infections, digestive disorders, cancers, and chronic conditions such as diabetes. The annual illness benefit maximum is ten thousand dollars, shared with the accident maximum as described in §2.1 only where a single event has both accident and illness components.

§2.3 Wellness Rider
An optional wellness rider reimburses up to four hundred fifty dollars per benefit year for routine care, including two vaccinations at up to seventy-five dollars each, one dental cleaning at up to two hundred dollars, and one wellness examination at up to one hundred dollars. Wellness reimbursements are not subject to the deductible or the coinsurance in §2.4.

§2.4 Cost Sharing
The annual deductible is two hundred fifty dollars per pet, payable once per benefit year. After the deductible, the coinsurance percentages in §2.1 and §2.2 apply. A premium discount of five percent applies for each additional pet, capped at fifteen percent total.

§3.1 Pre-Existing Conditions
Conditions that first appeared or showed symptoms before the effective date or during the waiting periods in §1.3 are excluded. However, a pre-existing condition that has been symptom-free and untreated for eighteen consecutive months becomes eligible for coverage, provided the pet undergoes an examination confirming the remission. Bilateral conditions, such as cruciate ligament disease, are treated as one condition if either side showed symptoms before enrollment.

§3.2 Excluded Treatments
Cosmetic procedures, tail docking, ear cropping, declawing, and breeding-related services are excluded. Experimental treatments and cloning services are excluded. Breathing surgery for flat-faced breeds is excluded unless the condition first appeared after the effective date and was not noted in the enrollment examination.

§3.3 Behavioral and Dental Limits
Behavioral therapy is covered at up to six sessions per benefit year and six hundred dollars total, only when prescribed by a Veterinarian. Dental illness treatment is covered only when the pet received a dental examination in each of the two preceding benefit years, as described in §2.3 or through a comparable preventive visit.

§3.4 Chronic Condition Caps
Chronic conditions, including epilepsy, arthritis, and kidney disease, carry a lifetime maximum of twenty-five thousand dollars per condition. Once a lifetime cap is reached, related expenses shift entirely to the policyholder, though unrelated conditions remain covered under §2.2.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Expenses exceeding one thousand five hundred dollars in a single course of treatment require prior approval. Requests are decided within two business days when submitted through the standard channel, or within four hours for emergency cases. Failure to obtain required prior approval reduces reimbursement by twenty percentage points but does not deny the claim outright.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of treatment. A pet's death must be reported within thirty days to process any refund of unearned premium. Changes in the pet's residence must be reported within sixty days, as coverage territories affect the provider network described in §4.4.

§4.3 Claim Documentation
Each claim must include an itemized invoice, the diagnosis, and the treatment dates. The plan may request complete medical records, which the treating clinic must supply within fourteen days of the request. Claims missing documentation are held open for sixty days before denial.

§4.4 Network and Out-of-Network
There is no restricted network, and any licensed Veterinarian qualifies under §1.1. Out-of-network reimbursement is reduced by ten percentage points of coinsurance only where the plan has negotiated rates with an in-network clinic. Emergency treatment anywhere is always reimbursed at in-network rates.

§5.1 Premium Administration
Premiums are due on the first day of each coverage month. A grace period of ten days applies before lapse. Reinstatement after lapse requires a new fourteen-day illness waiting period, but the accident waiting period in §1.3 does not restart.

§5.2 Claim Decisions
Claims are decided within ten business days of complete submission. Approved amounts are paid by electronic transfer within five business days of the decision. Partial approvals are issued with a written explanation of any reduced line items.

§5.3 Appeals
A denied or reduced claim may be appealed within one hundred eighty days by submitting additional records or a letter from the treating Veterinarian. A first appeal is reviewed by a different adjuster within fifteen business days. A second and final appeal is reviewed by an independent veterinary reviewer within thirty business days, and that decision is binding except where law provides otherwise.

§5.4 Dispute Resolution
If disputes remain after the appeal process in §5.3, the parties agree to mediation before any litigation. Mediation costs are shared equally. This policy is administered under the rules of the fictional demonstration jurisdiction and exists solely for software testing.

§4.1 Benefit Limits

§4.2 Extended Stay Exception
If an inpatient stay beyond 120 demo days is certified as medically necessary by the fictional review entity, up to 30 additional demo days are covered. This exception may be used once per Plan Year.

§4.3 Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures, experimental treatments, dental care, vision correction, and services rendered outside the demo network are excluded. Exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or to emergency services under §3.3 obtained outside the network.

§4.4 Annual Maximum
Total plan payments are capped at 500,000 demo dollars per Covered Student per Plan Year. Amounts applied toward the deductible do not count against this maximum.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
The annual deductible is 500 demo dollars per Covered Student and 1,000 demo dollars per family. After the deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of allowed amounts except where §3.2 or §5.2 states otherwise.

§5.2 Copayments
Primary care visits carry a 20 demo dollar copayment and specialist visits a 45 demo dollar copayment, payable at the time of service. Copayments do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§5.3 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The out-of-pocket maximum is 4,000 demo dollars per student and 8,000 demo dollars per family per Plan Year. Once reached, the plan pays 100 percent of Covered Services for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§5.4 Premiums
The synthetic monthly premium is 180 demo dollars for a student alone and 410 demo dollars for student plus dependents. Premiums are due by the fifth demo day of each month.

§6.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, imaging over 750 demo dollars in allowed cost, and all non-preferred brand drugs require prior approval from the fictional review entity. Requests must be recorded at least 5 demo days before the service, except in emergencies.

§6.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be filed within 90 demo days of the date of service. Written notice of any intended appeal must be recorded within 180 demo days of the denial.

§6.3 Claim Processing
Clean claims are adjudicated within 30 demo days of receipt in the demo system. Incomplete claims trigger a synthetic request for information that pauses the processing clock.

§6.4 Appeals
A first-level appeal must be decided within 30 demo days, and a second-level appeal within 45 demo days. A Covered Student may submit up to two levels of appeal per denied claim, and a denied appeal under §4.3 may be resubmitted if new documentation is provided.

§6.5 Coordination of Benefits
If a Covered Student has other fictional coverage, this plan pays secondary except for dependent children, where the parent whose demo birthday falls earlier in the year pays primary. Overpayments identified within 24 demo days may be recovered from future payments.

§7.1 Administration
The plan is administered by the fictional Office of Demo Benefits, which maintains enrollment records, processes claims, and issues synthetic ID credentials. Administrative decisions must be recorded in the test audit log within 10 demo days.

§7.2 Amendments
Amendments to this demo policy take effect on the first demo day of the month following approval. Enrollees receive synthetic notification at least 15 demo days before any change that reduces benefits.

§7.3 Data Nature Statement
Every name, amount, date, and entity in this document is fabricated for software testing. No clause in this document creates real coverage, obligations, or rights of any kind.

SYNTHETIC
Medigap Demo Plan Zephyr-7 (Illustrative Only)

§1.1 Purpose of This Document
This document is a synthetic sample created solely for software demonstration. It describes no real insurer, plan, or coverage. All figures are invented and have no legal effect.

§1.2 Definitions
"Eligible expense" means a charge for a covered service that does not exceed the demo fee schedule. "Benefit year" means the twelve-month period beginning each first of January. "Prior approval" means written consent obtained before a service is rendered, as described in §4.1.

§1.3 Eligibility
A demo enrollee must be at least 65 simulated years old and enrolled in a demo hospital plan. Enrollment is effective on the first day of the month following approval of the demo application. A six-month waiting period applies to pre-existing demo conditions, except that this waiting period is waived if the enrollee held comparable demo coverage within the prior 63 days.

§1.4 Effective Date and Termination
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the effective date and ends at 11:59 p.m. on the termination date. Termination occurs upon nonpayment of the demo premium after a 31-day grace period. Terminated enrollees may reinstate within 90 days by paying all missed demo premiums.

§2.1 Hospital Coinsurance Benefit
The plan pays 100 percent of demo hospital coinsurance for days 61 through 90 of a demo inpatient stay. For demo lifetime reserve days, the plan pays 50 percent of coinsurance, up to 1,200 demo dollars per day. No benefit is payable beyond 90 reserve days.

§2.2 Skilled Nursing Benefit
The plan pays demo skilled nursing coinsurance up to 100 days per benefit year. Days 21 through 100 are paid at 175 demo dollars per day. Care beyond day 100 is excluded, except in the case of a demo terminal condition approved under §4.1.

§2.3 Blood Benefit
The plan pays the first three pints of demo blood each benefit year. Pints four through ten are covered in full. Pints beyond ten are excluded unless replaced by the demo enrollee within 30 days.

§2.4 Part B Coinsurance Benefit
The plan pays 80 percent of eligible expenses for demo outpatient physician services after the 240 demo dollar annual deductible is met. The remaining 20 percent is the enrollee's responsibility, except as provided in §2.5.

§2.5 Excess Charge Benefit
The plan pays 100 percent of demo excess charges above the demo fee schedule, up to a maximum of 5,000 demo dollars per benefit year. Excess charges above this cap are the enrollee's responsibility.

§2.6 Preventive Services Benefit
Demo preventive screenings are covered in full with no cost sharing, up to 4 visits per benefit year. One additional visit is allowed if a screening indicates an abnormal demo result.

§3.1 Excess Charge Cap Exception
If a demo enrollee receives services from a demo participating provider, the cap in §2.5 does not apply and excess charges are paid in full. Participating provider status is determined by the demo administrator.

§3.2 Foreign Travel Emergency Benefit
Emergency care received outside the demo country is covered after a 250 demo dollar deductible. The plan pays 80 percent of eligible expenses up to a lifetime maximum of 50,000 demo dollars. Coverage applies only during the first 60 days of each demo trip.

§3.3 Durable Equipment Benefit
Demo durable equipment is covered at 80 percent after prior approval under §4.1. Rental charges are capped at the demo purchase price. Repairs are covered once per item per benefit year, up to 300 demo dollars.

§3.4 Home Recovery Benefit
Following a covered demo inpatient stay under §2.1, the plan pays up to 1,500 demo dollars for demo home aide visits. Visits are limited to 8 per week for 4 weeks. Custodial-only care is excluded.

§4.1 Prior Approval Rule
Prior approval is required for demo durable equipment under §3.3, demo skilled nursing stays beyond day 60 under §2.2, and any demo service exceeding 2,500 demo dollars. Requests are decided within 14 calendar days. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces the benefit by 50 percent.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Demo enrollees must notify the demo administrator of inpatient admissions within 48 hours, or within 7 days if the enrollee is incapacitated. Claims for out-of-network demo services must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. Late claims are denied, except where the enrollee was incapacitated for the entire filing window.

§4.3 Cost Sharing Summary
Cost sharing consists of the demo deductibles in §2.4 and §3.2, the 20 percent coinsurance in §2.4, and any reduction imposed under §4.1. Demo premiums are due monthly in advance. No cost sharing may be collected for demo preventive services under §2.6.

§4.4 Annual Out-of-Pocket Limit
Total demo enrollee cost sharing is capped at 6,800 demo dollars per benefit year. Once the cap is reached, eligible expenses are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the benefit year. Demo premiums do not count toward the cap.

§4.5 Limits and Exclusions
Excluded are demo cosmetic services, demo dental care, demo vision hardware, demo custodial care, and services received from a demo provider who is the enrollee's immediate family. Exceptions are demo dental care required to treat a demo accident, and demo vision hardware following demo cataract surgery, each covered at 50 percent up to 400 demo dollars per benefit year.

§4.6 Coordination of Benefits
If a demo enrollee holds other demo coverage, this plan pays secondary. Payments made by this plan are reduced so total demo benefits do not exceed eligible expenses. Enrollees must disclose other demo coverage within 30 days of acquiring it.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Demo providers submit claims directly to the demo administrator. Enrollees filing their own claims must use the demo claim form and include itemized demo receipts. Payment is issued within 30 days of a complete claim.

§5.2 Claim Denials
Every demo denial must state the reason, the clause relied upon, and the demo appeal rights. Denials are issued within 30 days of claim receipt. Silence for 45 days is treated as a denial for appeal purposes.

§5.3 Appeals
A demo enrollee may appeal a denial within 180 days of the denial notice. The first-level demo review is decided within 30 days by a reviewer uninvolved in the original denial. A second-level demo hearing may be requested within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided within 45 days.

§5.4 Grievances
Grievances about demo service quality, rather than claim denials under §5.3, may be filed at any time. The demo administrator responds in writing within 30 days. Grievances do not extend any deadline in this document.

§6.1 Administration
The demo administrator maintains all demo enrollment, claim, and appeal records for 7 years. Records are available to the demo enrollee upon written request within 15 business days. No real data may be entered into this synthetic document.

§6.2 Amendments
The demo administrator may amend this document upon 60 days written notice. Amendments may not reduce benefits during a benefit year except as required to preserve demo solvency. Continued demo enrollment after the notice period constitutes acceptance.

§6.3 Governing Interpretation
This document is governed by demo law, which is fictional. Any ambiguity is resolved in favor of the demo enrollee. All headings are for convenience and do not limit the scope of any clause.

SYNTHETIC
Demo University Student Health Plan — "Campus Shield Sample Plan A"

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Student" means a person enrolled as described in §2.1 whose coverage is in active status under this plan. "Medically Necessary Care" means services a Sample Provider determines are required to treat an illness or injury and that meet the standards in §3.2. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each first of September and ending the last day of the following August.

§1.2 Administrator
The plan is administered by a fictional Demo Benefits Office operating only within this software demonstration. The Administrator processes enrollments, maintains records, and coordinates claims review as described in §6.1. All references to the Administrator in this document refer to synthetic demo data only.

§2.1 Eligibility
A student is eligible if enrolled in at least six credit hours per term at the fictional Demo University. Coverage begins on the first day of the term following a waiting period of fourteen days from the date of enrollment. Students enrolled in fewer than six credit hours may apply for an eligibility waiver under §2.3.

§2.2 Dependents
Eligible students may enroll a spouse or domestic partner and dependent children under age nineteen. Dependent enrollment must be requested within thirty-one days of a qualifying life event such as marriage or birth. Dependent coverage terminates on the same date as the student's coverage under §5.1.

§2.3 Waivers
Students with comparable coverage may waive this plan by submitting a waiver form before the tenth day of the term. A waiver remains effective for the full Plan Year and may be revoked only during the annual open enrollment window. Students who lose outside coverage mid-year may enroll within sixty days of that loss, bypassing the waiting period in §2.1.

§3.1 Covered Benefits
The plan covers physician office visits up to twenty visits per Plan Year, paid at eighty percent after the deductible described in §4.1. Inpatient hospital care is covered up to sixty days per Plan Year at ninety percent after deductible. Emergency room visits are covered at one hundred percent for true emergencies as defined in §3.2, or at seventy percent if the visit is later determined non-emergent.

§3.2 Medical Necessity Standard
A service is Medically Necessary Care when it treats a diagnosed condition, is consistent with generally accepted demo clinical guidelines, and is not provided primarily for convenience. Preventive services, including one annual physical and routine immunizations, are exempt from the necessity review and from the deductible under §4.1. Services failing this standard may still be considered under the experimental treatment exception in §5.3.

§3.3 Mental Health Benefits
Outpatient mental health counseling is covered up to thirty sessions per Plan Year at eighty-five percent with no deductible. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered up to thirty days per Plan Year, coordinated with the day limits in §3.1. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms as mental health services, with no separate session cap.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
Each Covered Student pays an annual deductible of two hundred fifty dollars for non-preventive services, except as waived under §3.2. After the deductible, the student pays the coinsurance percentages stated in §3.1 and §3.3. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is three thousand dollars per student and six thousand dollars per family, after which covered services are paid at one hundred percent.

§4.2 Copayments
A copayment of fifteen dollars applies to each covered office visit under §3.1, and a copayment of ten dollars applies to each generic prescription fill. Brand-name prescriptions carry a forty-dollar copayment, with a generic-substitution requirement unless a physician documents medical necessity under §3.2. Copayments do not count toward the deductible in §4.1 but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§5.1 Limits
Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which the student ceases eligibility under §2.1 or graduates. Students on approved medical leave retain coverage for up to ninety additional days, provided the leave documentation is filed within thirty days of the leave start. Termination of coverage does not eliminate pending claims incurred while coverage was active.

§5.2 Exclusions
The plan excludes cosmetic surgery, vision correction, dental care except accident-related repair, and services received outside the demo network without prior approval under §5.4. Injuries sustained during intercollegiate varsity athletics are excluded unless the student purchased the athletics rider during open enrollment. Exclusions do not apply to services required to stabilize an emergency condition as defined in §3.1.

§5.3 Experimental Treatment Exception
Treatments normally excluded as experimental or investigational may be covered when the treating provider certifies in writing that no standard alternative exists and the Administrator grants prior approval. Approved experimental treatments are paid at fifty percent with a per-Plan-Year cap of five thousand dollars. This exception overrides the general exclusion in §5.2 for the approved treatment only.

§5.4 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, MRI and CT imaging, and any service under §5.3 require prior approval from the Administrator at least five business days before the service, or within seventy-two hours after an emergency admission. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment for the service to fifty percent. Approval decisions are issued within three business days of a complete request.

§5.5 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service, and claims received later are denied unless the student shows the delay was reasonable. Written notice of intent to appeal a denial must be filed within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice under §6.2. Students must report changes in eligibility status, such as dropping below the credit threshold in §2.1, within thirty days.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within thirty days of receipt, and students receive an explanation of benefits itemizing amounts applied to the deductible in §4.1. Claims missing documentation are pended once for thirty days while the Administrator requests the missing items. Pended claims that remain incomplete after thirty days are denied and become subject to the appeal process in §6.2.

§6.2 Appeals
A student may appeal a denied claim in two stages: an internal review decided within thirty days, followed by an optional external review by a fictional independent panel decided within forty-five days. The student may submit supporting records at either stage, including new medical necessity documentation under §3.2. A fully favorable appeal result triggers reprocessing of the claim within fifteen days and payment at the applicable coinsurance rate from §3.1.

§6.3 Records and Privacy
The Administrator maintains all demo records in a synthetic database used solely for this software demonstration. No real personal data, real institutions, or live communications exist in connection with this plan. Any resemblance to an actual health plan is coincidental and immaterial to the demo environment.
