SYNTHETIC
Meridian Blue Supplement Plan Zeta-7

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan" means the Meridian Blue Supplement Plan Zeta-7 described in this document. "Base Plan" means the underlying coverage to which this supplement attaches. "Eligible Expense" means a charge for a covered service that is reasonable, customary, and incurred while this Plan is in force.

§1.2 Administrator
The Plan is administered by a synthetic administrative office created solely for demonstration purposes. All references to the Administrator in this document refer to that fictional office. No real entity is associated with this Plan.

§2.1 Eligibility
An applicant must be enrolled in the Base Plan and must have maintained continuous Base Plan coverage for at least six consecutive months before applying. Enrollment is open during the annual window from October 15 through December 7 each year. Applicants outside the window may enroll only if they experience a qualifying event as described in §2.3.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Coverage for pre-existing conditions begins after a three-month waiting period from the effective date. All other covered benefits begin on the effective date. The waiting period is waived for applicants who had comparable supplemental coverage for at least twelve months immediately before applying.

§2.3 Qualifying Events
Qualifying events include relocation outside the prior service area, loss of comparable employer-sponsored supplemental coverage, or termination of a group contract. Notice of a qualifying event must be submitted within 30 days of the event. Coverage resulting from a qualifying event takes effect the first day of the following month.

§3.1 Hospital Benefit
The Plan pays 100 percent of Eligible Expenses for inpatient hospital care for the first 60 days per stay, after the Base Plan has paid its share. For days 61 through 90, the Plan pays $275 per day. There is no lifetime limit on hospital days under this Plan.

§3.2 Skilled Nursing Benefit
The Plan pays the full daily coinsurance for skilled nursing facility care for days 1 through 20 per benefit period, provided the stay meets the criteria in §3.1. For days 21 through 100, the Plan pays $173.50 per day. Stays beyond 100 days are excluded under §4.2.

§3.3 Physician and Outpatient Services
The Plan pays 20 percent of Eligible Expenses for physician services after the Base Plan payment, subject to an annual outpatient deductible of $185. Preventive services are paid at 100 percent with no deductible. Physical therapy is limited to 40 combined visits per calendar year, with exceptions allowed under §4.3.

§3.4 Foreign Travel Emergency
The Plan pays 80 percent of Eligible Expenses for medically necessary emergency care received outside the service area, after a $250 per-trip deductible. The lifetime maximum for this benefit is $55,000. Care must begin during the first 60 days of any trip outside the area.

§4.1 General Exclusions
The Plan does not cover services that are not medically necessary, experimental procedures, cosmetic surgery, or services already paid in full by the Base Plan. Dental care, routine vision, and hearing aids are excluded. Hearing aids are covered only when related to accidental injury, as described in §4.3.

§4.2 Limits and Exceptions
Custodial care, long-term care beyond the limits in §3.2, and private-duty nursing are excluded. Exceptions apply when such services are part of a hospice plan approved under §5.1. Prescription drugs outside a hospital setting are excluded in all cases.

§4.3 Medical Necessity Exceptions
The Administrator may waive a visit limit in §3.3 or an exclusion in §4.1 when a licensed provider certifies that denial would jeopardize recovery. Waiver requests must be filed in writing and are decided within 15 business days. A waiver granted once remains valid for the remainder of the calendar year.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions planned at least 7 days in advance, imaging services exceeding $1,000, and any stay under §3.2. Approval requests must be submitted before the service or within 48 hours in an emergency. Approved services remain approved for 90 days.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Enrollees must notify the Administrator of any hospital admission within 24 hours of admission, or 72 hours if admitted on a weekend. Failure to notify reduces the benefit under §3.1 by 25 percent. Notice requirements are waived for emergency admissions reported by a facility.

§6.1 Cost Sharing
The Plan includes an annual supplement deductible of $320 for Plan Year 2025 and $340 thereafter. After the deductible, cost sharing follows the benefit schedules in §3.1 through §3.4. Total annual out-of-pocket exposure under this Plan is capped at $6,800, excluding amounts excluded under §4.1.

§6.2 Premiums
Premiums are due on the first day of each month, with a 10-day grace period. Coverage lapses if payment is not received by the end of the grace period. Reinstatement within 30 days of lapse requires payment of all arrears and is subject to a new waiting period under §2.2 unless waived.

§7.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. Claims for services already processed by the Base Plan may be submitted by the provider directly. The Administrator pays or denies clean claims within 30 days of receipt.

§7.2 Appeals
A denial may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice. The first-level appeal is decided by a different reviewer within 30 days. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided by an independent reviewer within 45 days, as described in the appeal notice issued under this section.

§7.3 Records and Audit
Enrollees must retain receipts for out-of-pocket claims under §6.1 for three years. The Administrator may audit up to 5 percent of claims annually for verification. Audit findings may adjust payments but may not reduce benefits already paid in good faith.

§7.4 Termination and Administration
The Plan terminates if the Base Plan terminates, upon nonrenewal, or upon the enrollee's written request effective the end of a month. Unused benefits are not transferable. This document is synthetic, generated for software demonstration only, and confers no actual coverage.

Plan Name: NovaShield HD Select 7500

§1.1 Definitions
The term "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each first day of March and ending the last day of February. "Covered Person" means an individual who has satisfied the eligibility requirements of §1.2 and remains enrolled. "In-Network Provider" means any provider holding a current participation agreement with the Plan Administrator at the time services are rendered.

§1.2 Eligibility
An employee of a participating employer is eligible after completing a ninety-day waiting period from the first day of active employment. Dependents may be enrolled within thirty-one days of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, or loss of other coverage. Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which employment ends, subject to the continuation rights described in §4.3.

§1.3 Effective Date
Coverage becomes effective at 12:01 a.m. on the day following completion of the waiting period, provided the completed enrollment form has been received. Late enrollees must wait until the next annual enrollment window, except as provided in §1.2. No coverage exists for services rendered before the effective date.

§2.1 Deductible
The annual deductible is 7,500 dollars per Covered Person and 15,000 dollars per family, and it must be satisfied before most benefits are payable. Covered preventive services described in §2.2 are paid before the deductible is met. The deductible resets at the start of each Plan Year.

§2.2 Preventive Benefits
Annual physical examinations, immunizations, and routine cancer screenings are covered at one hundred percent with no cost sharing when performed by an In-Network Provider. One preventive visit per Covered Person per Plan Year is allowed. Preventive services never reduce or count toward the deductible.

§2.3 Post-Deductible Cost Sharing
After the deductible is satisfied, the Plan pays eighty percent of allowed charges for In-Network services and sixty percent for Out-of-Network services. The Covered Person pays the remaining coinsurance. Prescription drugs are subject to a 500 dollar separate deductible, after which generic drugs carry a 15 dollar copayment and brand-name drugs 45 dollars.

§2.4 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is 8,500 dollars per Covered Person and 17,000 dollars per family. Once reached, the Plan pays one hundred percent of covered In-Network charges for the remainder of the Plan Year. Amounts exceeding allowed charges do not count toward this maximum.

§3.1 Hospital Services
Inpatient hospital stays are covered at the coinsurance rate stated in §2.3, limited to 120 days per Covered Person per Plan Year. Private rooms beyond the semi-private rate are excluded unless medically necessary, as determined under the review process in §3.4. Emergency admissions are exempt from prior approval requirements.

§3.2 Mental Health Services
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at the coinsurance rate in §2.3, limited to 40 visits per Plan Year. Inpatient mental health care is limited to 60 days per Plan Year. Substance use disorder treatment is covered on the same terms and is not subject to any separate lifetime limit.

§3.3 Exclusions
Services that are cosmetic, experimental, or not medically necessary are excluded, except reconstructive surgery following a covered mastectomy, which is covered. Dental and vision care for adults are excluded, except accidental injury to sound natural teeth. Charges incurred outside the United States are covered only for emergency services.

§3.4 Prior Approval
Services exceeding 2,500 dollars in allowed charges, other than emergency care, require prior approval from the Plan Administrator at least five business days before rendering. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces the Plan's payment by twenty-five percent. A determination is issued within fifteen business days of a complete request.

§4.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within ninety days of the date of service; claims received later are denied without further review, except in the case of incapacity as described in §4.2. Covered Persons must use the standardized claim form available from the Plan Administrator. Incomplete claims are returned once with an explanation of deficiencies.

§4.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. The Plan Administrator issues a written decision within thirty days, and a second-level appeal may be filed within sixty days of that decision. Deadlines are extended for Covered Persons who demonstrate incapacity or an emergency preventing timely filing.

§4.3 Continuation of Coverage
A Covered Person whose coverage ends under §1.2 may elect continuation coverage for up to eighteen months by paying the full monthly premium of 620 dollars. Election must be made within sixty days of the termination notice, which is sent within forty-four days of the qualifying event. Continuation coverage ends early upon enrollment in any other group plan.

§4.4 Administration
The Plan Administrator maintains all enrollment records, processes claims under §4.1, and issues an annual summary of benefits each January. Interpretation of ambiguous provisions rests with the Plan Administrator, whose decisions are subject to the appeal process in §4.2. Amendments to this Plan take effect on the first day of the Plan Year following their adoption.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: Zorvex Shield Lite 30-Demo Coverage

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "Covered Person" to mean an individual enrolled under this synthetic demonstration coverage. "Eligible Expense" means a charge for a covered service that is reasonable, customary, and does not exceed the demo schedule amount of 250 dollars per service unless stated otherwise. "Plan Year" means the 30-day demonstration period beginning on the date shown on the sample enrollment card.

§1.2 Purpose of the Plan
This document exists solely to illustrate the structure of a short-term medical plan in a software demonstration. It confers no real coverage and should not be interpreted as an offer of insurance. All dollar amounts, deadlines, and benefit figures are invented for display purposes.

§1.3 Administrative Terms
The word "Administrator" refers to the fictional claims-processing function within the demo platform. "Prior Approval" means written consent recorded in the demo system before a service is rendered. "Notice" means any communication entered into the demo interface by an enrolled user.

§2.1 Eligibility
A person is eligible if they are at least 18 years old, reside in the fictional territory of North Meridia, and complete the sample enrollment screen. Enrollment is denied if the applicant has been hospitalized within the 30 days before applying. Dependents under age 26 may be added at a demo rate of 15 dollars per dependent per Plan Year.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Coverage for illness benefits begins on the 5th day after the effective date. Accident benefits, including treatment of injuries from falls or collisions, begin immediately with no waiting period. Preventive services described in §3.4 also begin immediately.

§2.3 Termination
Coverage ends at 11:59 p.m. on the 30th day of the Plan Year, upon nonpayment of the demo premium of 49 dollars, or upon entry of a termination request by the user. Services rendered after termination are not eligible expenses. A grace period of 5 days applies to premium payment before termination takes effect.

§3.1 Hospital Benefits
The plan pays 1,000 dollars per day for hospital room and board, limited to 10 days per Plan Year. Intensive care is paid at 1,500 dollars per day, limited to 5 days. The combined hospital limit under all subparts is 12,500 dollars per Plan Year.

§3.2 Physician Services
Office visits to a physician are paid at 120 dollars per visit, limited to 6 visits per Plan Year. House calls are paid at 180 dollars per visit and count toward the same 6-visit limit. Surgical procedures performed in a physician's office are paid at 50 percent of the demo schedule amount.

§3.3 Emergency Services
Emergency room treatment for accidents is paid at 300 dollars per occurrence with no visit limit. Emergency room treatment for illness is paid only if the condition meets the definition of emergency in §1.1 and is limited to 2 occurrences per Plan Year. Ambulance charges are paid at 150 dollars per trip, up to 4 trips per Plan Year.

§3.4 Preventive Services
One routine physical examination per Plan Year is paid at 100 dollars. Immunizations are paid at actual cost up to 75 dollars per Plan Year. Preventive benefits are not subject to the waiting period in §2.2.

§3.5 Prescription Benefits
Prescription drugs are paid at 50 percent of cost up to 200 dollars per Plan Year. Generic drugs receive an additional 10 percent of reimbursement. Controlled substances in demo schedule category F require Prior Approval as described in §4.1.

§4.1 Prior Approval Rules
Prior Approval is required for hospital admissions that are not emergencies, surgical procedures exceeding 500 dollars, and category F prescriptions. The Administrator must respond within 2 demo business days. Services rendered without required Prior Approval are reduced by 50 percent, except where the delay would have endangered the Covered Person.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service. Written notice of intent to appeal a denied claim must be entered within 60 days of the denial. Late claims are denied, except that claims submitted within 180 days are paid at 75 percent if the delay resulted from documented incapacity.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
A deductible of 100 dollars per Plan Year applies to all benefits except preventive services under §3.4 and accident-related emergency services under §3.3. After the deductible, the plan pays at the levels stated in Article 3. The Covered Person bears any amount above the demo schedule amount.

§5.2 Out-of-Pocket Maximum
The Covered Person's total out-of-pocket amount is capped at 2,000 dollars per Plan Year. Once the cap is reached, the plan pays 100 percent of Eligible Expenses for the remainder of the Plan Year. The cap does not include the demo premium or amounts above the schedule.

§6.1 Exclusions
The plan does not cover pre-existing conditions, cosmetic procedures, dental care except accidental injury to sound natural teeth, or injuries sustained while participating in professional athletics. Experimental treatments are excluded. Substance use disorder treatment is excluded, except for one covered detoxification admission of up to 3 days per Plan Year.

§6.2 War and Hazard Exclusions
Losses arising from war, declared or undeclared, nuclear events, or civil insurrection are excluded. Injuries from recreational aviation are excluded unless the Covered Person was a fare-paying passenger. These exclusions do not apply to accidental injuries unrelated to the excluded events.

§7.1 Claims Procedure
Claims are entered through the demo claims screen with the date of service, provider name, and itemized charges. The Administrator adjudicates claims within 10 demo business days. Payment is issued as a simulated entry in the demo ledger, and no real funds are disbursed.

§7.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in two levels within the demo platform. A first-level appeal must be decided within 15 demo business days, and a second-level appeal within 30 days. A claim denied at the second level is final, except that the Covered Person may request a review under §7.3.

§7.3 External Review
If a denial involves a disagreement over medical necessity, the Covered Person may request review by a simulated independent reviewer. The reviewer's decision is binding within the demo environment. The request must be made within 45 days of the second-level decision described in §7.2.

§8.1 Coordination of Benefits
If a Covered Person has other simulated coverage, this plan pays second except when it is the primary plan under the demo ordering rules. Overpayments must be returned to the Administrator within 30 days of notice. This section applies only within the demonstration environment.

§8.2 Subrogation
If a third party is responsible for a covered loss, the plan may recover benefits paid from any settlement the Covered Person receives. The plan's recovery is limited to amounts actually paid under this coverage. The Covered Person must notify the Administrator of any third-party claim within 30 days.

§8.3 Misrepresentation and Recovery
Material misstatements on the enrollment screen may void coverage retroactively to the effective date. Benefits paid in reliance on a misstatement must be returned within 60 days. Fraudulent claims result in termination and forfeiture of remaining demo benefits, except that this does not affect the appeal rights in §7.2.

§9.1 Conformity and Amendments
The Administrator may amend this document at any time during the demonstration by posting a revised version in the platform. Amendments apply only prospectively. No verbal statement modifies the terms of this plan.

§9.2 Governing Fiction
This plan is governed entirely by the rules of the software demonstration in which it appears. Any resemblance to real coverage, real regulation, or real entities is coincidental and unintended. All figures, deadlines, and names are synthetic placeholders.

SYNTHETIC
Quantum Meadow Employee PPO Health Plan (Sample Document for Software Demonstration Only)

§1.1 Definitions
For purposes of this plan, a Covered Service means a medical service or supply that is medically necessary and not listed as excluded in §4.1. The Plan Year begins on the first day of the demonstration month and ends twelve months later. A Network Provider is any provider who has agreed in the simulated provider directory to accept the negotiated fee schedule. In-network means care received from a Network Provider; all other care is out-of-network.

§1.2 Eligibility
Employees of the sponsoring demo employer who are scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous service. Eligible dependents include a lawful spouse and children under age 26. Enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the eligibility date. Late enrollees may join only during the annual open enrollment window.

§2.1 Hospital Benefits
In-network semi-private room and board is covered at 90 percent after the deductible, for up to 120 days per Plan Year. Out-of-network hospital stays are covered at 60 percent and are limited to 60 days per Plan Year. Maternity stays of 48 hours following a vaginal delivery and 96 hours following a cesarean are covered in full.

§2.2 Physician and Office Visits
In-network primary care visits carry a 25 dollar copayment and in-network specialist visits a 50 dollar copayment, with no deductible. Out-of-network visits are reimbursed at 70 percent of the allowed amount after the deductible. Preventive care as defined by the simulated guidelines is covered at 100 percent in network.

§2.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs carry a 10 dollar copayment, preferred brand a 30 dollar copayment, and non-preferred brand a 60 dollar copayment for up to a 30-day supply. A 90-day maintenance supply is available in network for two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1 and are limited to a 12-month supply per drug per Plan Year.

§2.4 Mental Health and Emergency Services
In-network outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent with a 30 visit limit per Plan Year, and inpatient mental health care is limited to 45 days. Emergency room visits carry a 150 dollar copayment, waived if the patient is admitted. Emergency care obtained out of network is paid at the in-network level.

§3.1 Annual Limits and Out-of-Pocket Maximums
The individual deductible is 1,500 dollars in network and 3,000 dollars out of network per Plan Year. The individual out-of-pocket maximum is 6,000 dollars in network and 12,000 dollars out of network; family amounts are double. Copayments under §2.2 do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Once the out-of-pocket maximum is reached, covered services are paid at 100 percent for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§3.2 Lifetime Maximums
The lifetime maximum for all covered benefits is 2,000,000 dollars per covered person. Organ transplant benefits carry a separate lifetime maximum of 500,000 dollars. Once any lifetime maximum is exhausted, no further benefits are payable under this plan for that category.

§4.1 Exclusions
Services that are cosmetic, experimental, or not medically necessary are excluded, except reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or mastectomy, which is covered. Routine vision and dental care are excluded except for pediatric dental up to 1,000 dollars per child per Plan Year. Care received outside the simulated service area is excluded except for emergencies as described in §2.4.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
An exclusion under §4.1 may be waived when the Plan Administrator determines, based on submitted clinical evidence, that the service is proven effective for the specific condition. Weight management counseling is covered when prescribed despite the general exclusion of weight loss programs. Hearing aids are excluded except when required following covered surgery, in which case one pair per ear per 36 months is covered up to 2,500 dollars per aid.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, imaging over 1,000 dollars, and specialty drugs require prior approval submitted at least 5 business days before the service, or within 48 hours for urgent requests. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces payment by 50 percent but does not deny the claim entirely. Approval decisions are issued within 3 business days for standard requests and 1 business day for urgent requests.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible if the delay is beyond the participant's control. Written notice of intent to appeal must be filed within 180 days of the explanation of payment. Changes in dependent status must be reported within 31 days of the event.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within 30 days of receipt, and participants receive an explanation of payment itemizing allowed amounts, payments, and remaining deductible under §3.1. Overpayments may be recovered by offset against future claims payments. Coordination of benefits applies when a participant has other coverage, with this plan paying secondary according to standard ordering rules.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in two levels. Level one review is conducted within 30 days by a reviewer not involved in the original denial. Level two review must be requested within 60 days of the level one decision and is decided within 45 days. External review is available for medical necessity denials after both internal levels are exhausted.

§7.1 Plan Administration
The Plan Administrator retains sole discretionary authority to interpret the plan and determine eligibility for benefits, subject to the appeal rights in §6.2. The administrator may amend or terminate the plan upon 60 days written notice to participants. This document is a fictional sample created solely for software demonstration and confers no actual benefits or rights.

SYNTHETIC
Demo Health Plan for Illustrative Students

§1.1 Definitions
In this plan, "Covered Institution" means any accredited fictional college or university located in the Demo Region. "Medically Necessary Care" means services that a licensed provider determines are required to treat an illness or injury. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each August 1 and ending July 31. "Covered Student" means a person who satisfies the eligibility rules in §2.1.

§1.2 Interpretation
References to a clause number include all sentences within that clause. Where a dollar amount and a percentage limit conflict, the lesser benefit applies. Words in the singular include the plural where context requires. Headings are for convenience only.

§1.3 Governing Documents
This plan is administered by the fictional Demo Administrators office. The plan document, any sample claim forms, and the annual notice constitute the entire synthetic arrangement. Nothing in this demo creates real coverage of any kind.

§2.1 Eligibility
A student is eligible if enrolled for at least six credit hours at a Covered Institution and under age 31. Enrollment must be completed within 30 days of the start of the academic term. Dependents under age 19 may be added within 60 days of a qualifying life event.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees must satisfy a 14-day waiting period before benefits begin, except for care resulting from accidental injury, which is covered from day one. Preventive services described in §3.1 are also exempt from the waiting period. Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which enrollment drops below six credit hours.

§2.3 Continuation
A student who graduates or withdraws may continue coverage for up to 90 days by paying the monthly contribution of $180. Continuation does not extend annual limits described in §4.1. Notice of election must be received within 45 days of loss of eligibility.

§3.1 Preventive Services
Annual physical examinations, routine immunizations, and two gynecological visits per Plan Year are covered at 100 percent with no cost sharing. One routine eye examination per Plan Year is covered up to $75. These services are exempt from the deductible and from the waiting period in §2.2.

§3.2 Physician and Clinic Services
Office visits are covered at 80 percent after the student pays a $25 copayment per visit. Visits to urgent care facilities carry a $45 copayment instead. Services obtained outside the Demo Provider Network are covered at 60 percent, as described in §5.2.

§3.3 Hospital and Surgical Benefits
Inpatient hospital care is covered at 80 percent for up to 45 days per Plan Year, with a $250 per-admission deductible. Outpatient surgery is covered at 75 percent with a $150 copayment. A second surgical opinion is required for any non-emergency procedure expected to exceed $2,000, as described in §5.1.

§3.4 Mental Health Services
Outpatient counseling is covered at 75 percent for up to 30 sessions per Plan Year. Inpatient psychiatric care is covered for up to 20 days per Plan Year at 80 percent. Crisis stabilization visits are exempt from the session limit and subject only to a $15 copayment.

§3.5 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs are covered with a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs with a $30 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs at 50 percent. A 30-day supply applies at retail pharmacies and a 90-day supply at the demo mail service. Controlled substances require provider attestation and are limited to one fill per 30 days.

§3.6 Emergency Care
Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent with a $100 copayment, waived if the student is admitted as an inpatient. Emergency care obtained outside the network is paid at the in-network level. Follow-up visits after an emergency are subject to the rules in §3.2.

§4.1 Annual and Lifetime Limits
Total benefits payable are limited to $150,000 per Covered Student per Plan Year. No lifetime maximum applies to preventive services described in §3.1. Once the annual limit is reached, no further benefits are payable until the next Plan Year begins.

§4.2 Exclusions
The plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, dental orthodontia, or vision hardware beyond the allowance in §3.1. Care received from a provider who is a spouse or parent of the student is excluded. Injuries sustained during paid professional athletics are excluded, except that intramural and club sports injuries are covered.

§4.3 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident is payable even though it is otherwise cosmetic, up to $5,000 per Plan Year. Dental care required to treat an accidental injury to sound natural teeth is covered at 70 percent. Experimental treatment may be covered if the Demo Review Board issues a written exception under §5.1.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Services exceeding $1,000, planned hospital admissions, and any procedure listed in §3.3 require prior approval submitted at least 10 business days in advance. Emergency admissions require notice within 48 hours of admission. Failure to obtain prior approval reduces the benefit payable by 25 percent but does not deny it entirely.

§5.2 Network Rules
The Demo Provider Network is a fictional list maintained for this demonstration. Out-of-network care is subject to the reduced level described in §3.2 unless the service is unavailable in-network. Students more than 50 miles from campus during official breaks may access any provider at in-network levels.

§5.3 Cost Sharing Summary
The annual deductible is $200 per Covered Student, applied to all services except those in §3.1. The annual out-of-pocket maximum is $3,500, after which covered services are paid at 100 percent. Copayments do not count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service using the sample form provided by Demo Administrators. Late claims are denied unless it was not reasonably possible to file in time, in which case notice must be given as soon as possible. Claims are paid within 30 days of receipt of a complete submission.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days by sending a written appeal to Demo Administrators. A first-level appeal is decided within 45 days by a reviewer not involved in the original denial. A second-level appeal to the Demo Review Board must be requested within 30 days of the first-level decision and is decided within 60 days.

§6.3 Notices
All notices under this plan must be in writing and sent to the fictional administrative address shown in the sample materials. A notice is deemed received on the date demonstrated in the demo records. The administrator may request additional documentation, and the deadline in §6.1 is tolled while the request is pending.

§6.4 Administration and Amendments
Demo Administrators may amend this plan annually with 60 days notice to enrolled students. Benefit changes do not apply retroactively to services already rendered. This synthetic document expires automatically at the conclusion of the software demonstration and confers no real rights.

SYNTHETIC
Sunridge Flex Health Plan for Small Employers — Demonstration Document

§1.1 Definitions
"Plan" means the Sunridge Flex Health Plan described in this document, which is a fictional product created solely for software demonstration purposes. "Covered Person" means an Employee or Dependent who has met the eligibility rules in §2.1 and §2.2 and whose coverage is in force. "Calendar Year" means the twelve-month period beginning January 1 and ending December 31, which is the basis for all annual limits in this Plan. "Allowable Charge" means the negotiated rate the Plan Administrator agrees to pay a provider, not to exceed 130 percent of the regional benchmark fee schedule.

§1.2 Plan Administrator
The Plan Administrator is the employer sponsoring this demonstration Plan, acting through its benefits office. The Administrator maintains enrollment records, processes premium deductions, and forwards claims documentation as described in §6.1. The Administrator's decisions on enrollment may be appealed under §6.4.

§1.3 Effective Date
This Plan takes effect on the first day of the Calendar Year in which it is adopted. Coverage for any individual begins on the later of the Plan's effective date or the individual's coverage date under §2.3. No coverage exists before that date under any circumstance.

§2.1 Employee Eligibility
An Employee is eligible if regularly scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week. Seasonal and temporary workers are not eligible, except that a temporary worker converted to regular status becomes eligible on the conversion date. Eligibility must be verified by the Administrator before any enrollment is accepted.

§2.2 Dependent Eligibility
Eligible Dependents include a lawful spouse and children under age 26. A child who is medically certified as disabled before age 26 may remain eligible indefinitely, subject to recertification every two years. Dependents of Dependents are not eligible.

§2.3 Enrollment and Waiting Period
New Employees must enroll within 31 days of their eligibility date. Coverage begins on the first day of the month following completion of a 60-day waiting period of continuous employment. Late enrollees, meaning those who miss the 31-day window, must wait until the next annual open enrollment and will be subject to the pre-existing condition rule in §4.4.

§2.4 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the Employee terminates employment, reduces hours below 30 per week, or fails to pay the required premium contribution. Dependent coverage ends when the Dependent ceases to satisfy §2.2. The Administrator will provide written notice of termination within 15 days of the event.

§3.1 Hospital Benefits
The Plan pays 80 percent of Allowable Charges for semi-private room and board up to $1,200 per day, for a maximum of 60 days per admission. Intensive care is covered at 80 percent up to $3,000 per day for a maximum of 15 days per admission. Pre-admission testing within 7 days of a covered admission is payable as part of that admission, subject to the prior approval rule in §5.1.

§3.2 Physician and Office Visits
Primary care office visits are covered at 100 percent of Allowable Charges after a $25 copayment per visit. Specialist visits are covered after a $50 copayment, with a limit of 36 combined visits per Calendar Year. Preventive care as described in §3.3 is not counted against the 36-visit limit.

§3.3 Preventive Care
Annual physical examinations, routine immunizations, and age-appropriate cancer screenings are covered at 100 percent with no copayment, once per Calendar Year per Covered Person. Well-child visits are covered according to the standard pediatric schedule, up to 8 visits before age 2 and annually thereafter. Preventive services do not reduce the visit limit in §3.2.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs are covered after a $10 copayment, preferred brand after a $40 copayment, and non-preferred brand after a $75 copayment, each for up to a 30-day supply at retail. A 90-day supply is available through mail order at twice the retail copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval under §5.1 and are limited to $15,000 per Calendar Year, with an exception allowing an additional $15,000 for drugs used to treat cancer.

§3.5 Emergency Services
Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent of Allowable Charges after a $150 copayment, which is waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient. Emergency care received outside the service area is covered at the same level, and no prior approval is required. Follow-up care after an emergency visit is not emergency care and is subject to §3.2.

§3.6 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered after a $30 copayment, limited to 30 sessions per Calendar Year. Inpatient mental health or substance use treatment is covered as described in §3.1, limited to 30 days per Calendar Year. An additional 10 outpatient sessions per Calendar Year are allowed when a treating provider documents medical necessity in writing.

§4.1 Annual Out-of-Pocket Limit
Each Covered Person's annual out-of-pocket limit is $6,500 for in-network services, including copayments and coinsurance but not premiums. Family coverage carries an out-of-pocket limit of $13,000 per Calendar Year. Once the limit is reached, the Plan pays 100 percent of Allowable Charges for the remainder of the Calendar Year.

§4.2 Lifetime Maximum
The lifetime maximum benefit for all covered services is $2,000,000 per Covered Person. Amounts paid under the preventive care benefit in §3.3 do not count against the lifetime maximum. When a Covered Person approaches the maximum, the Administrator will issue written notice as described in §6.3.

§4.3 Excluded Services
The Plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, dental care for persons over age 19, vision hardware for persons over age 19, infertility treatment, weight-loss surgery without documented medical necessity, or experimental procedures. Custodial care beyond 90 days per Calendar Year is excluded. Injury or illness arising from commission of a felony is excluded, except that treatment of a self-inflicted injury resulting from a documented mental health condition is covered under §3.6.

§4.4 Pre-Existing Conditions
A pre-existing condition is one for which advice, diagnosis, or treatment was received during the 6 months before the coverage date. The Plan excludes coverage for such conditions for 12 months following the coverage date. This exclusion is reduced month-for-month by prior credible coverage, and does not apply to pregnancy, to a newborn adopted or placed for adoption within 31 days of birth, or to a child under age 18.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for all inpatient admissions, except emergency admissions under §3.5, and for specialty drugs, imaging exceeding $1,000 in Allowable Charges, and durable medical equipment exceeding $2,500. Requests must be submitted in writing at least 10 days before scheduled services, or within 3 business days after an emergency admission. Approval is valid for 60 days from the date of issuance.

§5.2 Notification Deadlines
The Covered Person or representative must notify the Administrator of any emergency admission within 48 hours of admission or as soon as reasonably possible. Claims must be filed within 180 days of the date of service, as described in §6.1. Failure to meet a notification deadline reduces benefits by 25 percent, except where it was not reasonably possible to comply.

§5.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays secondary according to standard birthday-rule ordering for Dependents. Benefits payable under this Plan will be reduced so that total payments from all plans do not exceed 100 percent of Allowable Charges. The Covered Person must supply information about other coverage upon request, and refusal to cooperate suspends payment under this section until the information is provided.

§5.4 Subrogation
If a Covered Person recovers funds from a third party for an injury for which the Plan paid benefits, the Plan is entitled to reimbursement up to the amount paid. The Plan will reduce its recovery by a pro rata share of reasonable attorney fees incurred by the Covered Person. No settlement is final as to the Plan until the Administrator receives notice under §6.3.

§6.1 Claim Submission
Claims must be submitted in writing on a standard claim form within 180 days of the date of service. The claim must include the provider's statement of services, the diagnosis, and the charge. The Administrator will pay or deny a clean claim within 30 days of receipt; complex claims may take up to 90 days with written notice of the delay.

§6.2 Benefit Payments
Benefit payments are issued within 15 days after a claim is approved. Payments are made to the provider when the Covered Person has assigned benefits, and otherwise to the Covered Person. An overpayment discovered within 24 months of payment may be recovered by offset against future benefits or by written demand for refund.

§6.3 Notices
All notices required under this Plan, including those under §4.2 and §5.4, must be in writing and delivered to the address on file with the Administrator. A notice is deemed given on the date of deposit in the mail, postage prepaid. The Administrator must maintain proof of mailing for at least three years.

§6.4 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal any adverse benefit determination within 180 days of the denial notice. The appeal must be in writing and may include supporting documentation from a treating provider. A review committee independent of the original decision-maker will decide the appeal within 60 days, and a second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first-level denial, with a decision due within 30 days.

§6.5 Amendment and Termination
The employer reserves the right to amend or terminate this Plan at any time, with 60 days advance written notice to Covered Persons. No amendment may reduce benefits retroactively for services already rendered. Upon termination, claims for services rendered before the termination date remain payable under the terms in effect on the date of service.

§6.6 Demonstration Disclaimer
This Plan is synthetic and exists only to exercise software features such as clause parsing, cross-reference resolution, and eligibility logic. No entity offers, administers, or underwrites the coverage described here, and nothing in this document creates any right to benefits. Any resemblance to an actual benefit plan is coincidental.

SYNTHETIC
Fictional Demo Document — Sample Text Only

Bluebird Campus Care Plan (Demonstration Sample)

§1.1 Purpose
This sample plan text exists solely to demonstrate document layout in a software demo. It describes a fictional student health plan for a fictional institution. No real coverage, obligations, or entitlements arise from this text.

§1.2 Definitions
"Plan Year" means the fictional period from August 1 through July 31. "Covered Student" means a fictional enrolled student who has paid the fictional premium. "Custodial Unit" means the fictional campus clinic described in §2.3.

§1.3 Eligibility
Fictional students enrolled in at least six credit hours at the fictional campus are eligible. Eligibility begins after a waiting period of fourteen days from the fictional enrollment date. Dependents under age nineteen may be added during the fictional open window each September.

§1.4 Effective Date
Coverage begins on the first day of the month following the waiting period in §1.3. Fictional late enrollees must wait until the next quarterly intake. No coverage is retroactive.

§2.1 Premiums
The fictional premium is 420 currency units per Plan Year, payable in two installments. A late fee of 15 currency units applies after the tenth day of each fictional billing cycle. Nonpayment for sixty days terminates coverage as described in §2.4.

§2.2 Cost Sharing
Fictional students pay a 20 currency unit copayment per clinic visit. After the copayment, the plan pays eighty percent of allowed fictional charges. The annual fictional out-of-pocket maximum is 1,500 currency units.

§2.3 Custodial Unit Services
Visits to the fictional Custodial Unit are covered at one hundred percent with no copayment. This includes up to twelve fictional counseling sessions per Plan Year. Services beyond that limit follow the cost sharing in §2.2.

§2.4 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which a fictional student drops below six credit hours. A thirty-day fictional grace period applies after premium nonpayment. Reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus the fee in §2.1.

§3.1 Covered Benefits
Covered benefits include fictional physician visits, laboratory tests, emergency transport, and the counseling sessions in §2.3. Prescription drugs are covered subject to §3.2. Dental care is covered only for accidental injury, not routine care.

§3.2 Prescription Drugs
The plan pays seventy percent of fictional generic drug costs and fifty percent of fictional brand costs. A thirty-day supply limit applies per fictional fill. Prior approval is required for any fictional drug costing over 200 currency units, as described in §4.1.

§3.3 Hospital Benefits
Fictional inpatient stays are covered up to sixty days per Plan Year. The daily fictional allowance is 900 currency units. Days beyond sixty are excluded unless extended by the process in §4.1.

§3.4 Emergency Care
Fictional emergency services are covered at one hundred percent when the Custodial Unit is closed. The student must notify the plan within forty-eight hours of any fictional emergency admission. Failure to notify reduces payment to fifty percent.

§4.1 Prior Approval
Certain fictional services require prior approval, including hospital stays under §3.3 and high-cost drugs under §3.2. Requests must be submitted at least five fictional business days in advance. Approval is valid for sixty days from issuance.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
Fictional claims must be filed within ninety days of service. Notice of a fictional appeal must be filed within 120 days of a denial. Late fictional notices are barred except for emergencies under §3.4.

§4.3 Limits Per Year
The plan limits fictional physical therapy to twenty visits per Plan Year. Fictional ambulance transport is limited to two trips per Plan Year. All limits reset each August 1.

§4.4 Exclusions
Excluded fictional items include cosmetic procedures, experimental treatments, and injuries from fictional interstellar travel. Exclusions do not apply to emergency stabilization under §3.4. The plan also excludes services received outside the fictional service area except as permitted by §4.5.

§4.5 Referrals Outside the Area
Fictional students may obtain covered services outside the fictional service area with a written referral from the Custodial Unit. Such referrals must specify the fictional duration, not exceeding ninety days. Referred services remain subject to cost sharing under §2.2.

§5.1 Claims Submission
Fictional claims must include the fictional date of service, provider description, and itemized fictional charges. Incomplete fictional claims are returned within ten days with a deficiency notice. Corrected claims restart the ninety-day clock in §4.2.

§5.2 Claim Decisions
The fictional administrator decides claims within thirty days of receipt. Fictional denials must state the reason and cite the applicable clause, such as §4.4. Payment is made within fifteen days of an approval.

§5.3 Appeals
A fictional student may appeal a denial in two levels. The first fictional appeal is decided within twenty days by a different fictional reviewer. The second appeal is decided within forty days and is the final fictional administrative step.

§5.4 External Review
After exhausting §5.3, a fictional student may request review by the fictional independent panel. The fictional panel must receive the request within sixty days of the final denial. Its fictional decision binds the administrator.

§6.1 Administration
The fictional administrator maintains all fictional records for seven years. Fictional students may inspect their own fictional records upon written request. Responses are provided within thirty days.

§6.2 Plan Changes
The fictional sponsor may amend this sample text annually before August 1. Fictional students receive thirty days notice of any change to premiums or benefits under §3.1. Changes to exclusions in §4.4 require sixty days notice.

§6.3 Coordination
If a fictional student has other fictional coverage, this plan pays second. The administrator may recover fictional overpayments within three years of payment. Recovery does not apply to amounts paid in good faith under §5.2.

§6.4 Governing Text
This fictional document governs only within the software demo environment. Any conflict with §1.1 is resolved in favor of §1.1. All figures are invented and carry no real-world meaning.

SYNTHETIC
Short-Term Medical Plan: DemoShield Sample Coverage

§1.1 Definitions
This plan uses the term "Covered Person" to describe any individual enrolled under a Certificate issued by the plan administrator. "Medically Necessary Care" means treatment that a licensed provider certifies is required to diagnose or treat an illness or injury. "Benefit Period" means the span from the effective date through the earlier of the termination date or 180 days of continuous coverage.

§1.2 Eligibility
Applicants must be between 18 and 64 years old and reside in a fictional demo jurisdiction. Enrollment requires completion of a sample application attesting that the applicant has not been hospitalized within the prior 30 days. Coverage begins only after a waiting period of 14 days from the accepted application date, except for injuries, which are covered from day one.

§1.3 Effective and Termination Dates
Coverage becomes effective at 12:01 a.m. on the date stated in the sample Certificate. Coverage ends at 11:59 p.m. on the last day of the term or upon nonpayment of premium. Termination does not affect claims for services rendered while coverage was active.

§2.1 Hospital Benefits
The plan pays 80 percent of allowed charges for inpatient hospital stays, up to a maximum of 1,200 dollars per day and 60 days per Benefit Period. Intensive care is reimbursed at 100 percent of allowed charges up to 2,000 dollars per day for a maximum of 15 days. Charges above these limits are the Covered Person's responsibility.

§2.2 Physician and Outpatient Benefits
The plan pays 70 percent of allowed charges for physician office visits, limited to 8 visits per Benefit Period. Outpatient surgery is covered at 75 percent of allowed charges up to 10,000 dollars per occurrence. Emergency room visits are covered at 80 percent without applying the visit limit, as described in §4.2.

§2.3 Prescription Benefits
Generic prescriptions are covered at 100 percent of allowed charges after a 25 dollar copayment per fill. Brand-name prescriptions are covered at 60 percent after a 50 dollar copayment. A 30-day supply limit applies per fill, and no more than 12 fills are covered per Benefit Period.

§2.4 Preventive Benefits
One annual wellness examination is covered at 100 percent of a 250 dollar allowed amount. Immunizations commonly administered during that examination are included. Additional preventive visits in the same Benefit Period are subject to the physician visit limits in §2.2.

§3.1 Deductible
A deductible of 1,500 dollars per Covered Person applies to all benefits except preventive care and prescription drugs. The family deductible is 3,000 dollars regardless of the number of enrolled family members. Amounts applied to the deductible carry over only within the same Benefit Period.

§3.2 Copayments and Coinsurance
After the deductible in §3.1 is satisfied, coinsurance percentages in §2.1 through §2.3 apply. Copayments do not count toward the deductible. The total out-of-pocket maximum is 7,500 dollars per Covered Person per Benefit Period, after which the plan pays 100 percent of allowed charges for the remainder of the term.

§3.3 Premiums
The sample monthly premium is 145 dollars for a single Covered Person and 380 dollars for a family. Premiums are due on the first day of each coverage month. A grace period of 10 days applies before termination for nonpayment.

§4.1 General Exclusions
The plan does not cover pre-existing conditions, defined as any condition for which care was received or recommended within 24 months before the effective date. Maternity care, dental care, and vision care are excluded. Cosmetic procedures are excluded unless required to treat an accidental injury occurring during the Benefit Period.

§4.2 Exclusion Exceptions
Notwithstanding §4.1, emergency services rendered within 72 hours of an accidental injury are covered even if the injury reveals a pre-existing condition, but follow-up treatment of that condition remains excluded. Experimental treatments are excluded except when the plan administrator has issued prior written approval. Substance use treatment is excluded, except for one medically supervised detoxification episode of up to 5 days per Benefit Period.

§4.3 Optional Riders
A sample accident rider adds 15 dollars per day of hospital confinement resulting from an accident, up to 500 dollars. A sample outpatient therapy rider covers 20 physical therapy visits at 50 dollars per visit. Riders must be elected at application and cannot be added later.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, outpatient surgery, and any service expected to exceed 2,500 dollars require prior approval from the plan administrator. Approval requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before scheduled care, or within 48 hours after emergency admission. Failure to obtain approval reduces benefits by 50 percent but does not deny them entirely.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of a claim must be provided within 30 days of the date of service, or as soon as reasonably possible. Proof of loss must be submitted within 90 days of the notice. The administrator may waive late proof if it was not reasonably possible to submit on time.

§5.3 Claim Payment
Approved claims are paid within 30 days of receipt of complete documentation. Payments are made to the provider when assignment is on file, otherwise to the Covered Person. Interest of 12 percent per year accrues on claims unpaid beyond the 30-day period.

§5.4 Appeals
A Covered Person may appeal a denied claim within 180 days of the denial notice. The administrator must respond with a written decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first decision, and the outcome of the second appeal is final under this sample plan.

§6.1 Coordination of Benefits
If a Covered Person has other coverage, this plan pays only the portion of charges that other coverage does not cover, up to the allowed amount. This plan is always secondary to any major medical coverage in force. Duplicate payments must be refunded to the administrator within 30 days of demand.

§6.2 Subrogation
If benefits are paid for injuries caused by a third party, the administrator may recover those payments from any settlement or judgment. The Covered Person must cooperate and sign sample recovery documents on request. Recovery costs are shared proportionally with the Covered Person.

§6.3 Administration
The plan administrator processes claims, approvals, and appeals under this Certificate. Sample records are retained for 24 months after the Benefit Period ends, consistent with §5.2. All amounts, limits, and terms in this document are fictional and exist solely for demonstration purposes.

SYNTHETIC
Zenith Preferred Health Plan, Demo Edition, Group Policy Sample-9999

§1.1 Definitions
The Plan refers to this employer-sponsored preferred provider organization document created solely for software demonstration purposes. Covered Person means an employee or dependent who meets the eligibility rules in §2.1. Deductible means the annual amount of covered expenses the Covered Person must pay before benefits are payable. Negotiated Rate means the discounted fee the Plan has arranged with a Network Provider.

§1.2 Network Providers
A Network Provider is a physician, hospital, pharmacy, or facility that has a participation agreement with the demonstration network. Services received from a Network Provider are reimbursed at the in-network benefit level described in §4.1. Services from a Non-Network Provider are reimbursed at the out-of-network level described in §4.2. A provider's network status is determined on the date the service is rendered.

§1.3 Eligible Expenses
Eligible Expenses are charges for medically necessary services that are not excluded under §5.1 through §5.3. Charges in excess of the Negotiated Rate are not Eligible Expenses when care is received from a Network Provider. Expenses must be incurred while the Covered Person is enrolled under the Plan. Charges for items billed separately that are normally included in a procedure fee are not Eligible Expenses.

§2.1 Employee Eligibility
An employee is eligible on the first day of the month following completion of a 60-day waiting period of continuous full-time employment. Full-time means regularly scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week. Eligibility terminates on the last day of the month in which employment ends, except as continued under §2.4. Rehired employees within a 13-week break satisfy the waiting period retroactively.

§2.2 Dependent Eligibility
Eligible dependents include a lawful spouse and children under age 26. A child who is disabled before age 26 may remain eligible indefinitely upon proof submitted within 90 days of the request. Dependents become covered on the later of the employee's eligibility date or the date a completed enrollment form is filed. A newborn is covered automatically for the first 31 days.

§2.3 Enrollment and Changes
Enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the hire date or a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, or loss of other coverage. Late enrollees other than those with qualifying events must wait until the next annual enrollment period. Changes outside the enrollment window are permitted only within 31 days of a qualifying event. Coverage elections take effect as stated in §2.1 and §2.2.

§2.4 Continuation of Coverage
Coverage may be continued for up to 18 months following termination of employment for reasons other than gross misconduct. Continuation coverage costs 102 percent of the applicable premium, payable monthly in advance. A covered disability extension may add 11 months for a total of 29 months. Failure to pay within 30 days of the due date terminates continuation.

§3.1 Prior Authorization
Certain services require prior authorization, including inpatient admissions, scheduled surgery, imaging such as MRI and CT, and specialty drugs costing more than $1,500 per fill. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before a scheduled service, or within 48 hours for emergency admissions. Approved authorizations are valid for 60 days. Failure to obtain required authorization reduces benefits by 50 percent, except that authorization is never required for emergency care as defined in §3.2.

§3.2 Emergency Services
Emergency services are covered without prior authorization at the in-network level regardless of provider status. Emergency means a condition with acute symptoms severe enough that a prudent person could reasonably expect serious jeopardy to health. Follow-up care after the emergency stabilizes is subject to normal network rules under §1.2. Emergency room copays are waived if the Covered Person is admitted within 24 hours.

§3.3 Notice Deadlines
Written notice of intent to obtain a non-emergency transplant outside the demonstration network must be given 30 days in advance. Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service as described in §6.1. Notice of a dependent's loss of eligibility must be given within 60 days. Late notice voids coverage for the affected event, except where notice was impossible for reasons beyond the Covered Person's control.

§4.1 In-Network Benefits
After the individual Deductible of $1,500 per person or $3,000 per family, the Plan pays 85 percent of the Negotiated Rate for most services. Office visits are subject to a $25 copay with no Deductible. Inpatient hospitalization is covered at 90 percent after a $500 per-admission copay, limited to 120 days per calendar year. Preventive care as listed in §4.3 is covered at 100 percent.

§4.2 Out-of-Network Benefits
After a separate Deductible of $3,000 per person, the Plan pays 60 percent of the recognized charge for out-of-network services. The recognized charge is capped at 120 percent of the regional median fee. Out-of-network annual out-of-pocket maximum is $12,000 per person. Balanced-billed amounts above the recognized charge are the Covered Person's responsibility, except as limited by §3.2 for emergencies.

§4.3 Preventive Services
Routine physical examinations are covered once per calendar year at 100 percent with no cost sharing when a Network Provider is used. Well-child visits are covered according to the recommended schedule through age 18. Immunizations, annual flu shots, and routine cancer screenings are covered without Deductible. Services performed during a preventive visit that are not preventive, such as treatment of a new complaint, are subject to the cost sharing in §4.1.

§4.4 Prescription Drugs
Retail pharmacy copays are $15 for generic, $40 for preferred brand, and $75 for non-preferred drugs per 30-day supply. A 90-day maintenance supply is available through the demonstration mail program for twice the 30-day copay. Specialty drugs require prior authorization under §3.1 and carry a $100 copay per fill. Non-preferred brand charges above $150 per prescription are the Covered Person's responsibility.

§4.5 Mental Health and Substance Use
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at the in-network level with a $30 copay, limited to 40 visits per calendar year. Inpatient psychiatric treatment is covered under the day limits in §4.1. Intensive outpatient programs require prior authorization under §3.1. Substance use disorder treatment is covered on the same terms as mental health treatment, with no separate lifetime limit.

§5.1 General Exclusions
The Plan does not cover services that are not medically necessary, experimental, or investigational. Cosmetic surgery is excluded unless required to repair a functional impairment or resulting from an accidental injury. Dental care for children under 19 is excluded from medical benefits, except treatment of accidental injury to sound natural teeth within 12 months of the accident. Charges for services rendered by a person who lives in the Covered Person's household or is a close relative are excluded.

§5.2 Specific Exclusions
Weight loss programs are excluded except when bariatric surgery is authorized under §3.1 for persons with a qualifying diagnosis. Vision hardware such as eyeglasses and contact lenses is excluded, except one pair following cataract surgery. Hearing aids are limited to one device per ear every 36 months at a $1,000 maximum per device. Infertility treatment is excluded except for diagnostic testing up to $2,000 per calendar year.

§5.3 Exceptions to Exclusions
Excluded services become covered when a documented clinical trial protocol authorizes them, subject to prior authorization under §3.1. Items normally excluded under §5.1 are covered when needed to treat a covered condition such as reconstruction after a covered mastectomy. Exclusions do not apply to emergency services under §3.2. The Plan Administrator may grant individual exceptions in writing for demonstrable hardship.

§6.1 Claims Submission
Claims must be filed within 12 months of the date of service or benefits are forfeited. Network Providers file claims directly; Covered Persons using out-of-network providers must submit itemized bills within the same deadline. Complete claims are adjudicated within 30 days of receipt. Incomplete claims generate a written request for additional information, and the Covered Person then has 45 days to respond.

§6.2 Payment Rules
Benefits are paid to the provider when assignment is accepted, otherwise to the Covered Person. Payments exceeding the allowable amount are recovered from subsequent claims or by refund request within 60 days. Coordination of benefits limits total payment from all plans to 100 percent of allowable expenses. The Plan pays second according to the birthday rule for dependent children covered by two plans.

§6.3 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 180 days of the denial notice. The Plan issues a first-level appeal decision within 30 days, or 72 hours for urgent care appeals. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first decision and is decided by a reviewer not involved in the original denial. External review is available after both internal appeals are exhausted, and the Covered Person has 4 months to request it.

§7.1 Administration
The Plan Administrator maintains enrollment records, interprets the Plan, and may amend it annually at renewal. The Plan year runs from January 1 through December 31. Amendments apply prospectively only and do not reduce benefits for services already authorized under §3.1. This document is synthetic and confers no actual rights or coverage of any kind.

SYNTHETIC
Meridian Horizon Choice HDQ 2500

§1.1 Plan Name and Purpose
This document describes the Meridian Horizon Choice HDQ 2500, a fictional high-deductible health plan created solely for software demonstration purposes. All terms, amounts, and entities herein are invented and have no real-world counterpart. The plan is administered by the fictional Horizon Benefits Trust described in §6.1.

§1.2 Definitions
"Covered Service" means any medically necessary service listed in §3.1 and not excluded under §4.1. "Deductible" means the amount a Member must pay each Plan Year before the plan pays benefits, set at $2,500 for individual coverage and $5,000 for family coverage. "Plan Year" begins on the first day of the fictional calendar month designated at enrollment and lasts twelve months.

§1.3 Fictional Sponsor
The plan is sponsored by the fictional Northvale Software Consortium for demonstration purposes only. The sponsor has no legal existence and issues no real obligations. Any resemblance to actual plans is coincidental.

§2.1 Eligibility
Fictional employees of demo tenant accounts are eligible if they work at least 30 simulated hours per week. Enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the simulated hire date. Late enrollment is permitted only during the annual demonstration open period or upon a qualifying fictional life event.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Newly eligible fictional members are subject to a 60-day waiting period before coverage begins. The waiting period is waived for fictional members transferring from another demo plan within the same tenant. Coverage under this plan during the waiting period is limited to the preventive services described in §3.2.

§2.3 Dependents
A Member may enroll a fictional spouse and dependent children under age 26. Dependent coverage terminates at the end of the Plan Year in which the dependent reaches the limiting age. Disabled dependents who became disabled before age 26 may remain covered indefinitely upon submission of fictional proof annually.

§3.1 Covered Services
The plan covers inpatient hospital care at 80 percent after the Deductible, with a 120-day annual limit per admission spell. Outpatient surgery, imaging, and emergency care are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible. Office visits are covered at 100 percent after a $35 copay once the Deductible is met, except as provided in §3.2.

§3.2 Preventive Services
Preventive services, including annual physicals, immunizations, and age-appropriate screenings, are covered at 100 percent with no Deductible. One routine physical per Plan Year is allowed per Member. Preventive services do not count toward the Deductible described in §1.2.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
Generic drugs are covered at a $15 copay, preferred brand drugs at a $40 copay, and non-preferred brand drugs at a $75 copay, all after the Deductible. A 90-day supply maintenance program is available at twice the 30-day copay. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1.

§3.4 Mental Health Services
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible with a 40-visit annual limit. Inpatient mental health care is covered for up to 60 days per Plan Year. Substance use treatment is covered on the same terms, and no exclusions in §4.1 apply to these services beyond medical necessity.

§4.1 Exclusions
Services that are cosmetic, experimental, or not medically necessary are excluded. Dental and vision care for adults are excluded, except pediatric vision exams covered under §3.2 and accidental injury to sound natural teeth. Weight-loss surgery is excluded unless the Member completes a supervised 6-month program documented in advance.

§4.2 Limits
The out-of-pocket maximum is $6,500 individual and $13,000 family per Plan Year, after which Covered Services are paid at 100 percent. Lifetime maximum benefits are $5,000,000 per fictional Member. Copays described in §3.1 do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§4.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Member has coverage under another fictional plan, this plan pays secondary according to the birthday rule for dependents. Benefits payable will not exceed what this plan would pay as primary payer. Failure to disclose other coverage may result in claim denial under §6.2.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Inpatient admissions, imaging over $1,500, and specialty drugs require prior approval from the fictional review administrator. Requests must be submitted at least 5 business days before non-emergency services. Emergency admissions require notice within 48 hours of admission or the claim is reduced by 20 percent.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be filed within 90 days of the date of service. Members must notify the plan of address or coverage changes within 31 days of the change. Appeals under §6.3 must be initiated within 180 days of the denial notice.

§5.3 Cost Sharing
Members pay the Deductible, copays, and 20 percent coinsurance as described in §3.1. Providers may not bill Members beyond the negotiated fictional rate for Covered Services. Balance billing for emergency services is prohibited under this plan's terms.

§5.4 Continuation Coverage
A fictional Member losing eligibility may continue coverage for up to 18 months at 102 percent of the premium equivalent. Continuation coverage applies the same Deductible and limits described in §4.2. A second qualifying event extends dependent continuation to 36 months total.

§6.1 Administration
The plan is administered by the fictional Horizon Benefits Trust, which processes claims within 30 days of receipt. The Trust maintains all enrollment records and issues identification credentials for demo purposes. Administrative questions in the demo environment route to the tenant's configured help desk.

§6.2 Claims Submission
Claims must include the fictional member reference, date of service, and itemized charges. Incomplete claims are returned once for correction within 45 days. Claims corrected and resubmitted within that window retain the original filing date under §5.2.

§6.3 Appeals
A Member may appeal a denied claim in two levels. The first-level appeal is decided by the fictional review administrator within 30 days, and the second-level appeal by an independent fictional reviewer within 60 days. Exhaustion of both levels is required before any simulated external review.

§6.4 Amendments
The fictional sponsor may amend this document upon 60 days written notice within the demo environment. Amendments may not reduce benefits mid-Plan Year except as required by fictional regulation. All amendments are logged in the demo audit trail for transparency.

§7.1 Demonstration Disclaimer
This plan exists only as synthetic sample data for software demonstration. No premiums, benefits, or obligations described here are real or enforceable. Any resemblance to actual insurance products is unintentional.
