SYNTHETIC.
Plan: AuroraVoyage Demo Travel Medical Policy (Fictional Sample Document for Software Demonstration Only)

§1.1 Definitions
"Trip" means any journey outside the Insured Person's Home Country lasting no more than 180 consecutive days. "Emergency" means a sudden, unexpected medical condition requiring immediate care to prevent serious deterioration. "Home Country" means the country where the Insured Person maintains a permanent residence.

§1.2 Definitions Continued
"Pre-existing Condition" means any condition for which treatment, diagnosis, or medication occurred within the 24 months before the Trip start date. "Usual and Customary Charge" means the median cost of a service in the geographic area where it is provided. "Covered Accident" means a sudden, unintentional external event causing bodily injury.

§1.3 Interpretation
Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. Singular terms include the plural. References to dollar amounts mean United States dollars.

§2.1 Eligibility
Coverage is available to persons aged 6 months to 79 years at the time of application. The applicant must be traveling outside the Home Country for at least 5 days. Persons over 65 must complete a short health questionnaire at enrollment.

§2.2 Enrollment and Effective Date
Coverage begins at 12:01 a.m. on the later of the Trip start date or the date the premium is received. Coverage ends at 11:59 p.m. on the Trip end date or upon return to the Home Country, whichever is earlier. The maximum total period of coverage is 180 days.

§2.3 Waiting Periods
Illness benefits are subject to a 3-day waiting period from the effective date. Accident benefits have no waiting period. The waiting period does not apply to medical emergencies as defined in §1.1.

§3.1 Emergency Medical Benefits
The plan pays 100 percent of Usual and Customary Charges for Emergency hospital room and board up to 500 dollars per day, maximum 30 days per Trip. Emergency room visits are covered up to 2,500 dollars per Trip. Intensive care is covered at 1,000 dollars per day for up to 10 days.

§3.2 Outpatient and Physician Services
Physician office visits are covered up to 150 dollars per visit, limited to 10 visits per Trip. Prescription drugs are covered up to 500 dollars per Trip with a 25 dollar deductible per prescription. Physical therapy is covered up to 50 dollars per session, maximum 8 sessions, subject to prior approval as described in §5.1.

§3.3 Evacuation and Repatriation
Emergency medical evacuation is covered up to 100,000 dollars per Trip when arranged under §5.2. Repatriation of remains is covered up to 50,000 dollars. An evacuation requires coordination with the assistance provider; self-arranged evacuations are reimbursed only up to 25,000 dollars.

§3.4 Additional Benefits
Trip interruption medical follow-up in the Home Country is covered up to 1,000 dollars within 30 days of return. Emergency dental care for injury to sound natural teeth is covered up to 750 dollars per Trip. Accidental death and dismemberment is paid per the schedule in §3.5.

§3.5 Accidental Death and Dismemberment Schedule
The plan pays 25,000 dollars for loss of life, 25,000 dollars for loss of both hands or feet, and 12,500 dollars for loss of one hand or one foot. No more than 100 percent of the principal sum is payable for all losses from one accident. Losses must occur within 365 days of the Covered Accident.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
After any deductible, the plan pays 80 percent of eligible charges up to 10,000 dollars, then 100 percent up to the policy maximum. The deductible is 250 dollars per Trip for illness and 100 dollars per Trip for accident. Benefits under §3.1 for hospital room and board are not subject to coinsurance.

§4.2 Policy Maximums
The overall policy maximum is 250,000 dollars per Trip for insureds under age 65 and 100,000 dollars for insureds aged 65 to 79. Benefits under §3.3 are in addition to the overall maximum. Charges exceeding the Usual and Customary amount are the Insured Person's responsibility.

§4.3 Exclusions
The plan does not cover Pre-existing Conditions, except that acute onset of a Pre-existing Condition is covered up to 25,000 dollars when treatment is sought within 24 hours of symptom onset. Routine care, cosmetic procedures, and experimental treatment are excluded. Self-inflicted injury, war, and participation in professional athletics are excluded.

§4.4 Exclusions Continued
Treatment for substance abuse is excluded, except one emergency stabilization episode up to 2,000 dollars. Pregnancy and childbirth are excluded unless complications arise, which are covered up to 15,000 dollars. Mental health emergencies are covered only as described in §3.2 visit limits.

§5.1 Prior Approval Requirements
Hospital admissions, surgeries, physical therapy, and medical equipment over 500 dollars require prior approval from the assistance provider within 48 hours of the event. Approval obtained after treatment may reduce benefits by 25 percent. Emergency admissions must be reported within 48 hours even when prior approval was impossible.

§5.2 Notice and Deadlines
Evacuations under §3.3 must be arranged through the assistance provider before travel occurs. Written notice of any claim must be given within 90 days of the date of loss. Claims documentation must be submitted within 180 days of the date of loss.

§5.3 Claims Submission
Claims must include itemized bills, diagnosis codes, and proof of payment. Claims are paid in United States dollars within 30 days of receipt of complete documentation. Claims filed outside the deadline in §5.2 are denied unless it was reasonably impossible to file sooner.

§5.4 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within 60 days of the denial notice. The appeal must include new or supporting documentation and is reviewed by a different reviewer within 45 days. A second and final appeal may be filed within 30 days of the first appeal decision.

§6.1 Administration
This policy is administered by the fictional demo administrator named in the sample enrollment record. Premiums are due at enrollment and are fully refundable within 10 days if no claim has been filed. Coverage may be extended in 30-day increments up to the 180-day maximum by paying the additional premium before expiration.

§6.2 Termination and Misstatement
Coverage terminates immediately upon fraud, material misstatement, or return to the Home Country. If age was misstated, benefits are adjusted to the amount the premium would have purchased. Termination for fraud forfeits all benefits under §§3.1 through 3.5.

§6.3 Governing Terms
This document is entirely fictional and exists only to demonstrate software features. No real coverage is created, offered, or implied by this text. Any resemblance to an actual insurance product is unintentional.

SYNTHETIC
ZephyrShield MedComplete Plan Delta-7

§1.1 Definitions
This plan refers to covered medical services as eligible events. The term plan year means the twelve-month period beginning on the first day of the anniversary month of enrollment. A network provider means any practitioner who has signed the fictional participation agreement maintained by the demonstration system.

§1.2 Definitions continued
The term deductible means the amount a member must pay before benefits apply, set at one thousand two hundred dollars per plan year. Coinsurance means the member share of remaining costs, set at fifteen percent. Copayment means a fixed charge such as twenty-five dollars for physician office visits.

§2.1 Eligibility
Members must be simulated persons aged sixty-five or older enrolled in the demonstration dataset. Enrollment takes effect on the first day of the month following acceptance of the application. A waiting period of ninety days applies to all outpatient prescription benefits.

§2.2 Eligibility continued
Dependent simulation records are eligible until the end of the plan year in which they reach age twenty-six. Members who lapse coverage may reinstate within sixty days without a new waiting period, except for the prescription waiting period described in §2.1, which restarts in full.

§3.1 Hospital benefits
The plan pays ninety percent of eligible inpatient hospital costs after the deductible, up to one hundred eighty days per plan year. Days one through six are covered in full after a two hundred fifty dollar per-admission charge. The skilled nursing facility benefit described in §3.2 is subject to the same deductible.

§3.2 Skilled nursing and therapy
Skilled nursing facility care is covered up to one hundred days per plan year with no charge after day twenty. Physical, occupational, and speech therapy are each limited to forty combined outpatient visits per plan year. Home health visits are limited to sixty per plan year.

§4.1 Exclusions
Cosmetic procedures, dental care except reconstructive surgery following accidental injury, and routine vision services are excluded. Experimental treatments are excluded unless the treating provider documents that the therapy is part of an approved registry study. Hearing aids are excluded except one pair every thirty-six months with a seven hundred dollar allowance.

§4.2 Exclusions continued
Services rendered outside the network are covered at the out-of-network rate of seventy percent unless the service is unavailable within fifty miles, in which case in-network rates apply. Emergency services are always covered at in-network rates regardless of location.

§5.1 Prior approval
Imaging beyond plain radiography, inpatient admissions except emergencies, and any procedure costing over five thousand dollars require prior approval submitted at least ten business days in advance. Approval decisions are rendered within five business days. Retroactive approval is permitted for emergency admissions if notice is given within seventy-two hours.

§5.2 Notice deadlines
Members must notify the plan of planned non-emergency hospital admissions at least seven days in advance. Claims for covered services must be filed within twelve months of the date of service. Failure to meet the deadline in §5.1 reduces the payable amount by fifty percent.

§6.1 Cost sharing summary
The annual out-of-pocket maximum is six thousand eight hundred dollars, after which the plan pays one hundred percent of eligible costs. Copayments count toward the out-of-pocket maximum but the deductible does not. Prescription cost sharing is ten dollars generic, forty dollars preferred brand, and eighty dollars non-preferred brand per fill.

§6.2 Cost sharing exceptions
Preventive services listed in the demonstration schedule are covered at one hundred percent with no deductible or coinsurance. The out-of-network cost sharing described in §4.2 does not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

§7.1 Claims administration
Claims are adjudicated within thirty days of receipt, with payment or a written denial issued within fifteen days thereafter. Denials must state the specific plan provision relied upon, including any cross-reference such as §4.1 or §5.1. Clean claims received electronically are deemed adjudicated after fourteen days if no determination issues.

§7.2 Appeals
Members may appeal a denial within one hundred eighty days by submitting a written request with supporting documentation. First-level appeals are decided within thirty days, and second-level appeals within sixty days by a different reviewer. If an appeal is upheld in the member's favor, overpaid cost sharing is refunded within twenty days.

SYNTHETIC
Plan: Aurora Home Shield 3000

§1.1 Definitions
The "Insured Residence" means the single-family dwelling listed on the declarations page, including attached garage and permanently installed fixtures. "Covered Peril" means fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, theft, and accidental water discharge from interior plumbing. "Household Member" means any person who resides at the Insured Residence for at least nine months of the year.

§1.2 Definitions Continued
"Personal Property" means items owned or used by the Insured that are located at the Insured Residence. "Business Property" means any property used in connection with a trade or profession. "Ordinance Cost" means expenses required to bring a damaged structure into compliance with current building codes.

§2.1 Eligibility
The Insured Residence must be the primary residence of the policyholder and must be located within the service territory shown on the declarations page. Dwellings used primarily for short-term rental are not eligible. Homes more than forty years old are eligible only if the electrical and plumbing systems have been updated within the last twenty years.

§2.2 Waiting Period
Coverage for loss caused by water discharge under §3.3 begins thirty days after the policy effective date. All other coverages begin at 12:01 a.m. on the effective date. No waiting period applies to policies renewed without a lapse of more than ten days.

§3.1 Dwelling Benefits
The Insurer will pay to repair or rebuild the dwelling up to a limit of 450,000 dollars per occurrence. Replacement cost coverage applies only if the Insured repairs or rebuilds within eighteen months of the loss. Otherwise payment is limited to actual cash value.

§3.2 Personal Property Benefits
Personal Property is covered up to 100,000 dollars per occurrence, subject to a 500 dollar deductible. Theft of jewelry is limited to 2,500 dollars in the aggregate, and theft of firearms is limited to 3,000 dollars. Business Property is limited to 5,000 dollars per occurrence.

§3.3 Additional Living Expenses
If a Covered Peril renders the Insured Residence uninhabitable, the Insurer will pay reasonable additional living expenses up to 250 dollars per day for a maximum of 60 days. Coverage under this section is available only when the loss is payable under §3.1. Hotel receipts must be submitted within 90 days of the expense.

§4.1 Deductibles and Cost Sharing
A deductible of 1,000 dollars applies to all dwelling claims under §3.1, except that windstorm losses carry a deductible of 2 percent of the dwelling limit. The deductible applies once per occurrence and cannot be stacked across coverages. The deductible is waived for losses exceeding 250,000 dollars.

§4.2 Ordinance Coverage
Ordinance Costs are covered up to 25,000 dollars per occurrence when the loss is otherwise payable under §3.1. This coverage does not apply to routine upgrades performed at the time of repair. Insureds must submit contractor estimates to support any Ordinance Cost claim.

§5.1 Exclusions
Loss caused by flood, surface water, earth movement, or neglect is excluded. Loss caused by intentional acts of any Household Member is excluded. Wear and tear, mold arising over time, and animals are excluded.

§5.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Water damage from backup of a sewer drain is covered up to 10,000 dollars per occurrence if the sewer backup endorsement is shown on the declarations page. Damage to trees and shrubs caused by fire is covered up to 2,000 dollars per tree notwithstanding §5.1. Accidental discharge damage to the dwelling itself is covered even if the discharge originates from an excluded appliance.

§6.1 Prior Approval Requirements
The Insured must obtain prior approval from the Insurer before making emergency repairs exceeding 2,500 dollars. Emergency repairs necessary to prevent further damage may proceed without prior approval if the Insured notifies the Insurer within 24 hours. Non-emergency repairs started without prior approval will be reimbursed at actual cash value only.

§6.2 Notice Deadlines
The Insured must report a loss to the Insurer within 10 days of discovery. Claims for theft must additionally be reported to local law enforcement within 3 days of discovery. Failure to meet these deadlines voids coverage for the loss unless the Insured shows good cause for the delay.

§7.1 Claims Administration
The Insured must submit a signed proof of loss within 60 days of the Insurer's request. The Insurer will acknowledge complete claims within 15 days and will issue a decision within 30 days of receipt of the proof of loss. Payment is issued within 10 business days of an approved decision.

§7.2 Appeals
The Insured may appeal a denial in writing within 60 days of the denial notice. The Insurer will complete a first-level review within 30 days and a second-level review, if requested, within 45 days. An Insured who exhausts both reviews may pursue arbitration as described in the dispute resolution provision.

§7.3 Inspections
The Insurer may inspect the Insured Residence before issuance and after any claim exceeding 25,000 dollars. The Insured must provide reasonable access with at least 5 business days' notice. Refusal to permit inspection suspends coverage until access is granted.

§8.1 Premium and Renewal
The annual premium is payable in full or in four quarterly installments, with a 25 dollar fee per installment. Coverage lapses if any installment is more than 15 days past due. Renewal premiums may change upon 60 days' written notice.

§8.2 Cancellation
The Insurer may cancel for nonpayment with 10 days' notice and for any other reason with 30 days' notice during the first 60 days of the policy. After the first 60 days, cancellation is permitted only for nonpayment, fraud, or material misrepresentation. The Insured may cancel at any time with written notice and will receive a pro rata refund.

§9.1 Subrogation
If the Insurer pays a loss, it may recover from any party responsible for the damage. The Insured must not impair subrogation rights, including by releasing a responsible party without written consent. Recovery is applied first to reimburse the Insurer, then to refund the Insured's deductible.

§9.2 Concealment and Fraud
This policy is void if the Insured intentionally conceals or misstates any material fact relating to a claim. Fraudulent claims forfeit coverage for the entire occurrence in question. Innocent Household Members retain coverage for their own Personal Property, subject to the limits in §3.2.

SYNTHETIC
Plan name: Skyfall Guardian Accident Shield

§1.1 Definitions
"Accident" means a sudden, unforeseen bodily injury caused by an external event occurring during the coverage period. "Covered Person" means an enrolled participant whose coverage is active under this plan. "Medical Provider" means a licensed facility or practitioner rendering treatment for a covered Accident.

§1.2 Definitions continued
"Benefit Year" means the twelve-month period beginning on the enrollment date of each Covered Person. "Qualifying Injury" means an Accident requiring treatment by a Medical Provider within seventy-two hours of the event. Terms not defined here carry their ordinary meaning.

§2.1 Eligibility
Any person aged eighteen through sixty-five may enroll in this plan. Dependent children under age nineteen may be added to a primary enrollment. Enrollment is effective on the first day of the month following approval.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees are subject to a thirty-day waiting period before Accident benefits become payable. Injuries sustained during the waiting period are not covered. The waiting period is waived for enrollees transferring from a comparable accident plan with at least six months of prior continuous coverage.

§3.1 Medical Expense Benefit
This plan pays one hundred percent of eligible medical expenses for a Qualifying Injury up to a maximum of twenty-five thousand dollars per Accident. Eligible expenses include emergency room care, physician services, and prescribed medications. Expenses above this limit are the responsibility of the Covered Person.

§3.2 Hospital Confinement Benefit
A Covered Person hospitalized overnight for a Qualifying Injury receives three hundred dollars per day of confinement. This benefit is payable for a maximum of thirty days per Accident and ninety days per Benefit Year. Days in an intensive care unit are paid at six hundred dollars per day, subject to the same annual maximum.

§3.3 Physical Therapy Benefit
Physical therapy prescribed for recovery from a Qualifying Injury is payable at eighty percent of cost. This benefit is limited to twenty visits per Accident. Visits beyond this limit require prior approval as described in §6.2.

§3.4 Fracture Benefit
A fixed benefit of five hundred dollars is paid for a fractured arm or leg, one thousand dollars for a fractured hip or skull, and two hundred dollars for any other fractured bone. Only one fracture benefit is payable per bone per Benefit Year. This benefit is paid regardless of other benefits under §3.1.

§4.1 Cost Sharing
Each Accident is subject to a two hundred fifty dollar deductible payable by the Covered Person. After the deductible, coinsurance of twenty percent applies to benefits under §3.1, except for the fixed benefits in §3.3 and §3.4 which are not subject to coinsurance. The maximum out-of-pocket amount per Benefit Year is four thousand dollars.

§4.2 Exclusions
Benefits are not payable for injuries sustained while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, except as prescribed by a Medical Provider. Injuries from professional sports, self-inflicted acts, or military combat are excluded. Injuries occurring during ordinary commuting to or from work are covered despite this exclusion.

§4.3 Exclusions continued
Treatment of pre-existing conditions discovered during treatment of an Accident is not payable. Cosmetic surgery is excluded unless required to repair damage from a Qualifying Injury. Injuries sustained outside the country are covered for the first sixty days of travel, after which coverage lapses.

§5.1 Notice and Claim Filing
Written notice of a Qualifying Injury must be provided within twenty days of the Accident. Completed claim forms with itemized bills must be submitted within ninety days of the date of treatment. Late claims may be accepted where notice was impossible for reasons beyond the Covered Person's control.

§5.2 Prior Approval
Hospital admissions planned in advance for Accident recovery require prior approval from the plan administrator. Physical therapy beyond the visit limit in §3.3 also requires prior approval. Services rendered without required prior approval are paid at fifty percent of the otherwise eligible amount.

§5.3 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in writing within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice. The administrator must respond within sixty days of receiving a complete appeal. A second-level appeal may be requested within sixty days of the first appeal decision, and its decision is final under this plan.

§6.1 Administration
The plan administrator processes claims, maintains enrollment records, and issues benefit payments within thirty days of claim approval. Payments for benefits under §3.1 are made directly to the Medical Provider unless assignment is not made. Fixed benefits under §3.4 are paid directly to the Covered Person.

§6.2 Administration continued
Requests for prior approval under §5.2 must be submitted at least five business days before the service date. Emergency admissions are exempt from the advance notice requirement but must be reported within forty-eight hours. The administrator may request additional documentation, which must be supplied within thirty days of the request.

§6.3 Termination and Refunds
Coverage terminates at the end of the month in which a Covered Person reaches age seventy or requests cancellation. Premiums paid beyond the termination date are refunded on a pro-rata basis. Termination does not affect benefits for Accidents that occurred while coverage was active, subject to the limits in §3.1 and §3.2.

SYNTHETIC
HomeShield Quantum Reserve Policy, Sample Edition for Demonstration Use Only

§1.1 Definitions
This policy uses "dwelling" to mean the primary residential structure described in the schedule, including attached garages. "Personal property" means items owned or used by the insured inside the dwelling. "Covered peril" means only those causes of loss listed in §2.2. "Watercraft" means any vessel longer than twelve feet, as further limited in §3.4.

§1.2 Eligibility
Coverage applies only to dwellings used primarily as a private residence, occupied for at least ten months per calendar year. Dwellings left vacant for more than sixty consecutive days are ineligible unless vacancy coverage under §4.3 has been purchased. Home-based businesses occupying more than two hundred square feet are not eligible for personal property coverage.

§2.1 Insuring Agreement
The insurer agrees to pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a covered peril, subject to the limits and cost sharing described in §4.1. Payment will not exceed the smallest of the actual cash value, the replacement cost, or the applicable limit in the schedule. All payments are made in United States dollars.

§2.2 Covered Perils
Covered perils include fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, explosion, theft, vandalism, and accidental discharge of water from plumbing. Loss by theft is covered only if the dwelling shows visible signs of forced entry, except as waived under §3.2. Smoke from agricultural burning is covered only if the burning occurs within one mile of the dwelling.

§3.1 Dwelling Coverage Limit
Coverage A applies to the dwelling at a limit of not less than four hundred thousand dollars per occurrence. Detached structures are covered at ten percent of the Coverage A limit, up to forty thousand dollars. Building ordinance costs are covered only up to twenty-five thousand dollars per occurrence.

§3.2 Personal Property Coverage
Coverage B applies to personal property at fifty percent of the Coverage A limit. Special limits apply to jewelry, watches, and furs at one thousand five hundred dollars per item, and to firearms at two thousand five hundred dollars in the aggregate. The forced entry requirement in §2.2 is waived when theft occurs during a covered fire or windstorm.

§3.3 Additional Living Expenses
If a covered peril makes the dwelling uninhabitable, the insurer pays necessary increased living costs for up to twenty-four months. Monthly payments are capped at four thousand dollars. Payments end when the dwelling becomes habitable, even if the twenty-four month period has not run.

§3.4 Excluded Property
Animals, motor vehicles, and land are excluded property. Watercraft are excluded unless stored within a locked enclosure on the residence premises. Money and bank notes are excluded above two hundred dollars in any one loss, and stamps and collectibles are excluded above five hundred dollars.

§4.1 Deductible and Cost Sharing
A deductible of one thousand dollars applies to each occurrence, and a separate five thousand dollar deductible applies to all water discharge losses. Windstorm losses in designated coastal zones carry a deductible of two percent of the Coverage A limit. The insurer pays the remaining covered amount after the applicable deductible under §4.1 has been satisfied.

§4.2 Excluded Perils
Flood, surface water, earth movement, and wear or tear are excluded. Mold resulting from an excluded peril is excluded, but mold resulting from a covered water discharge loss is covered up to ten thousand dollars. Neglect by the insured to protect property after a covered loss voids coverage for resulting damage.

§4.3 Optional Endorsements
Vacancy coverage may be purchased for a stated additional premium and extends the sixty day limit in §1.2 to one hundred eighty days. A home systems endorsement covers appliance breakdown with a five hundred dollar deductible and a ten thousand dollar per item limit. Endorsements do not modify the excluded perils in §4.2.

§5.1 Duties After Loss
The insured must report any loss within thirty days of discovery. The insured must file a signed proof of loss within sixty days of the insurer's written request. Failure to meet these deadlines voids coverage for that loss unless the delay was beyond the insured's control.

§5.2 Prior Approval Rule
Emergency repairs to prevent further damage may proceed without approval, up to one thousand dollars. All other repairs require prior written approval from the insurer. Repairs made without required approval under §5.2 are covered only to the amount that would have been approved.

§5.3 Claim Administration
The insurer will acknowledge claims within ten business days and complete initial investigation within thirty days. Payment is issued within twenty days after agreement on the amount of loss. The insured may request one extension of the investigation period, not to exceed thirty days.

§5.4 Appeals
If a claim is denied in whole or in part, the insured may appeal in writing within one hundred eighty days of the denial notice. The insurer must issue a written appeal decision within forty-five days of receiving the appeal. A second-level appeal to an independent reviewer is available for claims exceeding twenty-five thousand dollars, and that review is final.

SYNTHETIC
Nova Horizon PPO Plan — Demonstration Document

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an individual enrolled under this Plan who satisfies the eligibility rules in §2.1. "Negotiated Rate" means the discounted amount the Plan has agreed to pay network providers for covered services. "Calendar Year" means the twelve-month period beginning January 1 and ending December 31. "Medical Necessity" means a service that is clinically appropriate and not primarily for the convenience of the participant or provider.

§1.2 Plan Purpose
This Plan is a preferred provider organization product created solely for software demonstration purposes. All dollar amounts, deadlines, and benefit limits are fictional and must not be treated as an offer of coverage. The document exists to illustrate how structured policy clauses can be rendered in a claims-adjudication interface.

§2.1 Eligibility and Enrollment
Employees working at least 30 hours per week are eligible on the first day of the month following 60 days of continuous service. Dependents include a legal spouse and children under age 26. Enrollment must be completed within 31 days of the eligibility date, or the person must wait until the next annual open enrollment period. A late enrollee other than a newborn or newly adopted child is subject to a 90-day waiting period.

§2.2 Termination of Coverage
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which employment terminates, except that a covered person may continue coverage for 18 months under the continuation rules referenced in §6.3. Coverage also ends if required contributions are more than 30 days delinquent. The Plan Administrator will send a termination notice within 15 days of the qualifying event.

§3.1 Medical Benefits
The Plan pays 90 percent of the Negotiated Rate for in-network hospital services and 70 percent of usual and customary charges for out-of-network services after the deductible in §4.1 is satisfied. Inpatient hospitalization is covered up to 120 days per Calendar Year. Outpatient surgery is covered at the same in-network level as other hospital services. Emergency room services are always treated as in-network for purposes of this section, including follow-up care described in §3.2.

§3.2 Physician and Preventive Services
Office visits are covered at 100 percent of the Negotiated Rate for in-network primary care with no deductible, subject to the copayment in §4.2. Preventive services, including annual physicals and immunizations, are covered at 100 percent in network with no visit limit. Out-of-network physician visits are covered at 60 percent after the deductible. Physical therapy is limited to 30 visits per Calendar Year, with exceptions granted under the medical necessity review in §5.2.

§3.3 Prescription Drugs
The Plan covers generic drugs at a $10 copayment, preferred brand drugs at a $35 copayment, and non-preferred brand drugs at 50 percent coinsurance. A 90-day maintenance supply is available through the mail-order program at two times the 30-day copayment. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1 and are limited to a 12-month supply per Calendar Year unless renewed under §5.2.

§4.1 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The Calendar Year deductible is $1,500 per person and $3,000 per family for in-network services, and $3,000 per person out of network. The out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 per person and $12,000 per family in network. Amounts paid above the Negotiated Rate do not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum. Deductible amounts carry over from the final quarter of one Calendar Year to the first quarter of the next.

§4.2 Copayments and Coinsurance
A $25 copayment applies to each in-network primary care visit under §3.2, and a $50 copayment applies to specialist visits. Copayments are not applied to the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket maximum in §4.1. Coinsurance under §3.1 is calculated only after the applicable deductible is satisfied. Emergency room visits carry a $150 copayment, waived if the person is admitted as an inpatient.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions planned at least 7 days in advance, all imaging involving radiation above 3 units, and specialty drugs under §3.3. Requests must be submitted by the provider at least 10 business days before the scheduled service. Emergency admissions require notification within 48 hours of admission. Failure to obtain required prior approval reduces benefits by 50 percent but does not eliminate them entirely.

§5.2 Utilization Review and Exceptions
The Plan conducts concurrent review of inpatient stays beyond the length thresholds published annually. A covered person may request an exception to any visit or supply limit in §3.2 or §3.3 by submitting a treating provider's statement of medical necessity. Exception decisions are issued within 15 business days, or 72 hours for expedited requests involving serious conditions. Denials of exceptions may be appealed under §7.2.

§5.3 Exclusions and Limitations
The Plan does not cover cosmetic surgery, experimental treatments, dental care for persons over age 19, or vision hardware beyond one examination and one pair of corrective lenses per Calendar Year. These exclusions do not apply to reconstructive surgery following accidental injury or to medically necessary treatment of congenital anomalies. Charges for services rendered by an immediate family member of the covered person are excluded. Out-of-network charges exceeding the usual and customary amount are the responsibility of the covered person.

§6.1 Coordination of Benefits
When a covered person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays secondary according to standard order-of-benefit rules, with the birthday rule applying to dependent children. Benefits paid by this Plan will not exceed the amount it would have paid as primary payer. The Plan may recover duplicate payments from providers or covered persons within 24 months of payment.

§6.2 Subrogation
If a covered person recovers damages for an injury for which the Plan paid benefits, the Plan is entitled to reimbursement from the recovery up to the amount paid. The Plan reduces its recovery proportionally when the covered person did not recover full damages. Covered persons must notify the Plan within 30 days of filing any claim or lawsuit related to such an injury.

§6.3 Continuation of Coverage
A covered person whose employment ends other than for gross misconduct may continue coverage for up to 18 months by paying 102 percent of the full monthly premium of $620 for single coverage or $1,450 for family coverage. Continuation ends early upon Medicare eligibility or enrollment in another group plan as described in §2.2. Written election must be made within 60 days of the termination notice.

§7.1 Claims Procedures
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service. The Plan pays or denies clean claims within 30 days of receipt, or within 15 days for electronic claims. An initial denial notice states the specific reason, the provision relied upon, and the materials needed to perfect the claim. Payment is made to the provider in network and to the covered person out of network.

§7.2 Appeals
A covered person may appeal an adverse benefit determination within 180 days of the denial notice under §7.1. The appeal is reviewed by a reviewer who was not involved in the original determination and who may consult an independent clinical expert for medical necessity disputes under §5.2. First-level appeals are decided within 30 days, and a second-level appeal may be requested within 60 days of the first decision. The second-level decision is final for internal purposes, and the notice explains any further external review rights.

SYNTHETIC
Plan Name: Luminara Short-Term Disability Shield, Demo Edition

§1.1 Definition of Disability
A Covered Disability means a physical or mental condition, certified by a Treating Provider, that prevents the Covered Person from performing the essential duties of their Regular Occupation. The condition must be documented in a written certification submitted within the timelines described in §5.2. Pregnancy, childbirth, and recovery from childbirth are Covered Disabilities for the periods stated in §3.3.

§1.2 Definition of Covered Person
A Covered Person is an enrolled participant of the fictional Demo Employer who is actively at work at least 20 hours per week. Enrollment must occur during the annual Demo Enrollment Window or within 31 days of a Qualifying Life Event. Persons enrolled solely for demonstration purposes are deemed Covered Persons for all purposes of this synthetic document.

§1.3 Treating Provider
A Treating Provider means a licensed practitioner of medicine, osteopathy, psychology, or physical therapy who is not the Covered Person or an immediate family member. Certifications from chiropractors are accepted only for conditions of the spine and only for the first 30 days of any Benefit Period. Telehealth certifications are accepted if the platform records the consultation date.

§2.1 Eligibility and Waiting Period
Coverage begins on the first day of the calendar month following 60 days of continuous eligible employment. A New Condition Waiting Period of 14 calendar days applies from the first day of a Covered Disability before benefits commence. The Waiting Period is waived entirely for disabilities caused by accidents occurring at the workplace.

§2.2 Actively at Work Requirement
The Covered Person must be actively at work on the day before the disability begins, or on the last scheduled workday if the disability begins on a weekend or holiday. A Covered Person who is on an approved layoff of 90 days or fewer retains eligibility. Failure to meet this requirement defers the Benefit Period until the requirement is satisfied.

§2.3 Recurrent Disability
A recurrence of the same condition within 90 days of returning to work is treated as a continuation of the original disability, with no new Waiting Period. Recurrences occurring more than 90 days after return are treated as a new disability subject to the Waiting Period in §2.1. A maximum of three recurrences per condition per calendar year may be treated as continuations.

§3.1 Weekly Benefit Amount
The Weekly Benefit equals 60 percent of the Covered Person's base weekly earnings, rounded to the nearest whole dollar, subject to a minimum benefit of $75 per week and a maximum benefit of $1,850 per week. Base weekly earnings do not include bonuses, commissions, overtime, or equity compensation. The maximum is applied before any offset described in §3.4.

§3.2 Benefit Period
Benefits are payable for up to 13 weeks per Covered Disability for conditions other than those listed in §3.3. For mental health conditions, benefits are payable for a maximum of 8 weeks per calendar year unless the prior approval rules of §4.1 are satisfied. No benefits are payable after the Covered Person's employment ends, except as provided in §2.2.

§3.3 Pregnancy and Childbirth Benefits
Recovery from childbirth is payable for 6 weeks following a vaginal delivery and 8 weeks following a cesarean delivery. Complications of pregnancy, as certified by a Treating Provider, extend the Benefit Period up to an additional 4 weeks. Pregnancy benefits are not subject to the New Condition Waiting Period in §2.1.

§3.4 Offsets
Benefits are reduced dollar for dollar by state disability benefits, sick leave paid at full salary, and workers' compensation awards for the same period. Paid time off used concurrently reduces the benefit by 100 percent of the daily equivalent of §3.1. Partial disability benefits equal 50 percent of the Weekly Benefit when the Covered Person works fewer than 20 hours per week.

§4.1 Prior Approval Requirements
Mental health disability benefits beyond 8 weeks per year, and any disability claimed for elective surgery recovery, require Prior Approval submitted at least 10 business days before benefits are requested. Prior Approval requests are decided within 5 business days. Benefits claimed without required Prior Approval are payable at 50 percent of the amount otherwise due under §3.1.

§4.2 Notice Deadlines
The Covered Person must notify the administrator of the disability within 7 calendar days of the first day of absence. Written certification from a Treating Provider is due within 21 calendar days of the first day of absence. Recertification is required every 30 days for disabilities lasting longer than 30 days.

§4.3 Exclusions
No benefits are payable for disabilities caused by intentionally self-inflicted injury, commission of a felony, active duty military service, or war. Disabilities arising from cosmetic surgery are excluded unless the surgery is necessitated by an accidental injury or a documented medical condition. Substance use disorders are covered only when treatment is received in a licensed inpatient facility, for a maximum of 4 weeks per calendar year.

§4.4 Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
Conditions for which the Covered Person received diagnosis, care, or prescription treatment during the 90 days before the effective date of coverage are excluded for the first 12 months of coverage. This limitation does not apply to pregnancy under §3.3 or to workplace accidents under §2.1. After 12 months of continuous coverage, this limitation ceases to apply.

§5.1 Cost Sharing
The Covered Person pays a premium contribution of $4.20 per week, deducted from payroll. There is no deductible per disability. The first 3 days of each Benefit Period are unpaid except where the Waiting Period is waived under §2.1, in which case all days are paid from day one.

§5.2 Claims Submission
Initial claims must be submitted on the Demo Claim Form within 45 calendar days of the first day of absence. Claims submitted after 45 days but within 180 days are payable only for days after the submission date. Claims submitted more than 180 days after the first day of absence are barred, except where the Covered Person was incapacitated, in which case the deadline extends to 30 days after incapacity ends.

§5.3 Claim Review and Payment
The administrator reviews complete claims within 10 business days and pays approved benefits every 2 weeks by direct deposit to the account designated by the Covered Person. Incomplete claims are acknowledged within 5 business days with a statement of missing items, and the review clock restarts when the last missing item is received. Benefits are payable only while the certification requirements of §1.3 remain current.

§5.4 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed within 180 days of the denial notice by submitting a written appeal to the Demo Appeals Unit. The appeal is decided by a reviewer who was not involved in the initial determination, within 30 calendar days, extendable once by 15 calendar days upon written notice. A second-level appeal may be filed within 60 days of the first appeal decision and is decided within 45 calendar days.

§6.1 Administration and Records
The administrator maintains claim records for 7 years in the Demo Records System. Covered Persons may request one free copy of their claim file per calendar year, delivered within 15 business days. All data in this document is synthetic and exists solely for software demonstration purposes.

§6.2 Termination and Non-Duplication
Coverage terminates on the last day of the calendar month in which employment ends, except for benefits in payment under §3.1, which continue through the end of the approved Benefit Period. Benefits under this plan do not duplicate benefits under any other synthetic demo plan. If two demo plans apply, the plan under which the Covered Person works the most hours is primary.

§6.3 Interpretation
This document is obviously synthetic and confers no actual rights or obligations. Headings are for convenience and do not affect interpretation of any clause. Where a deadline falls on a weekend or demo holiday, it extends to the next business day.

SYNTHETIC
Aurora Flex High-Deductible Health Plan 7300 (Demonstration Document)

§1.1 Definitions
"Covered Person" means an eligible individual enrolled under this Plan. "Deductible" means the amount of Covered Expenses the Covered Person must pay each Plan Year before benefits are payable. "Plan Year" means the twelve-month period beginning each first day of the demonstration month. "Allowed Amount" means the maximum recognized charge for a service as determined by the Plan Administrator.

§1.2 Administrator
The Plan Administrator is a fictional entity created solely for software testing purposes. It processes enrollment, claims, and appeals as described in this document. No real person or organization is referenced.

§2.1 Eligibility
Employees of a fictional employer who are scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are eligible to enroll. Enrollment must occur within 31 days of the date eligibility begins. Late enrollment is permitted only during the annual demonstration window or upon a qualifying event.

§2.2 Waiting Period
New enrollees are subject to a 30-day waiting period before coverage begins. The waiting period is waived for newborns and newly adopted children enrolled within 60 days. Coverage may not begin earlier than the first day following the waiting period.

§2.3 Termination
Coverage ends on the last day of the month in which the Covered Person ceases to be eligible. Coverage may continue for up to 18 months under the fictional continuation rules described in §6.3. The Administrator must provide written notice of termination within 15 days.

§3.1 Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Limits
The annual Deductible is 7,300 dollars for individual coverage and 14,600 dollars for family coverage. After the Deductible is met, the Plan pays 80 percent of the Allowed Amount for most services. The annual out-of-pocket limit is 8,150 dollars for individual coverage and 16,300 dollars for family coverage. Once the out-of-pocket limit is reached, the Plan pays 100 percent of Covered Expenses for the remainder of the Plan Year.

§3.2 Preventive Services
Preventive services, including one annual physical examination and routine immunizations, are covered at 100 percent with no Deductible. One routine screening per Plan Year per Covered Person is included. Services that become diagnostic during the same visit are subject to the Deductible as described in §3.1.

§3.3 Physician and Hospital Benefits
Covered office visits are paid at 80 percent after the Deductible. Inpatient hospital benefits are limited to 120 days per Plan Year at 80 percent of the Allowed Amount. Emergency room services are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, except that a 250 dollar facility charge applies when the visit does not result in admission.

§3.4 Prescription Drugs
Prescription drugs are covered at 75 percent after the Deductible, with a 30 dollar generic copay once the Deductible is met. A 90-day supply of maintenance medication is available at twice the 30-day cost. Specialty drugs require prior approval as described in §5.1 and are limited to a 90-day supply per fill.

§3.5 Mental Health and Rehabilitation
Outpatient mental health visits are covered at 80 percent after the Deductible, limited to 40 visits per Plan Year. Inpatient substance abuse treatment is limited to 30 days per Plan Year. Physical, occupational, and speech therapy are each limited to 30 combined visits per Plan Year.

§4.1 Exclusions
Services not medically necessary, cosmetic procedures, and experimental treatments are excluded. Dental and vision care are excluded except for accidental injury to sound natural teeth and one annual eye refraction. Weight loss programs, cosmetic orthodontia, and travel costs other than ambulance services are excluded.

§4.2 Exceptions to Exclusions
Reconstructive surgery following a covered mastectomy is not excluded under §4.1. Dental services required to treat a accidental injury are covered up to 2,500 dollars per occurrence. Investigational treatments are covered when the treating facility certifies that no standard alternative exists and prior approval is obtained.

§5.1 Prior Approval
Prior approval is required for inpatient admissions, imaging over 1,500 dollars, and all specialty drugs. Requests must be submitted at least 7 days before scheduled services or within 48 hours of an emergency admission. Approval is valid for 60 days from the date of issuance.

§5.2 Notice Deadlines
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the date of service. Notice of a qualifying event permitting late enrollment must be given within 31 days of the event. Written notice of intent to appeal must be filed within 180 days of the denial notice.

§5.3 Coordination of Benefits
When a Covered Person has coverage under more than one plan, this Plan pays after the primary plan. Benefits payable under this Plan are reduced by amounts received from the primary plan. The Administrator may recover overpayments made due to unreported other coverage.

§6.1 Claims Administration
Claims are processed within 30 days of receipt of a complete submission. Incomplete claims are returned with an itemized list of missing information within 15 days. Payment or denial notices are issued in writing.

§6.2 Appeals
A denied claim may be appealed in two levels. The first-level appeal is decided within 30 days by a reviewer not involved in the original denial. A second-level appeal must be filed within 60 days of the first-level decision and is decided within 45 days.

§6.3 Continuation and Reinstatement
Fictional continuation coverage under §2.3 requires monthly payment of 102 percent of the applicable premium. Reinstatement after a lapse of less than 90 days does not require a new waiting period. A lapse of 90 days or more requires re-enrollment under §2.1.

§7.1 Amendment
The Plan Sponsor may amend this document upon 30 days written notice to Covered Persons. Amendments apply prospectively unless the notice states otherwise. No amendment may reduce benefits retroactively for services already rendered.

§7.2 Entire Agreement
This document is entirely fictional and is intended only for use in software demonstrations. It does not describe any real plan, product, or coverage. Any resemblance to an actual policy is coincidental.
